title: E50 — xstate-statemachine adoption: factory, persistence, plugins, contract suite, catalogue
body:
> **Re-planned 2026-09-24: ADR-0016 Accepted — full adoption of xstate-statemachine==0.9.1 (tag v0.9.1 = 45bb7f3; wheel == tag 42/42; sha256 d832d4d9a17b7b8003f61fa0714a8e57eaff316bcd5dd699d81d410362687162; PEP 740 attested).** No in-house shim, no dual runtime, no shim retirement ladder. 59 tickets retired (keys kept for `blocked_by`), see `docs/plan/29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` §4.

## Goal
Every catalogue lifecycle B1–B20 (`28-statechart-catalogue.md`) is built directly on `xstate-statemachine==0.9.1` through `candleviewer.statechart` (factory, persistence, gateway, plugins, registry), guarded by a standing lint set and a blocking contract suite, within R0–R1 (Sprint 02–Sprint 08).

## Scope
- Pin + hash lock + PEP 740 attestation check (E50-T57)
- Standing lint set `tools/lint_statecharts.py` (E50-T11)
- Registry + `machine_hash` lock + upcasters (E50-T01, E50-T02)
- Factory with the FINAL mandatory config block (E50-T59)
- Persistence: quiescent persist, drain journal, sealed restore, chain_trips latch (E50-T10, E50-T49)
- Plugins: CvErrorHooks / CvMetricsPlugin / CvAuditPlugin (E50-T60)
- Charts B1–B20 from corrected v0.9.1 contracts + round-14 fixes (E50-S01, E50-S02, E50-T14, E50-T16, E50-T43)
- Gateway + CV-C68 cv_re_mint (E50-T15, E50-T56)
- Contract suite, event coverage, budgets, chaos, nightly gate + BENCH-6 (E50-T31, E50-T05, E50-T06, E50-Q01, E50-T04)
- Upstream contributions and liaison (E50-C01, E50-C02, E50-C17)

Out of scope (permanent): per-tick rule evaluation stays plain code (BENCH-2 381 ev/s vs 2,000); `after:` timers only where p99 ≤100 ms does not matter (BENCH-6 55–92 ms).

## Exit criteria
- `tests/xstate_contract/` green on both service spellings under `-W error::RuntimeWarning` for 5 consecutive nightlies
- Every catalogue machine B1–B20 loads under `statechart.factory.build` with the mandatory config block
- `tools/lint_statecharts.py` green on main (CI-blocking)

title: Adopt xstate-statemachine==0.9.1: dependency pin with hash lock + PEP 740 attestation verify in CI
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** the in-house shim and dual-runtime paths are withdrawn; this ticket now targets the pinned library directly per 29 §4b.

MUST-09 orders the pin first: every other E50 ticket imports the library. ADR-0016 MUST-08 (vendored copy) is superseded by pin + hash + attestation.

Runtime: xstate-statemachine==0.9.1 (tag v0.9.1 = 45bb7f3; wheel == tag 42/42; sha256 d832d4d9a17b7b8003f61fa0714a8e57eaff316bcd5dd699d81d410362687162; PEP 740 attested). There is no in-house shim and no dual runtime; this ticket builds directly on the library.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/pyproject.toml`: add under `[project.dependencies]` exactly `xstate-statemachine = "==0.9.1"`
- `uv.lock` / `requirements.lock` entry with `--hash=sha256:d832d4d9a17b7b8003f61fa0714a8e57eaff316bcd5dd699d81d410362687162`; install with `--require-hashes`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` job `xstate-pin-attestation`: download the wheel, check sha256, then `python -m pypi_attestations verify pypi --repository https://github.com/basiltt/xstate-statemachine pypi:xstate_statemachine-0.9.1-py3-none-any.whl` (fallback: PyPI JSON API `https://pypi.org/integrity/xstate-statemachine/0.9.1/xstate_statemachine-0.9.1-py3-none-any.whl/provenance` checked for publisher `basiltt/xstate-statemachine`, or `gh attestation verify <wheel> --repo basiltt/xstate-statemachine`)
- `tools/check_pin.py`: fails if the pin is not `==0.9.1` (bans `~=`/`>=`) or the lock hash differs

## Out of scope
- Any library usage code (E50-T59 onward)
- Pin bumps: go through E50-C17 + an ADR-0016 amendment

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Pin is exact and hash-locked
  Given services/api/pyproject.toml
  Then it contains the line xstate-statemachine = "==0.9.1"
  And the lock file records sha256 d832d4d9a17b7b8003f61fa0714a8e57eaff316bcd5dd699d81d410362687162
Scenario: Tampered wheel is rejected
  When the install runs with a wheel whose sha256 differs
  Then pip --require-hashes fails and CI is red
Scenario: Attestation verified in CI
  When job xstate-pin-attestation runs
  Then pypi_attestations verify for repository https://github.com/basiltt/xstate-statemachine exits 0
  And a missing or mismatched provenance fails the job
Scenario: Loose specifier refused
  Given a PR changes the pin to "~=0.9.1"
  Then tools/check_pin.py fails
```

## Technical notes / design
- Pin with `==` only: #231 shows validation tightening inside a minor release
- Wheel equals tag v0.9.1 = 45bb7f3 across 42/42 modules (79-r14)

FINAL mandatory config block (79-r14 §7, applied unconditionally by `statechart/factory.py`): `strict_config=True` + chart `"strictConfig": true`; recursive key walk (CV-C57); `actionErrorPolicy:"rollback"`; `guardErrorPolicy:"raise"` on order/control charts with an ordered unguarded auditing fall-through; `onUnhandled:"defer"` (control lane escalates via `CvErrorHooks`); `strictTargets:true`; `strict=True, event_schemas=CV_EVENT_SCHEMAS`; `max_queue_size=CV_INBOX_BOUND[lane], overflow_policy="refuse"`; `maxIterations` sized to the descent plateau (CV-C62); `service_pool_size` order 32 / control 8 / platform 16; injected `clock=`; plugins `[CvErrorHooks(), CvMetricsPlugin(), CvAuditPlugin()]` (restores pass `from_snapshot(plugins=...)`); `await asyncio.wait_for(interp.start(), CV_START_TIMEOUT)`; async `Interpreter` only (MUSTNOT-06).

## Test plan
- Unit test for `tools/check_pin.py` with loose/mismatched fixtures
- CI dry run with a corrupted wheel to prove the hash/attestation step fails
- Contract-suite membership: runs inside `tests/xstate_contract/` (or its lint/registry jobs) with `pytest -W error::RuntimeWarning`; both service spellings (`def`→coroutine and `async def`).

## Security notes
Supply-chain control: exact pin, hash lock and PEP 740 provenance tied to the upstream GitHub repo. A failure blocks merge.

## Accessibility notes
Not applicable: backend/tooling ticket with no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Per-tick rule evaluation stays plain code (BENCH-2: 381 ev/s vs 2,000 needed); nothing here touches the §3 hot-path exclusion list (CV-LINT-HOTPATH). Contract suite budget < 60 s.

## Observability
Failures surface through `CvErrorHooks` and `cv_machine_*` metrics (E50-T60); CI job output names the machine key and `machine_hash`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Pin line, lock hash and CI attestation job merged
- [ ] Negative CI run evidence attached
- [ ] CI green, including `tools/lint_statecharts.py` and `pytest tests/xstate_contract -W error::RuntimeWarning`
- [ ] Reviewed; docs in `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` still accurate

## Dependencies
- Blocked by `E02-T02`

## Branch
`feat/e50-xstate-pin`

## References
- `docs/plan/29-statechart-adoption-plan.md`
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md` (Accepted, Amendment 15)
- `docs/research/xstate/79-r14-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7
- `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md`

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. docs/plan/20-architecture.md §4.2/§12 (module boundaries, metrics)
2. docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md (relevant §)
3. docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md (if statechart-labelled) + ADR-0016

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `services/api` (owner: @CandleViewer/backend)

**Interfaces you must not break**
- REST endpoints under `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` touched by this ticket (regenerate `packages/protocol`, never hand-edit)

**Commands**
- `cd services/api && pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`
- `cd services/api && ruff check . && black --check . && mypy --strict .`
- `cd services/api && lint-imports`

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e50-xstate-pin`
- PR title: "E50-T57: Adopt xstate-statemachine==0.9.1: dependency pin with hash lock + PEP 740 attestation verify in CI"
- Body includes: `Closes #<issue-for-E50-T57>`
- Required reviewers: CODEOWNERS for `/services/api/` (@CandleViewer/backend); 2 approvals minimum (C-10.1)
- Labels: carry over this ticket's labels: type/tech, area/backend-platform, priority/p1, qa

**Done means**
- Pin line, lock hash and CI attestation job merged
- Negative CI run evidence attached
- CI green, including `tools/lint_statecharts.py` and `pytest tests/xstate_contract -W error::RuntimeWarning`
- Reviewed; docs in `29-statechart-adoption-plan.md` still accurate

**Do NOT**
- Any library usage code (E50-T59 onward)
- Pin bumps: go through E50-C17 + an ADR-0016 amendment
- Widen any package's public API or add a dependency without a linked ADR.

**If blocked**
- Comment on the `E50-T57` GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (failing gate, missing decision, unmet dependency); move issue Status to `Blocked`; never silently work around a failing gate or merge with a required check disabled.

title: Machine-JSON registry: schema/target validation, recursive key walk (CV-C57), machine_hash, Stately export
body:
## Context
> **Re-scoped 2026-09-24 for full xstate-statemachine adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted):** absorbs E50-T44 (CV-C57); validation feeds the library factory instead of a shim.

The chart JSON is the normative contract (ADR-0016 Part 1). The registry is the single loader: it validates before `create_machine` ever sees a chart.

Runtime: xstate-statemachine==0.9.1 (tag v0.9.1 = 45bb7f3; wheel == tag 42/42; sha256 d832d4d9a17b7b8003f61fa0714a8e57eaff316bcd5dd699d81d410362687162; PEP 740 attested). There is no in-house shim and no dual runtime; this ticket builds directly on the library.

## Scope / Deliverables

- `machine_hash = sha256(canonical_json(chart))`; `registry.hash(key)`; `registry.export_stately(key)`
- `tools/statechart/render_catalogue.py`: regenerates `28-statechart-catalogue.md` tables; `make gen && git diff --exit-code` in CI

```gherkin
Scenario: Unknown key anywhere is rejected
  Given a chart with an unknown key inside a nested invoke.src
  When registry.validate runs
  Then it raises naming the machine and the JSON path
Scenario: Relative or unknown target rejected
  Given a transition target ".child" or "#b01.nope"
  Then validation fails before create_machine is called
Scenario: machine_hash is stable
  When the same chart is loaded twice with keys reordered
  Then registry.hash returns the same sha256
```

## Test plan

- Round-trip `export_stately` on all registered charts
- Contract-suite membership: runs inside `tests/xstate_contract/` (or its lint/registry jobs) with `pytest -W error::RuntimeWarning`; both service spellings (`def`→coroutine and `async def`).

## Security notes

## Accessibility notes

## Context
The factory is the ONLY construction site (29 §1.2). It applies the FINAL mandatory block unconditionally so no caller can opt out. Absorbs T20, T28, T30, T46 (C56 half).

Runtime: xstate-statemachine==0.9.1 (tag v0.9.1 = 45bb7f3; wheel == tag 42/42; sha256 d832d4d9a17b7b8003f61fa0714a8e57eaff316bcd5dd699d81d410362687162; PEP 740 attested). There is no in-house shim and no dual runtime; this ticket builds directly on the library.

## Scope / Deliverables

- `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/config.py`: `CV_INBOX_BOUND`, `CV_START_TIMEOUT`, `CV_EVENT_SCHEMAS`, `CV_SERVICE_POOL`, lane table order|control|platform
- `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/bindings/` loader: fresh `MachineLogic` per `create_machine()`, `asyncio.iscoroutinefunction` asserted on every action (CV-C18, CV-C67)

## Out of scope

- Plugin implementations (E50-T60) — stubs allowed until then

```gherkin

  Given each registered machine B1..B20
  When build(key, clock=SimulatedClock(), lane=<lane>) is awaited
  Then the interpreter is started with strict=True, overflow_policy="refuse" and the lane inbox bound
Scenario: start() is bounded
  Given a binding whose entry never yields
  When build runs
  Then asyncio.TimeoutError is raised after CV_START_TIMEOUT and startup fails hard
Scenario: Sync engine refused
  When anything requests SyncInterpreter from the factory
  Then an AssertionError is raised
Scenario: No RuntimeWarning
  When pytest tests/xstate_contract -W error::RuntimeWarning runs the factory tests

```

- Callers cannot pass policy kwargs; any extra kwarg is a TypeError

title: CvErrorHooks / CvMetricsPlugin / CvAuditPlugin (C09, C36, C50, C59, C63, C69; cv_machine_* families; write-ahead machine_events)
body:
## Context
Observability of the library runtime is a plugin set passed on every build and restore. Absorbs T39, T45 (gauge), T48 (C59), T54 (read), T58 (C69).

Runtime: xstate-statemachine==0.9.1 (tag v0.9.1 = 45bb7f3; wheel == tag 42/42; sha256 d832d4d9a17b7b8003f61fa0714a8e57eaff316bcd5dd699d81d410362687162; PEP 740 attested). There is no in-house shim and no dual runtime; this ticket builds directly on the library.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/plugins/errors.py` `CvErrorHooks`: on_transition_failed, on_invalid_event, on_event_dropped, on_chain_budget_exceeded, on_invocation_stranded, on_receipt_dropped; control lane escalates unhandled/guard-denied to page
- `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/plugins/metrics.py` `CvMetricsPlugin`: `cv_machine_transitions_total`, `cv_machine_send_refused_total{kind,reason}`, `cv_machine_chain_trips`, `cv_machine_timer_handles`, `cv_machine_dropped_receipts_total`
- `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/plugins/audit.py` `CvAuditPlugin`: write-ahead `machine_events` rows, hash-chained (M19)

## Out of scope
- Grafana dashboards (E04 follow-up)

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Chain trip is observed on both lanes
  Given a chart exceeding maxIterations
  Then on_chain_budget_exceeded fires and cv_machine_chain_trips increments
  And supervisors read chain_trips, never last_error
Scenario: Dropped receipt pages
  When on_receipt_dropped fires
  Then cv_machine_dropped_receipts_total increments and an alert is raised
Scenario: Audit is write-ahead
  When a transition commits
  Then its machine_events row was written before the action ran
```

## Technical notes / design
- Hooks must never raise into the interpreter; they log and count

FINAL mandatory config block (79-r14 §7, applied unconditionally by `statechart/factory.py`): `strict_config=True` + chart `"strictConfig": true`; recursive key walk (CV-C57); `actionErrorPolicy:"rollback"`; `guardErrorPolicy:"raise"` on order/control charts with an ordered unguarded auditing fall-through; `onUnhandled:"defer"` (control lane escalates via `CvErrorHooks`); `strictTargets:true`; `strict=True, event_schemas=CV_EVENT_SCHEMAS`; `max_queue_size=CV_INBOX_BOUND[lane], overflow_policy="refuse"`; `maxIterations` sized to the descent plateau (CV-C62); `service_pool_size` order 32 / control 8 / platform 16; injected `clock=`; plugins `[CvErrorHooks(), CvMetricsPlugin(), CvAuditPlugin()]` (restores pass `from_snapshot(plugins=...)`); `await asyncio.wait_for(interp.start(), CV_START_TIMEOUT)`; async `Interpreter` only (MUSTNOT-06).

## Test plan
- Unit tests per hook with SimulatedClock
- Metrics scrape test
- Contract-suite membership: runs inside `tests/xstate_contract/` (or its lint/registry jobs) with `pytest -W error::RuntimeWarning`; both service spellings (`def`→coroutine and `async def`).

## Security notes
Library imported only via `candleviewer.statechart` (CV-LINT-IMPORT); pin is hash-locked and attestation-verified in CI (E50-T57). No secrets in machine context or snapshots.

## Accessibility notes
Not applicable: backend/tooling ticket with no UI surface.

## Performance notes
Per-tick rule evaluation stays plain code (BENCH-2: 381 ev/s vs 2,000 needed); nothing here touches the §3 hot-path exclusion list (CV-LINT-HOTPATH). Contract suite budget < 60 s.

## Observability
This ticket IS the observability surface: `cv_machine_*` Prometheus families, audit rows, pages.

title: Spike: fix the statechart subset and prove the in-house shim is ~1,500 LOC, not a second interpreter
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: shim/dual-runtime/gate/decision work withdrawn by the owner decision for full adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted; 29-statechart-adoption-plan §4a)**

## Context
ADR-0016 Part 2 commits to executing the twenty contracts with a thin in-house interpreter shim until the adoption gate passes. "Thin" is the entire load-bearing word. The ADR's own negative consequences list says it plainly: the shim is real code on the order path, and a shim that grows into a general interpreter is a worse outcome than either adopting the library or hand-rolling.

This spike closes that risk before any of it is built, by answering two questions with evidence rather than confidence: exactly which statechart features do the twenty contracts in `docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md` actually use, and what does a shim implementing precisely that subset - and nothing else - cost in lines?

The answer is bounded from above by an unpleasant fact: the library implementing the *full* feature set is 12,104 LOC across nine modules, and `12-challenge-register.md` LC-57 records that its two engines duplicate rather than share the core algorithm. A subset shim that lands anywhere near that number is a failed spike, and the honest response is to say so in the spike report rather than to start building.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A **feature census** across all twenty contracts: for each of compound states, parallel regions, guarded transition arrays, `entry`/`exit`, `always`, final states, `tags`, wildcard handlers, `invoke` with `onDone`/`onError`, and snapshot/restore - which machines use it, how many times, and what breaks if it is dropped. Published as a table.
- A **negative census**: every XState v5 feature the contracts do **not** use (`after`, `history`, `delayed transitions`, `spawn` outside `invoke`, actions with parameters, typed events, `sendParent`, nested `always` chains). Each is recorded as explicitly out of the shim's scope, with a note on what a future contract would have to change to need it.
- A **walking skeleton**: the shim's transition core plus B17 (`live_gate`, 3 states) and B8 (`position_protection`, 2 parallel regions, invokes) executing end to end, with LOC measured.
- An **extrapolated LOC estimate** for the full subset, with the walking skeleton as the denominator, and a stated go/no-go against the 1,500-LOC target.
- A **semantics decision record** for each of the seven Blockers: exactly what the shim does instead, written as the test name that will assert it.
- A **spike report** in `docs/research/xstate/21-shim-subset.md` with a recommendation.

## Out of scope
- Building the production shim - that is E50-T07, and it starts from this report.
- The JSON registry and CI gates (E50-T01).
- Any comparison against the library's performance; the library is not adopted and adoption is gated. Throughput measurement belongs to E50-T06.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The subset is known, not assumed
  Given all twenty contracts in 28-statechart-catalogue.md
  When the feature census runs
  Then every statechart feature used by any contract is listed with its using machines and a count
  And every XState v5 feature not used is listed as explicitly out of the shim's scope

Scenario: The walking skeleton actually runs two real contracts
  Given the skeleton shim and the B17 and B8 contracts unmodified from the catalogue
  When each is driven through its documented happy path and one failure path
  Then the observed state trace matches the contract's transition table exactly
  And B8's two parallel regions advance independently

Scenario: The size question is answered with a number
  When the spike reports
  Then it states measured skeleton LOC, extrapolated full-subset LOC, and a go/no-go against 1,500
  And if the estimate exceeds 1,500 the report recommends an alternative rather than proceeding

Scenario: Each Blocker has a decided answer before any production code exists
  Given LC-01, LC-02, LC-03, LC-15, LC-16, LC-17 and LC-22
  Then the report names, for each, the shim's behaviour and the test that will assert it
```

## Technical notes / design
Timeboxed to one sprint; the deliverable is the report, and throwaway code is expected and acceptable (`docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md`, Spike DoD).

B17 and B8 are chosen deliberately: B17 is the smallest contract in the catalogue (three states, no invokes) so the skeleton can be exercised immediately, and B8 is the hardest shape that is not also the largest - two parallel regions, four invokes, guarded `onError` arrays and a wildcard deferral - so the skeleton meets every structural feature except sheer size.

The census must read the JSON, not the prose: a script over the machine files, so it can be re-run when a contract changes and so the shim's scope can be re-derived rather than remembered.

## Test plan
A spike's tests are its evidence. The skeleton carries trace-assertion tests for B17 and B8 that are **kept and promoted** into E50-T07's suite rather than discarded, because they are the first two conformance cases. The census script gets one unit test asserting it fails loudly on a machine it cannot parse, so a silently shrinking census is impossible.

## Security notes
The spike establishes a security-relevant rule that E50-T07 inherits: the shim resolves actions and guards from a static registry only. It does not `eval`, does not import by name from machine JSON, and does not accept a machine definition from outside the repository. A machine definition is executable configuration and is treated as code. The report states this as a design constraint.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. Where statechart state reaches the admin health panel (E42) it must be conveyed as text, never colour alone (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
Not a performance spike, but the skeleton records a rough per-transition cost so that E50-T06 has a starting point. For calibration only: the library measures ~33 us per transition and ~8,813 ev/s on a realistic machine shape. The shim is not required to beat that; it is required to be within the same order of magnitude, because the budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` were set against those numbers.

## Observability
None - throwaway code. The report names the `cv_machine_*` series E50-T07 will emit.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `docs/research/xstate/21-shim-subset.md` merged with the feature census, the negative census, the LOC estimate and a go/no-go recommendation.
- [ ] Walking skeleton runs B17 and B8 unmodified; trace tests committed for promotion into E50-T07.
- [ ] A decided shim behaviour recorded for each of the seven Blockers, each named as a test.
- [ ] Census script committed and re-runnable.
- [ ] Reviewed by the Architect; outcome reflected in E50-T07's estimate before it enters a sprint.

## Dependencies
- **E02-T01** - the Python workspace and `services/api` package layout the skeleton lives in.

## Branch
`spike/e50-shim-subset`

## References
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md
- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md
- docs/research/xstate/10-fit-analysis.md Part A, Part B, Part C
- docs/research/xstate/11-adversarial-review.md section 3, section 5
- docs/research/xstate/12-challenge-register.md
- docs/research/xstate/01-library-core.md (module inventory, LOC)
- docs/research/xstate/05-semantics-probes.md (A1-A20, B1-B14, C1-C17)

title: In-house interpreter shim executing the catalogue subset with corrected Blocker semantics
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: shim/dual-runtime/gate/decision work withdrawn by the owner decision for full adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted; 29-statechart-adoption-plan §4a)**

## Context
ADR-0016 Part 2 makes this the executor for every lifecycle in the catalogue from the first lifecycle ticket until - and possibly after - the adoption gate is reviewed at Sprint 08.

It exists for one reason, and it is not "we prefer our own code". The seven Blockers in `12-challenge-register.md` are all the same design philosophy: *resolution and execution failures degrade to silent no-ops rather than errors*. An action that raises still commits its transition and that state is durably persisted as truth. An `always` self-target deadlocks with `is_running == True` and no error. An event with no handler in the current state is silently discarded - probe C17 lost three `PARTIAL` fills deterministically across ten runs. The mandated deferral buffer is persisted and then never drained after a crash, so three fills sat stranded in a machine that looked healthy.

Every one of those has a CandleViewer-side mitigation, and every mitigation fails silently if a developer forgets it. The shim implements the corrected behaviour *in the executor*, where it cannot be forgotten, which is a categorically stronger position than a house rule.

The shim is not a reimplementation of the library and must not grow into one. `E50-K01` fixes the subset and the LOC budget before a line is written.

## Scope / Deliverables
**The subset** (from `E50-K01`, and nothing beyond it): compound states, parallel regions, guarded transition arrays with first-match, `entry`/`exit` actions, `always`, final states, `tags`, wildcard `*` handlers, `invoke` with `onDone`/`onError`, snapshot and restore. **No `after`** - A2 puts every deadline in context as an absolute `*_us` timestamp armed by the `MonotonicScheduler`.

**The corrected semantics**, each shipping with the test that asserts it:
- A raising action **aborts and rolls back the transition**, sets `context['_fault']`, and routes to the machine's fault state. The transition does not commit (LC-01, LC-15).
- An explicit self-target is **external** by default, so `entry` re-runs; an `always` self-target is rejected at build time rather than deadlocking (LC-02, LC-04).
- An event with no handler in the current state is **deferred, counted and logged**, never discarded (LC-03).
- `_deferred` is drained **at boot, unconditionally, before invokes are re-driven** (LC-17).
- Child actors are addressed through an **application-owned registry** keyed by our own id (LC-16).
- A guard that raises is a **loud error** and is treated as **deny** (LC-09); guard evaluation **short-circuits** once a branch is selected (LC-10).
- Restore merges `{**machine_defaults, **snapshot_context}` (LC-22).
- Targets are absolute and pre-resolved at load; there is no fallback resolution ladder (LC-06/07/08).

**Plus**: a terminal-state reaper that stops and evicts (MUST-11); a bounded per-machine queue with a depth metric and a backpressure signal (LC-41); `send_threadsafe` as the only cross-thread entry point (LC-43); logging at WARNING by default with no per-transition INFO (A8, LC-45); shared machine definitions across instances, verified non-aliasing of context (A8, LC-47).

## Out of scope
- The `MachineGateway` - validation, dedupe, event-name checking and metric emission at the boundary - which is `E29-T11` and wraps this.
- Persistence migrations and the boot procedure (`E29-T12`); this ticket provides snapshot/restore primitives and consumes E50-T02's envelope.
- The `MonotonicScheduler` (`E33-T01`). The shim deliberately has no timing facility at all.
- Any library integration; that is E50-T03's conformance harness and, if the gate passes, E50-X01.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A raising action does not commit its transition
  Given a transition whose action list is [persist, explode, notify]
  When the machine processes the triggering event
  Then the machine is not in the target state, context carries _fault, and the fault state is entered
  And the snapshot writer refuses to persist that context

Scenario: A self-transition re-enters
  Given a state with entry action inc and a self-target carrying reenter true
  When the triggering event is delivered five times
  Then inc has run five times

Scenario: An unhandled event is deferred, not discarded
  Given a machine in a state with no handler for EXEC
  When three EXEC events are delivered
  Then all three are in _deferred, cv_machine_unhandled_events_total has increased by three,
   and each was logged

Scenario: A deferral buffer survives a crash and drains at boot
  Given a machine crashed while in a state holding three deferred fills
  When the process restarts
  Then the three fills are drained before any invoke is re-driven, and the machine applies all three

Scenario: A raising guard denies rather than permitting
  Given a safety guard whose body raises
  When the guarded transition is evaluated
  Then the guard returns deny, an ERROR is logged, and the permissive branch is not taken

Scenario: Guard evaluation short-circuits
  Given a guarded branch list [g1 false, g2 true, g3 true]
  Then g2 is selected and g3 is never called

Scenario: A terminal machine is reaped
  Given a machine reaches a final state
  Then it is stopped and evicted, and cv_machine_live_count for its kind decreases by one

Scenario: A cross-thread send is not lost
  Given an event sent from a non-loop thread through send_threadsafe
  Then it is delivered exactly once, and a direct send from a foreign thread raises rather than
   silently dropping
```

## Technical notes / design
Lives in `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/`, target 1,500 LOC excluding tests, with the `E50-K01` estimate as the accepted budget. Exceeding it by more than 25% triggers an architect review rather than a quiet expansion.

Machine definitions are **shared** across instances and context is per-instance; the library measured a 19x build-cost saving from this (325 us to 17.3 us) and it costs nothing to do from the start. A test asserts contexts are not aliased and that target resolution does not mutate the shared definition (LC-47).

The action executor is the heart of the difference. Actions run against a **staged** context; the stage is committed only when the whole action list completes. A raise discards the stage, sets `_fault` on the live context and routes to the fault state. This is what makes MUST-01 enforceable in the executor rather than in a decorator every developer must remember.

There is no `SyncInterpreter` equivalent and there never will be (MUSTNOT-06): thread-per-timer and unlocked cross-thread context mutation are exactly what the shared-definition design depends on not existing.

## Test plan
Unit, one test per corrected behaviour above, each **named for the LC id it closes**, so a future reader can map the suite to the register. Property-based: random event sequences over the B1, B2 and B8 contracts asserting their catalogue invariants at every step. Chaos: kill mid-action, kill mid-invoke, kill with a non-empty deferral buffer, restart and assert recovery. Concurrency: cross-thread sends under load; shared-definition non-aliasing across 500 instances. Soak: 24 h with churn, asserting `cv_machine_live_count` returns to baseline (the reaper's real test). Coverage at least 90%; the B17 and B8 trace tests from `E50-K01` are promoted into this suite.

## Security notes
Actions and guards are resolved from a **static registry only**. The shim never `eval`s, never imports by name from machine JSON, and never accepts a machine definition from outside the repository - a machine definition is executable configuration and is treated as code (STRIDE: tampering, elevation of privilege). The shim is on the order path, so it inherits the order path's controls: every transition writes its audit trail through the existing writer (C-2.9), and no context, log line or metric label may contain a credential (C-2.7), asserted by a redaction test. **The shim is never an enforcement point** for a safety decision (MUSTNOT-05); it records and orchestrates while synchronous flags enforce. Security review label required.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. Where statechart state reaches the admin health panel (E42) it must be conveyed as text, never colour alone (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
Budgets from `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` and `10` Part C6, measured in E50-T06: at least 8,000 machine-ev/s aggregate with 500 resident order machines, and per-fill latency p95 under 1 ms on a healthy loop. Three design choices exist purely for this: no per-transition INFO logging (the measured profile was dominated by it), shared machine definitions, and compact snapshot serialisation. **C-2.17 applies**: no shim operation may block the asyncio loop beyond 50 ms. The shim is never on a hot path - MUSTNOT-01 and MUSTNOT-03 keep market-rate traffic out of it entirely, and that exclusion, not shim speed, is what makes the budget hold.

## Observability
Emits the full `cv_machine_*` set: `live_count{kind}`, `deferred_depth{kind}`, `unhandled_events_total{kind,event}`, `transition_seconds{kind}`, `quarantined_total{kind}`, `queue_depth{kind}`, and `cv_statechart_runtime{kind,runtime}`. Every quarantine raises P1. Every ERROR log from the shim routes to the P1 alert handler, because the shim logs at ERROR only for conditions that are defects by construction.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Shim merged, within the `E50-K01` LOC budget or with a recorded architect-approved variance.
- [ ] One passing test per corrected Blocker semantic, each named for its LC id.
- [ ] All twenty contracts load and their happy paths execute (full conformance is E50-T03).
- [ ] 24 h soak with churn shows `cv_machine_live_count` flat.
- [ ] Coverage at least 90%; no per-transition INFO logging, asserted by a test.
- [ ] Security engineer sign-off; architect code-owner review.
- [ ] `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/README.md` states the subset and the non-goals explicitly.

## Dependencies
- **E50-K01** - the subset and the LOC budget.
- **E50-T01** - pre-resolved, validated machine definitions.
- **E50-T02** - the snapshot envelope and the fault gate this cooperates with.
- **E04** - the metrics facade.
- Consumed by **E29-T11** (`MachineGateway`) and every lifecycle family.

## Branch
`feat/e50-statechart-shim`

## References

- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md
- docs/research/xstate/10-fit-analysis.md Part A, Part B, Part C

title: Dual-runtime conformance harness: every contract against both the shim and the library behind a feature flag
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: shim/dual-runtime/gate/decision work withdrawn by the owner decision for full adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted; 29-statechart-adoption-plan §4a)**

## Context
This is the ticket that makes ADR-0016's central claim true or false. The ADR asserts that adopting `xstate-statemachine` later is a **feature flag flip, not a rewrite**. That claim is only credible if there is a mechanism that answers "did the swap change any behaviour?" with green or red rather than with a judgement call, and that mechanism is this harness.

It has a second job that matters at least as much. The seven Blockers are all silent failures, and a library release that *claims* to fix one is not evidence that it did. Running the same contracts through both runtimes and diffing the traces turns "upstream says LC-03 is fixed" into an observation. That is what feeds `E50-T04`'s gate report and, ultimately, the go/no-go at `E50-X01`.

The harness is also the library-bump gate the adversarial review demands, and its warning applies directly: if `tests/xstate_contract/` cannot be kept under 60 s it will not gate bumps, and the pin becomes theatre. That budget is enforced by `E50-T06`.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `tests/xstate_contract/harness.py`: loads a contract and a **scenario** - an event sequence with expected state and action traces - and executes it against a named runtime.
- **Trace equality** as the assertion: the ordered sequence of `(active state set, actions executed, context deltas on named keys)` must be identical across runtimes. A divergence reports the machine, the scenario, the event index and the first differing step, not just "not equal".
- **Scenario sets per machine**, derived from the catalogue rather than invented: the happy path, each documented failure path, each invariant's witness sequence, and a crash-and-restore variant.
- **`CV_STATECHART_RUNTIME`** wiring: `shim` (default) and `library`, selectable per machine family, with the library import behind the vendored path so the flag works with or without the package installed.
- **One CI job running both**, so a divergence is a build failure rather than a nightly surprise. The library side is reported as **informational until the adoption gate passes** and blocking after - a divergence must never block delivery on a runtime we have not adopted.
- **The Blocker probes as conformance cases**: `adv01`, `adv05`, `adv06` and the `C17` fill-drop sequence expressed as scenarios, so the register's evidence and the test suite are the same artefact.
- A **conformance report** artefact per run: per machine, per runtime, pass/fail and the divergence list, consumed by `E50-T04`.

## Out of scope
- Adopting the library (`E50-X01`).
- The per-invariant behavioural suite over the production implementations (`E50-Q01`); this harness tests the **contract against the runtimes**, not the modules against the contract.
- The suite time budget and the throughput gate (`E50-T06`).
- Vendoring the library source (MUST-08) - that lands with adoption, not before.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Both runtimes agree on every contract
  Given all twenty contracts and their scenario sets
  When the harness runs with CV_STATECHART_RUNTIME=shim and again with =library
  Then the state trace and the action trace are identical for every scenario

Scenario: A divergence is actionable, not just red
  Given a scenario where the two runtimes differ
  Then the failure names the machine, the scenario, the event index, the expected step and the
   observed step for each runtime

Scenario: The fill-drop Blocker is a standing test, not a memory
  Given the C17 sequence: three PARTIAL fills delivered while the machine sits in an invoke state
  Then the shim applies or defers all three and none is discarded
  And the library's result is recorded in the conformance report as evidence for LC-03

Scenario: The action-failure Blocker is a standing test
  Given an action list of [persist, explode, notify] on a committed transition
  Then the shim does not enter the target state and sets _fault
  And the library's behaviour is recorded as evidence for LC-01 and LC-15

Scenario: The library side cannot block delivery before adoption
  Given the adoption gate has not passed
  When the library runtime diverges on a contract
  Then the job reports the divergence and the build is not failed by it
  And once the gate has passed the same divergence fails the build

Scenario: A contract without scenarios cannot pass silently
  Given a registered machine with no scenario set
  Then the harness fails naming the machine, so coverage cannot quietly shrink
```

## Technical notes / design
Trace equality is over a **normalised** trace: active state sets are sorted, context comparison is restricted to keys the scenario declares significant, and internal bookkeeping keys are excluded. Without normalisation the harness would fail on irrelevant representational differences - the library exposes active states as a flat set with no hierarchical `value` (LC-49), and the shim need not copy that - and a harness that cries wolf stops being run.

Scenarios live beside the contracts and are covered by the same `make gen` staleness discipline, so adding a transition without adding a scenario is visible in review.

The `library` runtime is imported lazily. Before adoption the package is a dev-only dependency, pinned `==` exactly with its source sha256 (MUST-07); it never enters the production dependency graph, which is what keeps a gated decision actually gated.

## Test plan
The harness is itself tested: a deliberately divergent stub runtime asserts the diff reporting names the right step; a scenario-less machine asserts the coverage failure; a normalisation test asserts that hierarchical-versus-flat state representation does not produce a false divergence. Every contract's scenario set must cover every transition in that contract at least once, asserted as a transition-coverage check, so "all green" means "all exercised".

## Security notes
The library is a dev/test-only dependency until the gate passes and must not appear in the production dependency graph - asserted by a dependency-boundary test, since an accidental production import would adopt an unadopted runtime by mistake. Scenarios use synthetic ids and quantities only; no recorded production data, no credentials. The harness executes registered actions from the static registry, exactly as the shim does.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. Where statechart state reaches the admin health panel (E42) it must be conveyed as text, never colour alone (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
The harness's own budget is owned by `E50-T06` (60 s total for `tests/xstate_contract/`). Design consequence: scenarios are short, deterministic and free of sleeps - every deadline in every contract is an absolute timestamp in context (A2), so scenarios advance a fake clock rather than waiting, which is the only reason a 20-machine dual-runtime suite can fit in 60 s at all.

## Observability
The conformance report is published as a CI artefact and summarised in the job output: machines passed, scenarios run, transitions covered, divergences by machine. `cv_statechart_runtime{kind,runtime}` makes the active executor visible in production for the same families the harness covers.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Harness, scenario sets for all twenty contracts, and the dual-runtime CI job merged.
- [ ] Transition coverage at 100% across scenario sets, enforced.
- [ ] The four Blocker probes expressed as scenarios and passing on the shim.
- [ ] Divergence reporting verified against a deliberately divergent stub runtime.
- [ ] Library runtime informational-only until the gate passes, and the switch to blocking is a one-line configuration change.
- [ ] Dependency-boundary test proves the library is not in the production graph.
- [ ] QA lead and architect review.

## Dependencies
- **E50-T07** - the shim runtime.
- **E50-S01 / E50-S02** - the contracts and their invariant ids.
- **E50-T02** - the snapshot envelope, used by the crash-and-restore scenarios.
- Feeds **E50-T04** (gate report), **E50-C01** (upstream contribution) and **E50-X01** (the decision).

## Branch
`feat/e50-conformance-harness`

## References
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md
- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md
- docs/research/xstate/10-fit-analysis.md Part A, Part B, Part C
- docs/research/xstate/11-adversarial-review.md section 3, section 5
- docs/research/xstate/12-challenge-register.md
- docs/research/xstate/adversarial/ (adv01, adv05, adv06)
- docs/research/xstate/05-semantics-probes.md (C17, C8/C9 determinism)
- docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md; docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0012-testing-pyramid.md

title: Track upstream [VERIFIED FIXED main@cec108b]: An action that raises still commits the transition, with no programmatic error channel
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context
> **Round-7 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `221ce7c`).** **Still VERIFIED FIXED at `221ce7c`.** No regression; the `verify`-set FAIL on LC-01 is our harness asserting the pre-#145 contract (H-1, round 6), now allow-listed in `run_gate.py` as `VERIFY_BASELINE_FAILURES`.
> Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md`, `docs/research/xstate/43-r7-findings-register.md`.

> **Round-6 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `cec108b`).** #145 closes the last live piece: `actionErrorPolicy:"fail"` halts with `status="stopped"` and a cleared configuration, retains `TransitionFailedError`, round-trips through a snapshot, and the halted blob is refused by `from_snapshot`. Symmetric on both engines. The `"rollback"` path is separately confirmed, with the caveat now tracked as R6-03. **Note:** the `plugins.py:201-202` docstring still says `status == "error"`; the code and CHANGELOG say `"stopped"` (R6-20, doc-only). Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §1/§5.

**Severity: Blocker. Register ids: LC-01, LC-15.**

Closing this upstream removes one of the seven Blockers that stand between CandleViewer and adopting `basiltt/xstate-statemachine`.

This Chore tracks the upstream fix. It is not a CandleViewer implementation ticket - the CandleViewer-side mitigation is already scoped elsewhere and is listed under "Current mitigation" below. The Chore exists because ADR-0016 gates adoption on these being fixed **upstream** and re-verified, and because a tracking item that lives only in a research document is a tracking item nobody looks at.

**Why this matters to us.** This is the defect that shapes the entire CandleViewer mitigation stack, and closing it upstream removes four layers of defensive scaffolding from the order path at once.

**Measured evidence.** The action handler catches `Exception`, logs "Action '%s' raised...; skipping remaining actions" and continues. Probe `bench_g2_error_channel.py`: `actions:["first","explode","third"] -> b` leaves `third` skipped but `entry_b` run, the machine in `b`, `status == "running"`, no exception raised, and `on_transition` fired as a success. Reproduced on **both** engines. Probe `adv01` extends it: the resulting half-applied state is then written by `get_snapshot()`, so the corruption becomes durable (LC-15).

**Affected contracts.** B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, B19, B20 - every order-path family.

**Current CandleViewer mitigation.** `@cv_action` wrapper writing `_fault`, a `FAULT` transition to `quarantined`, the ERROR-log-to-P1 handler, the snapshot fault gate (MUST-01) and independent reconciliation. Four layers, none sufficient alone, all silent if forgotten.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **File the upstream issue** against `basiltt/xstate-statemachine` with: the measured evidence above, a minimal runnable reproduction, the proposed fix, and the CandleViewer contracts affected. The register confirms there are no duplicate upstream issues to collide with.
- **Link it both ways**: the issue number recorded in `docs/research/xstate/12-challenge-register.md` against LC-01, LC-15, and this Chore linked from the issue.
- **Ensure the repro is in the gate**: `docs/research/xstate/issues/repro/` contains a runnable case that `run_gate.py` executes on every release, so "is it fixed?" is answered by the scheduled job (`E50-T04`) rather than by reading a changelog.
- **Proposed fix** to carry into the issue body: Add a per-machine `action_error_policy: continue | rollback | fail`. The rollback path already exists for *transition* failures (0.6.0 "Transition atomicity") and can be reused. Minimum viable: pass `failed_actions: list[str]` into `on_transition` and fire a dedicated `on_transition_failed` hook.
- **Re-verify on each release** and close this Chore only when the gate report shows the repro passing, not when the issue is marked closed upstream.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fix upstream. If the owner chooses to fix it - and as maintainer, that is a scheduling decision rather than a hope - that is work in the library's own repository and backlog, not here.
- The CandleViewer mitigation, which is already scoped in its own ticket and must ship regardless of whether this is ever fixed upstream. **Adoption is gated; delivery is not.**
- Vendoring or forking (MUST-08), which is a separate decision recorded in ADR-0016.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The issue exists and is discoverable from both directions
  Given this Chore is In Progress
  Then an upstream issue exists carrying the evidence, a minimal repro and the proposed fix
  And 12-challenge-register.md records its number against LC-01, LC-15

Scenario: The repro runs in the gate on every release
  Given a new upstream release
  When the scheduled gate job runs
  Then this item's repro is executed and its pass or fail appears in the gate report

Scenario: The Chore closes on evidence, not on assertion
  Given the upstream issue is marked closed
  When the gate next runs against a release containing the fix
  Then this Chore may be closed only if the repro passes in that report
  And if the issue is closed but the repro still fails, the Chore stays open and the
   discrepancy is recorded

Scenario: A fix that later regresses reopens the question
  Given this item passed in an earlier gate report
  When it fails in a later one
  Then a P1 alert fires and this Chore is reopened as a regression
```

## Technical notes / design
The repro must be **minimal and runnable without CandleViewer** - a single file against a clean install of the library - or it cannot be part of the gate and cannot be acted on upstream. Where the original evidence came from a probe under `docs/research/xstate/probes/` or `docs/research/xstate/adversarial/`, the repro is the reduced form of that probe, and the reduction is part of this Chore.

The register groups some upstream filings (several LC ids to one issue) where the underlying cause is shared. This Chore covers LC-01, LC-15 as one filing; the gate still evaluates each id's repro separately, because a partial fix that closes one id and not another is a realistic outcome and the report should say so.

## Test plan
The repro **is** the test, and it is a negative test today: it must **fail** against the current release, proving it actually exercises the defect. A repro that passes against the current release is broken and must be fixed before this Chore proceeds - a gate item that has always passed tests nothing. `E50-T04` executes it on every release and records the result.

## Security notes
The upstream issue carries reproduction code and measured behaviour only. It must contain no CandleViewer account identifiers, no strategy detail, no credentials and no data from a live or demo account (C-2.7). Because this is a Blocker on the order path, the issue should state the *class* of consequence - silent state corruption, lost fills - without describing CandleViewer's specific exposure.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. Where statechart state reaches the admin health panel (E42) it must be conveyed as text, never colour alone (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
No CandleViewer runtime impact; this Chore ships no product code. If this item is ever fixed upstream, the corresponding mitigation's cost can be removed, and that removal is scoped at `E50-X01` rather than assumed here.

## Observability
Visible through `cv_ci_xstate_gate_items_open{severity}` and the per-version gate reports. The count of open Blockers is the headline number at the Sprint 08 go/no-go.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Upstream issue filed with evidence, minimal repro and proposed fix; number recorded in `12-challenge-register.md` against LC-01, LC-15.
- [ ] Minimal repro committed under `docs/research/xstate/issues/repro/` and **verified to fail** against the current release.
- [ ] `run_gate.py` executes the repro and reports it per release.
- [ ] Closed only when a gate report shows the repro **passing** against a released version.
- [ ] Any close-without-pass discrepancy recorded in the register.
- [ ] Architect review (ADR-0016 is architect-owned).

## Dependencies
- **E50-T04** - the scheduled gate job that verifies closure. Filing may proceed before it exists; **closing may not**.
- `docs/research/xstate/12-challenge-register.md` - the register row this Chore tracks.
- Feeds **E50-X01**, whose input is the count of open Blockers and unmitigated High items.

## Branch
`chore/e50-u01-upstream-lc-01`

## References
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md
- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md
- docs/research/xstate/10-fit-analysis.md Part A, Part B, Part C
- docs/research/xstate/11-adversarial-review.md section 3, section 5
- docs/research/xstate/12-challenge-register.md
- docs/research/xstate/issues/LC-01-action-raise-commits-transition.md
- docs/research/xstate/20-adoption-gate.md; gate/run_gate.py
- docs/research/xstate/05-semantics-probes.md; docs/research/xstate/adversarial/

## Verified on 0.8.0 — 2026-09-17

**Gate run:** `xstate-statemachine` 0.8.0, commit `9bf6065`, CPython 3.13.7,
Windows 11 x64, `gate/run_gate.py` against the primary check set
(`docs/research/xstate/issues/verify-0.8.0/`). Evidence:
`docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md`.

- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-01 — FIXED-OPT-IN** (upstream #27). `actionErrorPolicy: "rollback"` restores configuration *and* context; `"fail"` rolls back and stops with `TransitionFailedError`. Covers every action slot including `start()`'s initial entry, and cancels `after` timers / invokes armed by a partially-entered target. Under the default `"continue"` the failure is now observable via `interpreter.last_transition_ok` and the `on_transition_failed` hook.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-15 — closed as a consequence.** `last_transition_ok` gives the persistence layer the cleanliness flag the issue asked for. MUST-01 (snapshot writer refuses a `_fault` context) is retained as defence in depth, not deleted.
- **Residual, carried into the design:** rollback is a context + configuration transaction, **not an effect transaction** — a `sendTo` or `raise` emitted by an earlier action in the same list survives it (new defect N-5). Constraint CV-C02 requires outward-facing actions to be last in their list. **Cost:** `"rollback"` measures **-22.4% throughput** while armed and never firing (35,532 -> 27,586 ev/s), which puts BENCH-1 at ~2.46x against its 3.0x bar (constraint CV-C13).
- **Follow-up drafted, not filed:** `docs/research/xstate/issues/followups-0.8.0/LC-01.md` (effect-transaction scope, the per-MachineNode DeprecationWarning, the armed cost, and the double `on_transition_failed` under `"continue"`).

**Acceptance criteria status:** **MET, CONDITIONALLY.** The Chore's Definition of Done requires a gate report showing the repro passing against a released version. `verify-0.8.0/LC-01_action-raise-commits-transition.py` exits 0. But the fix is **FIXED-OPT-IN**: `actionErrorPolicy` still defaults to `"continue"`, which commits the transition exactly as 0.7.0 did. This Chore therefore closes **only** once CV-LINT-XS1 enforces `actionErrorPolicy: "rollback"/"fail"` on every catalogue machine (`E29-T10`). Until then it stays open, per its own "close on evidence, not on assertion" criterion.

## Verification on `main` @ `5327ba6` (2026-09-18)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it. Source: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 2.

**Status: unchanged - STAYS OPEN, and the reason is still ours.** `verify-main-5327ba6/LC-01_action-error-policy.py` exits 0, and the fix gained real ground this window: `rollback`/`fail` now also **withdraw self-`raise`d events** queued by the failed action list (verified in eight hostile shapes including parallel regions and child actors), the default-flip `DeprecationWarning` fires once per **process** rather than once per `MachineNode`, and the no-action checkpoint skip removes the idle cost (reproduced at 0.998x-1.056x of baseline, versus 0.776x before).

Two limits are unchanged and keep the CandleViewer side intact: rollback is still **not an effect transaction** - it cannot un-send a `sendTo`, which the library now states explicitly - so **CV-C02 stands verbatim**; and `actionErrorPolicy` still defaults to `"continue"`. Upstream `#27` is **closable** (draft: `issues/comments-main-5327ba6/27.md`), but this Chore closes only when **CV-LINT-XS1** enforces `"rollback"/"fail"` on every catalogue machine (`E29-T10`).

New, riding along on `#27` rather than filed separately: the checkpoint-skip predicate does not model `always`/`on` action lists on the transition target (F-7, Medium; verified safe in the case tested, but narrower than the invariant it upholds).

## Verification on `main` @ `3c527b0` (2026-09-18, PR #83 merged)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it, two passes running. Source: `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 3.

**Status: VERIFIED unchanged - stays open against our own linter, not against upstream.** Nothing in PR #83 touches `actionErrorPolicy`. All nine acceptance criteria that describe behaviour hold; the two deviations are wording only (`InvalidConfigError` not `ValueError`; `failed_actions` surfaced via `on_transition_failed` + `last_transition_ok` rather than as an argument on `on_transition`). Upstream `#27` is **confirm closed** (`issues/post-3c527b0/27.md`).

This Chore still closes only when **CV-LINT-XS1** enforces `"rollback"/"fail"` on every catalogue machine (`E29-T10`). F-7 continues to ride along on `#27` as a Medium note (the checkpoint-skip predicate does not model `always`/`on` action lists on the transition target).

title: Track upstream [VERIFIED FIXED 0.8.0]: `always` with a self-target deadlocks silently
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context
**Severity: Blocker. Register ids: LC-02, LC-04.**

A deferred event's receipt resolves `changed=False, error=None`, indistinguishable from "processed, correctly no-op", for an event that is parked and about to drive its transition. A FILL arriving one microstep early - the precise scenario `defer` was adopted to fix - returns a receipt saying the fill did not land.

Drafted upstream as `issues/new-main/M-1-deferred-event-receipt-false-negative.md`. Mitigated our side by the **new CV-C06 clause**: a `changed=False, error=None` receipt is *inconclusive* while `deferred_count > 0`, locked by `test_receipt_is_inconclusive_when_deferred`.

## Verification on `main` @ `3c527b0` (2026-09-18, PR #83 merged)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it, two passes running. Source: `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 3.

**Status: STAYS OPEN, and the mitigation this Chore recorded is WITHDRAWN AS UNSOUND.**

`onUnhandled: "defer"` itself is unchanged and correct. **M-1 is STILL-PRESENT** on `3c527b0` - PR #83 rewrote `_handle_unhandled_event` (for `#79`) and reworked `interpreter.py` (for `#43`) and the receipt gap survived both. `Receipt` is still `('state_ids', 'changed', 'error')`; no field carries the defer disposition; the receipt object is not updated on replay.

**The material change is negative.** The **CV-C06 `deferred_count` clause this Chore recorded as our mitigation does not work.** At the caller's `await` point `deferred_count` reads **`0`** for the deferred case *and* for the genuine no-op - the `1` observed in the original probe is read from inside the macrostep, where a caller cannot stand. `test_receipt_is_inconclusive_when_deferred` **cannot be written as specified**.

**The clause is replaced by a prohibition:** a `wait=True` receipt reading `changed=False, error=None` is **inadmissible** as a gate on any machine configured `onUnhandled: "defer"` - which is every catalogue machine. **No order-path statechart ships** until either upstream fixes the receipt or `cv.statechart` obtains an out-of-band defer discriminator (a correlated `on_event_deferred` hook), which the library does not expose. Tracked as **`E50-C16`**.

Filed upstream as new issue 1 in `issues/post-3c527b0/` (High).

LC-13 compounds it: a duplicate `systemId` registration silently replaces the previous actor.

**Affected contracts.** B2, B3 - the whole fan-out path.

Unversioned 0.7.x payloads restore unchanged.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-17 — closed via LC-03** (see `E50-C05`).
- **NOT FIXED: LC-20.** Restoring a snapshot taken mid-`after` still does not resume the delayed transition (probe C6, `fired: false`). Out of scope for #44, which covers `invoke` only. Reconciling `pending_invocations()` against our own order/exec store is now the **only** signal that can catch it.
- **G-2 (High)** - event provenance is lost across a snapshot, so a restored `escalate` event becomes user traffic and fails a machine configured `onUnhandled: "error"`.

Both drive new constraint **CV-C20** (`cv.statechart.persistence` quiesces before snapshotting and reconciles every pending invocation on restore). **CV-C07 stands, strengthened.** LC-20 (`after` timers not resumed on restore) is still untouched.

title: Track upstream [PARTIAL main@cec108b]: Timers starve catastrophically under event-loop load and cannot be made deterministic
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context
> **Round-7 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `221ce7c`).** **Still PARTIAL, unchanged.** #174 documents the blocking-timer behaviour but **no code changed**: busy-loop `after` lateness still measures ~15-30 ms over a 50 ms budget, and the `after:100`-behind-a-500 ms-service class reproduces unchanged. Under 100 concurrent busy interpreters, mean timer error is ~130-160 ms with no hang. BENCH-6's `load_500` and `load_500+cpu_hog` tiers were **not run** for a second consecutive round (time budget) - a stated gap, not a result. The standing constraint (external `MonotonicScheduler` for all algo timing) stands. **New interaction worth recording here:** the documented remedy for a blocking service is `async def`, and upstream R7-01 makes `async def` invoke cycles unbounded - so there is currently no service kind safe on both axes (DC-4).
> Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md`, `docs/research/xstate/43-r7-findings-register.md`.

> **Round-6 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `cec108b`).** #118 fixes the `AfterEvent` telemetry fields (`scheduled_for`/`fired_at` restore as `None`, never `0.0`; `lateness_ms` is `None` when unknown) and #154 attaches the clock on both sync early-return paths. But **R6-14 is a regression**: `after` lateness is 88–92 ms against a 50 ms budget under a busy loop, 5/5 deterministic. The per-macrostep settle budget bounds iterations, not lateness. BENCH-6 remains unmet, so the standing constraint (external `MonotonicScheduler` for all algo timing) stands. Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §1/§5.

**Severity: High. Register ids: LC-26, LC-27, LC-38.**

This is one of the nineteen High items that must have either an upstream fix or a documented, tested, mechanically enforced mitigation before adoption.

This Chore tracks the upstream fix. It is not a CandleViewer implementation ticket - the CandleViewer-side mitigation is already scoped elsewhere and is listed under "Current mitigation" below. The Chore exists because ADR-0016 gates adoption on these being fixed **upstream** and re-verified, and because a tracking item that lives only in a research document is a tracking item nobody looks at.

**Why this matters to us.** Would let coarse timeouts stay in-machine, removing an entire external subsystem from the algo design.

**Measured evidence.** Under 500 busy interpreters a 10 ms `after` fires **2.25 s late**, with the absolute error constant across 10 ms, 100 ms and 1 s requests - the signature of event-loop starvation rather than timer inaccuracy. There is no clock injection, so `after` cannot be made deterministic in tests (LC-27). `SyncInterpreter` runs `after` timers on background threads with unlocked context mutation (LC-38).

**Affected contracts.** B5, B6, B7, B10, B13, B19, B20 - anything with a deadline.

**Current CandleViewer mitigation.** House rule A2: every deadline is an absolute `*_us` timestamp in context, armed by an external `MonotonicScheduler` and re-armed on restore. The catalogue contains no `after` at all, and the linter bans the key.

## Scope / Deliverables

- **Link it both ways**: the issue number recorded in `docs/research/xstate/12-challenge-register.md` against LC-26, LC-27, LC-38, and this Chore linked from the issue.

- **Proposed fix** to carry into the issue body: Document the starvation characteristic prominently, and add clock injection so `after` can be driven by a test clock. Isolating timer dispatch from the main event loop would close the starvation half.
- **Re-verify on each release** and close this Chore only when the gate report shows the repro passing, not when the issue is marked closed upstream.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fix upstream. If the owner chooses to fix it - and as maintainer, that is a scheduling decision rather than a hope - that is work in the library's own repository and backlog, not here.
- The CandleViewer mitigation, which is already scoped in its own ticket and must ship regardless of whether this is ever fixed upstream. **Adoption is gated; delivery is not.**
- Vendoring or forking (MUST-08), which is a separate decision recorded in ADR-0016.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The issue exists and is discoverable from both directions
  Given this Chore is In Progress
  Then an upstream issue exists carrying the evidence, a minimal repro and the proposed fix
  And 12-challenge-register.md records its number against LC-26, LC-27, LC-38

Scenario: The repro runs in the gate on every release
  Given a new upstream release
  When the scheduled gate job runs
  Then this item's repro is executed and its pass or fail appears in the gate report

Scenario: The Chore closes on evidence, not on assertion
  Given the upstream issue is marked closed
  When the gate next runs against a release containing the fix
  Then this Chore may be closed only if the repro passes in that report
  And if the issue is closed but the repro still fails, the Chore stays open and the
   discrepancy is recorded

Scenario: A fix that later regresses reopens the question
  Given this item passed in an earlier gate report
  When it fails in a later one
  Then a P1 alert fires and this Chore is reopened as a regression
```

## Technical notes / design
The repro must be **minimal and runnable without CandleViewer** - a single file against a clean install of the library - or it cannot be part of the gate and cannot be acted on upstream. Where the original evidence came from a probe under `docs/research/xstate/probes/` or `docs/research/xstate/adversarial/`, the repro is the reduced form of that probe, and the reduction is part of this Chore.

## Verified on 0.8.0 — 2026-09-17

**Gate run:** `xstate-statemachine` 0.8.0, commit `9bf6065`, CPython 3.13.7,
Windows 11 x64, `gate/run_gate.py` against the primary check set
(`docs/research/xstate/issues/verify-0.8.0/`). Evidence:
`docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md`.

- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-26 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (upstream #48). `RealClock` delivers a fired `after` through a **priority lane** the async run loop checks ahead of the inbox, so a due timer can no longer be starved behind a burst of external events. `AfterEvent` gains `scheduled_for`, `fired_at` and `lateness_ms`. Measured: p95 lateness at 500 busy interpreters **2530 ms -> 174.4 ms, a 14.5x improvement**.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-27 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (upstream #49). A `Clock` protocol with `RealClock` and `SimulatedClock` (virtual time), injectable on both engines and inherited by invoked/spawned children. A 600 ms `after` fires in 0.2 ms of wall clock. This is the change that makes replay/backtest deterministic.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-38 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (upstream #50). `SyncInterpreter` no longer spawns an OS thread per `after` timer or delayed send: 25 machines with armed timers -> **+0 threads**. The unlocked cross-thread context mutation is gone.
- **THRESHOLD STILL MISSED: BENCH-6.** 174.4 ms against a <=100 ms bar. Constraint CV-C12 therefore stands unchanged: `after` remains **banned** in catalogue machines; all algo timing (TWAP intervals, chase repricing, iceberg release) stays on the external `MonotonicScheduler` with absolute deadlines in context. Enforced by CV-LINT-XS10.
- **NEW HIGH DEFECT (N-2), drafted for filing.** `RealClock.set_timeout` branches on the *caller's* context, not the owning engine, so a `SyncInterpreter` constructed **inside a running asyncio loop** parks its deadlines on `loop.call_later`, leaving `clock._heap` empty — `tick()` then cannot deliver a genuinely-due deadline. Measured: off-loop `pending=1` -> `sy.b`; in-loop `pending=0` -> stuck at `sy.a`. Draft + repro: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-02-sync-timer-unreachable-in-loop.md`. Immaterial to us directly (MUSTNOT-06 bans `SyncInterpreter`) but it reinforces that ban.
- **Gotcha to encode in a test helper:** `SimulatedClock.increment()` takes **milliseconds** and, inside a running loop, returns a `_MustAwait` wrapper that is neither a coroutine nor a future — an `asyncio.iscoroutine()` guard silently skips the await and no timer fires. Constraint CV-C10 requires the shared `cv.testing.advance()` helper.

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it. Source: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 2.

New, drafted upstream as `issues/new-main/F-2-kwargs-clock-receives-unexpected-sync.md` (High): the legacy-clock compatibility shim treats a `**kwargs` clock as *consent* to receive `sync=`, so an ordinary 0.8.0-protocol wrapper is handed a keyword it has never heard of - failing at the first `after`, at runtime under load.
