title: Track upstream [VERIFIED FIXED main@cec108b]: A raising guard is swallowed as False, and guards keep being evaluated after a branch is selected
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context
> **Round-7 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `221ce7c`).** **Still VERIFIED FIXED at `221ce7c`, and materially improved.** #170 makes the receipt matrix `(denied, error, deferred, changed)` **injective** on both engines, which retires our W-04a wrapper obligation: `Receipt.denied` alone is a correct denial discriminator again.
> Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md`, `docs/research/xstate/43-r7-findings-register.md`.

> **Round-6 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `cec108b`).** #152 closes the previous round's ship-blocker: `guardErrorPolicy:"raise"` now cancels only the *failing* candidate, so the unguarded fallback is still taken, with `last_error`/`receipt.error` set. Verified on both engines. Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §1/§5.

**Severity: High. Register ids: LC-09, LC-10.**

This is one of the nineteen High items that must have either an upstream fix or a documented, tested, mechanically enforced mitigation before adoption.

This Chore tracks the upstream fix. It is not a CandleViewer implementation ticket - the CandleViewer-side mitigation is already scoped elsewhere and is listed under "Current mitigation" below. The Chore exists because ADR-0016 gates adoption on these being fixed **upstream** and re-verified, and because a tracking item that lives only in a research document is a tracking item nobody looks at.

**Why this matters to us.** Makes safety guards honest: a *crashing* risk check would stop being indistinguishable from a *failing* one.

**Measured evidence.** Probe A20: a guard that raises is caught and treated as `False`, so a crashing `within_risk_caps` and a correctly-denying one produce identical behaviour - and in an `or` composition it can fall through to the permissive branch. Probe A6: with `[g1 false, g2 true, g3 true]` the correct branch is selected but **all three guards are called**, so a guard with a counter or a cache write misbehaves.

**Affected contracts.** B1, B8, B9, B17, B18, B20 - every safety-guarded family.

**Current CandleViewer mitigation.** House rule A6: guards are pure, total and written in the **deny** polarity on safety paths, each with its own try/except returning `False` explicitly and logging at ERROR. The shim short-circuits and treats a raising guard as a loud error.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **File the upstream issue** against `basiltt/xstate-statemachine` with: the measured evidence above, a minimal runnable reproduction, the proposed fix, and the CandleViewer contracts affected. The register confirms there are no duplicate upstream issues to collide with.
- **Link it both ways**: the issue number recorded in `docs/research/xstate/12-challenge-register.md` against LC-09, LC-10, and this Chore linked from the issue.
- **Ensure the repro is in the gate**: `docs/research/xstate/issues/repro/` contains a runnable case that `run_gate.py` executes on every release, so "is it fixed?" is answered by the scheduled job (`E50-T04`) rather than by reading a changelog.
- **Proposed fix** to carry into the issue body: Add a guard error policy with an `on_guard_error` hook, defaulting to propagating rather than swallowing. Short-circuit guard evaluation once a branch is selected.
- **Re-verify on each release** and close this Chore only when the gate report shows the repro passing, not when the issue is marked closed upstream.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fix upstream. If the owner chooses to fix it - and as maintainer, that is a scheduling decision rather than a hope - that is work in the library's own repository and backlog, not here.
- The CandleViewer mitigation, which is already scoped in its own ticket and must ship regardless of whether this is ever fixed upstream. **Adoption is gated; delivery is not.**
- Vendoring or forking (MUST-08), which is a separate decision recorded in ADR-0016.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The issue exists and is discoverable from both directions
  Given this Chore is In Progress
  Then an upstream issue exists carrying the evidence, a minimal repro and the proposed fix
  And 12-challenge-register.md records its number against LC-09, LC-10

Scenario: The repro runs in the gate on every release
  Given a new upstream release
  When the scheduled gate job runs
  Then this item's repro is executed and its pass or fail appears in the gate report

Scenario: The Chore closes on evidence, not on assertion
  Given the upstream issue is marked closed
  When the gate next runs against a release containing the fix
  Then this Chore may be closed only if the repro passes in that report
  And if the issue is closed but the repro still fails, the Chore stays open and the
   discrepancy is recorded

Scenario: A fix that later regresses reopens the question
  Given this item passed in an earlier gate report
  When it fails in a later one
  Then a P1 alert fires and this Chore is reopened as a regression
```

## Technical notes / design
The repro must be **minimal and runnable without CandleViewer** - a single file against a clean install of the library - or it cannot be part of the gate and cannot be acted on upstream. Where the original evidence came from a probe under `docs/research/xstate/probes/` or `docs/research/xstate/adversarial/`, the repro is the reduced form of that probe, and the reduction is part of this Chore.

The register groups some upstream filings (several LC ids to one issue) where the underlying cause is shared. This Chore covers LC-09, LC-10 as one filing; the gate still evaluates each id's repro separately, because a partial fix that closes one id and not another is a realistic outcome and the report should say so.

## Test plan
The repro **is** the test, and it is a negative test today: it must **fail** against the current release, proving it actually exercises the defect. A repro that passes against the current release is broken and must be fixed before this Chore proceeds - a gate item that has always passed tests nothing. `E50-T04` executes it on every release and records the result.

## Security notes
The upstream issue carries reproduction code and measured behaviour only. It must contain no CandleViewer account identifiers, no strategy detail, no credentials and no data from a live or demo account (C-2.7). Standard disclosure hygiene applies.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. Where statechart state reaches the admin health panel (E42) it must be conveyed as text, never colour alone (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
No CandleViewer runtime impact; this Chore ships no product code. If this item is ever fixed upstream, the corresponding mitigation's cost can be removed, and that removal is scoped at `E50-X01` rather than assumed here.

## Observability
Visible through `cv_ci_xstate_gate_items_open{severity}` and the per-version gate reports. The count of open Blockers is the headline number at the Sprint 08 go/no-go.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Upstream issue filed with evidence, minimal repro and proposed fix; number recorded in `12-challenge-register.md` against LC-09, LC-10.
- [ ] Minimal repro committed under `docs/research/xstate/issues/repro/` and **verified to fail** against the current release.
- [ ] `run_gate.py` executes the repro and reports it per release.
- [ ] Closed only when a gate report shows the repro **passing** against a released version.
- [ ] Any close-without-pass discrepancy recorded in the register.
- [ ] Architect review (ADR-0016 is architect-owned).

## Dependencies
- **E50-T04** - the scheduled gate job that verifies closure. Filing may proceed before it exists; **closing may not**.
- `docs/research/xstate/12-challenge-register.md` - the register row this Chore tracks.
- Feeds **E50-X01**, whose input is the count of open Blockers and unmitigated High items.

## Branch
`chore/e50-u09-upstream-lc-09`

## References
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md
- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md
- docs/research/xstate/10-fit-analysis.md Part A, Part B, Part C
- docs/research/xstate/11-adversarial-review.md section 3, section 5
- docs/research/xstate/12-challenge-register.md
- docs/research/xstate/issues/LC-09-guard-exception-swallowed.md
- docs/research/xstate/20-adoption-gate.md; gate/run_gate.py
- docs/research/xstate/05-semantics-probes.md; docs/research/xstate/adversarial/

## Verified on 0.8.0 — 2026-09-17

**Gate run:** `xstate-statemachine` 0.8.0, commit `9bf6065`, CPython 3.13.7,
Windows 11 x64, `gate/run_gate.py` against the primary check set
(`docs/research/xstate/issues/verify-0.8.0/`). Evidence:
`docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md`.

- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-09 — FIXED-DEFAULT (observability) / FIXED-OPT-IN (outcome)** (upstream #35). `guardErrorPolicy: "false" | "true" | "raise"` was added, and crucially the new `on_guard_error` hook fires **under the 0.7.x default**, before the substituted result is reported. So a raising guard is no longer invisible even without opting in — which was the issue's core complaint. Changing the *transition outcome* still requires `"raise"`.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-10 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (grouped under #35).
- **Our setting is `guardErrorPolicy: "raise"`** on all twenty machines (CV-LINT-XS3), because house rule A6 makes safety guards deny-by-default: a guard that crashes must not be silently reported as a denial on the order path.
- **Not re-verified this pass:** `SyncInterpreter` propagation under `"raise"`, invalid-policy-value rejection at `create_machine()`, and the interpreter-level override of the machine-config policy. Immaterial — we do not use the sync engine and we set the policy in the machine JSON.

**Acceptance criteria status:** **MET, CONDITIONALLY.** The *observability* half — the actual complaint, that a crashing guard is indistinguishable from a denying one — is FIXED-DEFAULT. The *outcome* half needs `guardErrorPolicy: "raise"`, so this Chore closes once CV-LINT-XS3 enforces it.

## Verification on `main` @ `5327ba6` (2026-09-18)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it. Source: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 2.

**Status: unchanged.** Nothing in the `v0.8.0..5327ba6` diff touches `guardErrorPolicy` or guard short-circuiting, and no regression was found in this area. The position is exactly as recorded for 0.8.0: the *observability* half is FIXED-DEFAULT, the *outcome* half needs `guardErrorPolicy: "raise"`, so this Chore closes once **CV-LINT-XS3** enforces it (`E29-T10`). **CV-C04 stands** - `strict` and a non-default `actionErrorPolicy` are set together, neither alone closing the typo class.

## Verification on `main` @ `3c527b0` (2026-09-18, PR #83 merged)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it, two passes running. Source: `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 3.

**Status: unchanged.** No part of the `5327ba6..3c527b0` diff touches `guardErrorPolicy` or guard short-circuiting, and no regression was found. This Chore still closes once **CV-LINT-XS3** enforces `guardErrorPolicy: "raise"` (`E29-T10`). **CV-C04 stands.**

Residuals are Low/Medium: R6-08 (the `onUnhandled:"error"` receipt is unpopulated for one event) and R6-05. Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §1/§5.

**Severity: High. Register ids: LC-34, LC-41, LC-42, LC-43, LC-48, LC-49.**

This is one of the nineteen High items that must have either an upstream fix or a documented, tested, mechanically enforced mitigation before adoption.

This Chore tracks the upstream fix. It is not a CandleViewer implementation ticket - the CandleViewer-side mitigation is already scoped elsewhere and is listed under "Current mitigation" below. No strict mode: event names and payloads are unvalidated, so a typo'd event is deferred and replayed forever (LC-34). The interpreter queue is unbounded with no depth signal (LC-41). `send()` is fire-and-forget and cannot answer synchronously (LC-42). A cross-thread `send()` silently loses the event - the coroutine is simply never awaited (LC-43). Active states are a flat `Set[str]` with no hierarchical `value` (LC-49).

**Affected contracts.** All twenty.

**Current CandleViewer mitigation.** The `MachineGateway` (`E29-T11`) provides validation, dedupe, a bounded queue, thread-safe sends and metrics; the shim emits the `cv_machine_*` series directly; `E50-T05` provides the build-time event-name gate.

- The CandleViewer mitigation, which is already scoped in its own ticket and must ship regardless of whether this is ever fixed upstream. **Adoption is gated; delivery is not.**

## Verified on 0.8.0 — 2026-09-17

**Gate run:** `xstate-statemachine` 0.8.0, commit `9bf6065`, CPython 3.13.7,
Windows 11 x64, `gate/run_gate.py` against the primary check set
(`docs/research/xstate/issues/verify-0.8.0/`). Evidence:
`docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md`.

- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-48 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (upstream #33). Five error hooks on `PluginBase` — `on_transition_failed`, `on_guard_error`, `on_unhandled_event`, `on_error`, `on_done` — all implemented by `LoggingInspector`, all firing **under the 0.7.x defaults**. Existing plugins load unchanged. This is the right shape: observability unconditional, recovery opt-in.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-41 — FIXED-DEFAULT (`queue_depth`) / FIXED-OPT-IN (bounding)** (upstream #38). Bounded inbox with `RAISE` / `BLOCK` / `DROP_NEWEST`, plus `on_event_dropped`. Attacked hard: **13/13, no findings** — `RAISE` fires at exactly the bound, `BLOCK` applies real backpressure with zero loss, and a `BLOCK` send issued *from inside an action* correctly reroutes to the internal queue instead of self-deadlocking.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-42 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (upstream #39). `send(wait=True)` resolves to a `Receipt(state_ids, changed, error)` only after the whole macrostep, reports the **settled** state after `always` transitions, carries the action error, and resolves with `InterpreterStoppedError` rather than hanging on a stopped interpreter. `send(priority=True)` jumps a 20-deep backlog and is exempt from the bound.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-49 — FIXED-DEFAULT** (upstream #58). `interpreter.value` gives the active configuration in XState's hierarchical form, tree-walked so state keys containing `.` are safe. Lets us delete our bespoke id-string projector for the WebSocket UI feed.
- Verified 0.8.0: **LC-34 — FIXED-OPT-IN** (upstream #51). `strict` raises `UnknownEventError` synchronously at the call site with a difflib suggestion; `event_schemas` validates payloads independently of `strict`.
- **LC-43 — PARTIAL, with a regression** (upstream #37). The core fix is real: bare cross-thread `send()` now raises `WrongThreadError` instead of losing the event. **But `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(interp.send(...), loop)` — the pattern the original issue named as the only correct 0.7.0 form — now raises too**, undocumented and with no deprecation window, because the thread check runs eagerly before the coroutine is scheduled (new defect N-6). Constraint CV-C14 bans it and routes everything through a validating gateway wrapper.
- **NEW HIGH DEFECT (N-1), drafted for filing.** `send(event, wait=True)` keys its receipt map on `id(event_obj)`, so two concurrent sends with the **same `Event` instance** collide and the first future is never resolved — an unkillable coroutine, no error, no timeout. Controls rule out `id()` recycling (200-way concurrent with fresh objects all resolve). Constraint CV-C06 + CV-LINT-XS9 require a freshly-constructed event at every `wait=True` call site. Draft + repro: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-01-send-wait-receipt-id-collision.md`.
- **NEW MEDIUM DEFECT (N-4), drafted for filing.** `send_threadsafe()` — now the *only* cross-thread API — bypasses `strict` and `event_schemas` entirely. Verified: an invalid-payload `FILL` skips the validator **and transitions the machine**. Draft + repro: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-04-send-threadsafe-bypasses-strict.md`.
- **NEW MEDIUM DEFECT (N-8), drafted for filing.** Events named `error.*` or `done.*` are invisible to a `"*"` handler and exempt from `onUnhandled: "error"`. Constraint CV-C15 bans such names; `E50-T05`'s event-name gate enforces it. Draft + repro: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-08-error-done-namespace-invisible.md`.
- **Residual on LC-48:** `on_transition_failed` fires **twice** per transition under `"continue"` (once per action slot), and the async engine emits no `on_transition` for the initial entry while the sync engine does. Constraint CV-C09 requires our plugins to dedupe and to filter the synthetic init event.

**Acceptance criteria status:** **PARTIALLY MET — stays open.** Four of the six register ids are FIXED-DEFAULT, one is FIXED-OPT-IN, and **LC-43 is PARTIAL with a regression**. Two new defects (N-1 High, N-4 Medium) landed inside the features this Chore asked for. Keep open against LC-43, N-1 and N-4.

## Verification on `main` @ `5327ba6` (2026-09-18)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it. Source: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 2.

**Status: substantially improved - STAYS OPEN against newly-surfaced gaps in the same feature area.** Three items this Chore was held open against are now **FIXED**:

- **N-1** (`#39` / `#75`): receipts are no longer keyed on `id()` - the queued envelope gets its own identity via `Interpreter._detach()` at the send boundary. Held at 500-way concurrency under three policies simultaneously, and with `stop()` racing outstanding duplicates. **CV-C06's fresh-`Event` clause RETIRES**, and with it **CV-LINT-XS9**'s reuse rule and `test_send_receipt_fresh_event_only`.
- **N-4** (`#51` / `#78`): `send_threadsafe()` now runs `_check_strict` (name + schema) on the calling thread before anything is queued, under loop saturation and 10-thread contention. **CV-C14's gateway-validation clause RETIRES**; CV-C14 becomes a ban-only rule.
- **LC-43** (`#37`): the `WrongThreadError` message now names the `run_coroutine_threadsafe(interp.send(...))` idiom, states it is rejected since 0.8.0, and points to `send_threadsafe()`. The ban in CV-C14 is reinforced.

Stays open against: **M-2** (async `max_iterations` does not bound an action-side `send()` - drives new constraint **CV-C16** / CV-LINT-XS11), **M-6** (`send_threadsafe` error precedence before `start()`, riding along on `#78`), and the fact that a cut `raise` chain is entirely silent with `status` still `"running"` and `last_transition_ok` still `True` (drives **CV-C17**).

Note also that `#43` / LC-28 remains **NOT-FIXED** for its task-count criterion - still a flat 2.0 asyncio tasks per idle child at n=2/10/50. That is a capacity-planning input, not a correctness one: continue to budget 2 tasks per invoked/spawned child actor. The latency and idle-CPU wins from the poll removal are real and hold.

## Verification on `main` @ `3c527b0` (2026-09-18, PR #83 merged)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it, two passes running. Source: `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 3.

**Status: substantially improved again - STAYS OPEN, with one item closed and one new async hole.**

**Closed on this commit:** `#43`/LC-28's task-count criterion finally landed. An idle invoked child now costs **one** asyncio task, not two (`children + 1`; 1.0 tasks/child at n=2/10/50, independently reproduced three ways), `onDone` latency drops to 0.96 ms median, zero stray timer callbacks while idle, and teardown is clean on state exit, on parent `stop()` and on rollback of the entering transition. **Revise any capacity planning that used `2 x children`.** `#43` is confirm closed.

**Also landed:** `#80`'s `ErrorEvent(type, error, src)` gives us the programmatic error channel this Chore has been asking for on the invoke path - drives new constraint **CV-C21** (branch on `isinstance(event, ErrorEvent)`, read `event.error`; never `.data`, never `event.type.startswith("error.")`, never `event.payload.get(...)` on an error-shaped event). Note `escalate` is the one failure path **not** converted (G-6).

**New and open:** **G-1 (High)** - `Event.system` is a public, user-settable dataclass field, so `send(Event("X", system=True))` bypasses `strict`, `event_schemas`, `onUnhandled` and `"*"` on both engines and via `send_threadsafe`. Drives new constraint **CV-C19** (never forge it; never trust library provenance as a routing or trust boundary). **G-9 (Low)** - the completion-delivery task is created via `_loop_create_task` and registered with neither the `TaskManager` nor a strong reference (latent; 0/300 lost under a GC-hostile probe), riding along on `#43`. **G-8 (Medium)** - `SyncInterpreter` still never delivers `onError` for a failed invoked **child machine**, a fourth sync-only gap under CV-C03.

Stays open against M-2, M-6, G-1 and the still-silent chain cut (CV-C17).

title: Adoption go/no-go review: adopt, defer, or keep the shim permanently
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: shim/dual-runtime/gate/decision work withdrawn by the owner decision for full adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted; 29-statechart-adoption-plan §4a)**

> **ROUND 10 RECORDED VERDICT (2026-09-22, `main` @ `19cb1f1`, merge of PR #211, commit `4dbf86e`): ADOPT WITH CONSTRAINTS — decision-table ROW 8.** Up from row 6 at `f28719c`. Row 8 is *"all Blocker **and High** closed, all Medium triaged, benchmark thresholds not all met"*: **the constraints that remain are benchmark-derived architectural consequences, not containment for open library defects.** Round 9's own verdict named row 8 as "the honest ceiling for this library in our system." **We have reached it.**
>
> 8 issues verified: **all eight FIXED, clean — 0 partial, 0 not-fixed, 0 documentation-only.** **The first round in ten where every fix landed on every axis it claimed** — rounds 6/7/8/9 each found a fix holding on one engine or one service spelling and not the other; round 10 finds none.
>
> Post-refutation: **0 Blocker · 0 High · 5 Medium · 7 Low**, plus 1 refuted outright. **The High row is empty for the first time.** Trajectory: **4 Blocker · 8 High at round 5 -> 0 · 2 at round 9 -> 0 · 0 now.**
>
> **Both round-9 Highs are closed, at the sites round 9 named.** **R9-02 -> #203**: `after` selection gated on `is_system_event` at `base_interpreter.py:4624`; the discriminating control (a public `AfterEvent` firing a 60 s timer instantly at the **default** `strict=false`) is refused on both engines. **R9-04 -> #204**: roll-forward invoke arming closed on **both engines and both service kinds** — `LD-01` 3 leaks -> **0/6**, B6-B10 `def` lane 51/52 -> **52/52**, drives 13/14 -> **14/14**, and `167 rollback_reinvoke_spin` (a recorded *permanent* expected-FAIL) now **PASS x5/5**.
>
> **THE OWED MEASUREMENT IS DISCHARGED — it was the single largest risk on the board.** Decision-table row 2 keys on coverage and fires *before* any adoption row; round 9 could not finish the run inside its bound. The suite finished this round: **3505 passed, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 566.57 s, coverage 92.78 %** — above the library's own 90 % floor and our 86 % bar, up from 92.70 %. Row 2 is now not-triggered **on measured evidence rather than inference**.
>
> **Refutation moved all three Blocker/High library candidates DOWN and none up — the fifth consecutive round in which our own claims were what did not survive, and the first in which it was total.**
>  - **R10-01 (Blocker -> Low).** Seven engine-event forgery vectors, all reproducing — but **Class A** (in-process Python: `engine_after`, `type(held)(...)`, `pickle`, `deepcopy`, `_EngineAfter`, `_replace`) is *strictly weaker than its own premise*, since a plain registered action already writes context arbitrarily and a live `Interpreter` exposes `_enter_states`/`_exit_states`; and **Class B** (blob-write) was **tested, not accepted** — a hand-edited snapshot with **no event forgery whatsoever** restores to `{'z.late'}` with context `{'n': 999}`. The boundary #195/#203 actually target holds in every probe under `strict:true` + `onUnhandled:"error"`. **Not filed as a vulnerability.**
>  - **R10-02 (High -> REFUTED outright).** A self-targeting `onDone` is an **internal** transition by contract; XState v5 makes internal the default with `reenter: true` the opt-in, documented three times including a troubleshooting entry naming this exact shape. With `"reenter": true`, polled to convergence on both engines and both kinds: `entries == submits == 22 == maxIterations + 2`, `RunawayChainError`, stranded hook fired. **Zero violations.**
>  - **R10-03 (High -> Medium).** Real, but implied by the #206 changelog and `json-config.md:110`, and the **documented** `after` idiom measures 93/92 beats in 3 s with zero drops against 9 for the `raise(delay=)` spelling.
>
> **On the contract side, two Blockers and two Highs came off the library's ledger — proved by construction, not argument.** **R10-C1 -> our C-04** and **R10-C2 -> our C-07b**: corrected charts pass on **both engines and both spellings**; the engine follows the chart in every cell. **R10-C3 High -> Medium** (`stale_lockout` **is** escapable via `RECONNECTED`, so the High premise fails). **R10-C4 High -> REFUTED (Low)** (sibling-only kill declaration: 1.458 s vs **0.001 s** with an ancestor handler).
>
> **Contracts: 20/20 build clean on both service spellings, ZERO library defects across all four groups.** A first.
>
> **Constraints — retired: CV-C46** (order path never on `SyncInterpreter`) and **CV-C45's send-side clause**; **CV-C32 retires as a *safety* rule** while the rule stands verbatim, re-grounded on R10-D2. **Widened: CV-C45 restore clause** (match serialised `kind`, and **re-arm deadlines from context**). **New: CV-C47, CV-C48, CV-C49, CV-C50, CV-C4x** (E50-T37..T40).
>
> **Benchmarks:** **BENCH-2 still misses** (443.6 market ev/s vs 2 000 — ~4.5x, down from ~14x) and **BENCH-6 is UNMEASURED for a second consecutive round** (`bench_c_timers` timed out at 115 s with zero output). BENCH-1 reads as met (p95 144.6 ms vs 300 ms) and `bench_a` moved ~5x — but **no matched-load A/B was run**, the policy *ratios* held steady while the absolute baseline moved, and **neither improvement is relied upon**.
>
> **PIN: `xstate-statemachine == 0.8.1` once tagged, and ONLY if `__version__` on that tag actually reports `0.8.1`**; until then commit **`19cb1f1`** plus its **source sha256**, vendored per MUST-08. **We would pin a tag cut at this commit**, with one blocking precondition (bump `__version__`, still reporting `0.8.0` for a tenth round) and three doc fixes preferred in the same release (the `+2`/`+3` plateau contradiction; the overstated #209 lap-parity claim; naming #206 as a behaviour break).
>
> **PHASE-3 ORDER-PATH SHIM RETIREMENT MAY BEGIN** (E50-T34). Both library gates are closed and precondition (iii) is met at 92.78 %. The three remaining conditions carry **no library dependency**: five green nightlies, lint+tests, and a two-week canary.
>
> **The binding constraint on our order path is now entirely our own catalogue.** **C-04 and C-07b are the only Blockers of any kind left in a ten-round study, they are ours, and they are open five rounds.** Next thing to work: E50-T33.
>
> Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/59-r10-final-readiness-verdict.md`, `docs/research/xstate/58-r10-findings-register.md`, `docs/research/xstate/20-adoption-gate.md` §9.15, `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md` Amendment 10. Upstream drafts (**not posted**): `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-19cb1f1/`.

> **Round 9 input and recorded verdict (2026-09-22, `main` @ `f28719c`, merge of PR #202): ADOPT WITH CONSTRAINTS — all four lifecycle families, ORDER PATH INCLUDED.** This supersedes eight consecutive rounds of DEFER on the order path. Decision-table **row 6**.
>
> 12 issues verified: **11 fixed in code** (9 clean, 2 narrower than claimed), **1 partial** (#197), **0 not-fixed**, **0 documentation-only**. **Zero true PASS->FAIL gate regressions** (the single flip, `LC-42`, is a flaky sub-millisecond latency threshold, 4/5 PASS). Post-refutation **0 Blocker · 2 High · 5 Medium · 8 Low** — the best position in nine rounds; refutation moved **3 of 5** Blocker/High **down** (R9-01 Blocker->Low, R9-03 High->REFUTED outright, R9-05 High->Medium) and **none up**.
>
> **The Blocker row is EMPTY for the first time.** Round-8's R8-01 is closed by **#192**: the priority lane now sheds by provenance, not FIFO position — verified on both engines, both service kinds, and the real B18 kill switch (**12/12 presses accepted, 0 shed, press pre-empts the chain**). That was the single exit condition round 8 recorded, and nothing else had to move.
>
> **Two open Highs, both mechanically contained** — which is what makes this row 6 and not row 7 (a documented convention is explicitly not a mitigation):
> - **R9-02** — `after` transitions are selected on the **public exported** `AfterEvent`, never on #195's `_EngineAfter`. A forged `pending_events` record with **no `"engine"` flag** is handed straight to the inbox by `_enqueue_restored`, so a **60-second timer fires instantly from untrusted snapshot data even at `strict=true`**, with no API call. Contained by **CV-C45 (widened)** — E50-T29. Upstream fix is one line.
> - **R9-04** — a `def` service armed by a transition an `always` rolls **forward** is still submitted; **3 of 6 lanes leak**, contradicting `production-characteristics.md:97` verbatim and SCXML 6.4. Contained by **CV-C32 + new CV-C46** — E50-T30.
>
> **OWED MEASUREMENT, recorded as open rather than as a pass:** the full suite + coverage run did not finish inside the wall-clock bound (~51 % of tests observed green; 92.70 % at `6db65d8`). **Decision-table row 2 keys on coverage**, so it leads the round-10 recipe (E50-T24).
>
> **Pin policy:** `xstate-statemachine == 0.8.1` once tagged **and only if `__version__` on that tag actually reports `0.8.1`**; until then commit **`f28719c`** plus its **source sha256**, with a **vendored copy per MUST-08** as what CI and production build against. Nine rounds have keyed on commits because `__version__` still reports `0.8.0`.
>
> **Standing gate:** `tests/xstate_contract/` enters CI as a **blocking** gate on **both service spellings**. A red cell returns us to row 7 (DEFER) — this is the mechanism the whole verdict rests on.
>
> **What is now on the critical path is OURS.** C-04 (B16 elevation survives `LOGOUT`/`REVOKE`) and C-07b (B18 kill switch bricked by a guard-denied `RELEASE`) are the only Blockers of any kind still open, on machines the library has already cleared — E50-T14/T16.
>
> Verdict: `docs/research/xstate/54-r9-final-readiness-verdict.md` §6.

> **Round 8 input and recorded verdict (2026-09-21, `main` @ `6db65d8`): DEFER (order path) / GO (non-order paths under CV-C01...CV-C45).** 16 issues verified: **15 fixed in code** (10 clean, 5 narrower than claimed), **1 documentation-only** (#174), **0 not-fixed** - the first round with no not-fixed row. Suite 3 457 passed plus one load-sensitive flake at **92.70 %** coverage. **Zero true PASS->FAIL gate regressions** (the two deltas are OUR stale `machine_hash` fixtures, correctly superseded by #185). Post-refutation **1 Blocker · 3 High · 7 Medium · 4 Low** - the best position in eight rounds; refutation moved 3 of 6 Blocker/High **down**, none up.
>
> **Both round-7 Blockers are closed.** The single surviving Blocker is **R8-01**: the priority lane charges by provenance (`interpreter.py:2342-2389`) and sheds by queue position (`:1598`), so a priority event issued from an action livelocks unbounded and unobservably while an external one at an already-tripped chain is silently destroyed as `chain_budget`. It is the regression surface of this release's own #180 and is **one function's worth of work**.
>
> **Decision-table row 6 (ADOPT WITH CONSTRAINTS) is otherwise satisfied** - open-High is **3** (R8-02, R8-03, R8-05) against a bar of 5, each with a mechanically enforced mitigation. Closing R8-01 flips the verdict for the order path.
>
> **B16-B20 are now all LIBRARY-GO**, and what blocks B16 and B18 is **ours** (C-04, C-07b, both Blockers on any runtime). **B18 leaves the library-blocked set.**
>
> Verdict: `docs/research/xstate/49-r8-final-readiness-verdict.md`. Register: `48-r8-findings-register.md`. Upstream drafts (NOT posted): `issues/post-6db65d8/`.
>
> **Pin:** commit `6db65d8` + source sha256, evaluation only, endorsement withheld; vendored copy per MUST-08 for the non-order machines going live now. On adoption: `xstate-statemachine == 0.8.1` once tagged, **and only if the tag is cut after R8-01 lands**.
>
> **Exit condition:** R8-01's two repros exit 0 at the commit under test, and the upstream fix ships with a test parametrised over issuer provenance x chain state x service kind. Then re-run this ticket.

## Context
> **Round 7 input and recorded verdict (2026-09-20, `main` @ `221ce7c`): DEFER (order path) / GO (non-order paths)** - same direction as round 6, different cause. 12 issues verified: 7 fixed, 2 partial (#167/#168 - one defect), 2 documentation-only (#122 correct-as-designed, our reopen withdrawn; #174 open), 1 not-fixed (#175 Case D). Suite 3 418/0 plus one non-reproducible flake at **92.64 %** coverage. **Zero true PASS->FAIL gate regressions**, and three regressions introduced by this round's own fix work that the gate cannot see. Post-refutation **2 Blocker · 4 High · 6 Medium · 8 Low**; refutation moved 3 of 8 Blocker/High **down**, none up, and refuted one outright.
>
> **Decision-table row 4** (Blocker row non-empty). The two Blockers are **R7-01** (an `async def` invoked service's completion is published on the public inbox lane and never charged, so every self-generated invoke cycle is unbounded - 28 108 service calls vs **23** for the identical chart with `def`, with one variant settling into an **empty configuration** reporting `ok=True`) and **R7-02** (external `send(priority=True)` charged to the chain budget - 751 of 1 500 dropped as `chain_budget`, control drops zero). **Neither is wrappable, and this round tested that rather than asserting it** (DC-4: the only mitigation for R7-01 is plain-`def` services, which #174 documents as blocking the machine's own `after` timers, and our own refutation of R7-04 shows plain `def` has its own inbox-starvation failure on the same shape - there is no service kind safe on both axes).
>
> **Non-order paths GO now** (B10-B17, B19, B20) under CV-C01…CV-C42. B19 is included because CV-C38 bounds its only invoke cycle; **B18 is excluded** because its kill-switch path is itself the unbounded shape (one `ENGAGE` produced 3 547 `flatten_all_positions` invocations in 3.0 s, still accelerating, `status="running"`, `error=None`). **Order path (B1-B9, B18) DEFERS** to the in-house shim. **Exit condition:** R7-01 and R7-02 closed with pinned tests **parametrised over service kind** -> Blocker row clears, open-High is 4, each mechanically mitigated = decision-table row 6, ADOPT WITH CONSTRAINTS. Re-verification recipe: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md` §9. **X01 re-runs when those two lines land upstream.**

> **Round 6 input (2026-09-20, main @cec108b):** **DEFER (order path) / GO (non-order paths)** — unchanged in direction, much narrower in cause. 26 issues verified (24 closed, 1 partial #122, 1 not-fixed #157); 3 Medium regressions; suite 3399/0 at **92.77 %** coverage (new 90 % floor). Post-refutation **2 Blocker · 2 High · 7 Medium · 9 Low** — refutation moved 6 of 10 Blocker/High candidates *down*, none up. Both Blockers (R6-01 async `always`+completed-`invoke` livelock; R6-03 `rollback`+`invoke.onDone` re-invoking ~1400/s silently) are **async-only**, with the sync engine provably correct, and **one upstream change closes both plus R6-02**: give `interpreter.py` the sync engine's chain/macrostep termination accounting (`:1427` exemption + porting #144's rule to `_run_event_loop`). Absent them, open-High is 2 — inside the bar of 5, both mechanically mitigated — i.e. decision row 6, ADOPT WITH CONSTRAINTS. Non-order machines B10–B17/B19/B20 move to the library now under CV-C01–C37 (they drove **zero** new library defects this round); order path stays on the shim. **Do not pin a 0.8.1 tag cut at `cec108b`.** Exit condition: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §9. Shim-retirement ladder: §10.6. ADR-0016 Amendment 6.
> **Round 5 input (2026-09-19, main @3ed3099):** **DEFER (order path) / GO (non-order paths).** 39 issues verified (34 closed, 5 partial), no regressions, suite 3322/0. New: 4 Blocker (R5-01 parallel-tear snapshot, R5-02 no restore legality check, R5-04 nested-invoke livelock, R5-12 `fail` policy reverts to source) + 8 High. Non-order machines B10–B17/B19/B20 may move to the library now under CV-C01–C34; order path stays on the shim. Exit condition: `docs/research/xstate/34-r5-final-readiness-verdict.md` §9. ADR-0016 Amendment 5.
> **Round 4 input (2026-09-18, main @5e07ba8):** gate = **DEFER** on open Blockers R4-01 (torn mid-macrostep snapshot) and R4-04 (non-terminating start); 6 High incl. R4-06/R4-07 introduced by the round-3 fixes. Operative blocker is upstream. Exit condition + re-verification recipe: `docs/research/xstate/29-r4-final-verdict.md` §8. Non-order paths may start under CV-C23–C29 (ADR-0016 Amendment 4).
ADR-0016 is **Proposed (gated)**, and this is the ticket that resolves the gated half. The ADR's decision deadline is this review, and it exists on a fixed date precisely so the question is answered rather than drifting.

Three things are decided here, and they are genuinely open:

**Adopt.** Every Blocker closed upstream and verified by a passing repro in the gate report; every High item fixed or mechanically mitigated; conformance parity green on both runtimes; the performance budgets holding; the contract suite under 60 s; the prerequisites (`E29-T10`, `E29-T11`, `E29-T12`, the reaper) shipped; the pin and the vendored copy in place. Adoption is then a per-family flag flip with the harness green on both sides.

**Defer.** Progress is real but incomplete. The shim remains the runtime and this review is repeated at the next train boundary. This costs nothing, because no delivery date depends on the outcome.

**Keep the shim permanently.** This is a **first-class outcome, not a failure state**, and the ADR says so explicitly. If the shim has proven reliable, the contracts are enforced, and the library's remaining advantages do not justify a migration, then closing ADR-0016 Part 3 is the honest answer. The ADR's own risk list names the temptation in the other direction too - a shim comfortable enough to reduce the pressure to ever adopt - so this review must weigh both.

The review's inputs are evidence, not opinion: the latest gate report, the conformance report, the benchmark results, the invariant suite status, the open-Blocker count, and the operational record of the shim to date.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Assemble the evidence pack**: the latest `docs/research/xstate/gate/reports/<version>.md`; the dual-runtime conformance report; benchmark results against budget; `E50-Q01` invariant coverage and chaos/soak results; the open-Blocker and unmitigated-High counts; the status of each `E50-U*` Chore; and the shim's production record - quarantines, stranded deferrals, unhandled events, live-count drift.
- **Evaluate all seven gate criteria** from ADR-0016 Part 3 explicitly, each answered yes or no with its evidence, with no criterion answered by judgement alone.
- **Assess the cost of each outcome**: migration effort and risk for *adopt*; carrying cost for *defer*; the maintenance and key-person implications of *keep permanently*, including what happens to the shim if its author is unavailable (`R10 Key-person` is this Epic's risk category for a reason).
- **Decide**, with the Owner, the Architect, the Backend lead, QA and DevSecOps present.
- **Record the decision** as a dated amendment to ADR-0016 (never an in-place edit of a decided outcome - `27-adrs/README.md` rule 3), naming the evidence and the reasoning.
- **If adopting**: a migration plan with per-family flag order, the pin and sha256 (MUST-07), the vendored copy and import switch (MUST-08), the quarterly vendored-copy test, and the point at which the library side of the conformance job becomes blocking.
- **If deferring**: the next review date and the specific criteria that must change.
- **If keeping the shim**: close ADR-0016 Part 3, stand down `E50-T04`'s schedule to quarterly, and record the shim's long-term ownership and its bus-factor mitigation.

## Out of scope
- Performing the migration, which is a follow-on epic scoped only if *adopt* is chosen.
- Fixing anything upstream (`E50-U*`).
- Reopening the *contract* half of ADR-0016. The contracts are binding regardless of outcome; that half was never gated and nothing in this review reconsiders it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The review happens on schedule regardless of the answer
  Given Sprint 08
  Then the review is held with the Owner, Architect, Backend lead, QA and DevSecOps
  And it is held even if the obvious answer is defer

Scenario: Every criterion is answered with evidence
  Given the seven gate criteria in ADR-0016 Part 3
  Then each is recorded as met or not met with the artefact that shows it
  And no criterion is recorded as met on the basis of an upstream issue being closed alone

Scenario: The outcome is recorded where it will be found
  When the review concludes
  Then ADR-0016 carries a dated amendment naming the outcome, the evidence and the reasoning
  And the original decision text is not edited in place

Scenario: Keeping the shim is a real option
  Given the shim has met every budget and the contracts are enforced
  When the review runs
  Then keep-the-shim-permanently is evaluated on its merits, including its key-person risk,
   and is not treated as a failure to adopt

Scenario: Adoption, if chosen, is bounded and reversible
  Given the outcome is adopt
  Then the plan specifies per-family flag order, the exact pin with sha256, the vendored copy,
   and the rollback path for each family

Scenario: No delivery date moves either way
  When the outcome is recorded
  Then no R0-R5 milestone, exit criterion or sprint commitment changes as a result
```

## Technical notes / design
The review is a **decision ticket**, and its product is a recorded decision with its reasoning, not code. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`'s Spike DoD applies.

Two failure modes are worth naming in advance, because both are likely. The first is adopting on a *closed issue* rather than a *passing repro*: a Blocker marked fixed upstream whose repro still fails is not closed, and the gate report exists to make that distinction unavoidable. The second is deferring indefinitely without saying so - if the answer has been *defer* twice, the review should seriously evaluate *keep permanently*, because a third deferral is usually that decision made by omission.

The key-person question deserves real weight in the *keep permanently* branch. The shim is ~1,500 LOC of order-path infrastructure written in-house; the library is 12,104 LOC maintained by the same person. Neither option escapes the concentration, and the review should say which one it prefers to concentrate on rather than pretending the choice removes the risk.

## Test plan
No code. The evidence pack is validated by re-running the gate and the conformance harness on the day of the review rather than relying on a stale report, since a report more than a release old may describe a version nobody would adopt.

## Security notes
If the outcome is *adopt*, the security consequences are explicit and must be part of the decision: a new third-party runtime enters the order path, which requires the exact pin with source sha256 (MUST-07), the vendored copy with a quarterly contract-suite test (MUST-08), Trivy/pip-audit coverage, and a supply-chain review. MUSTNOT-05 and MUSTNOT-06 continue to hold under either runtime: statecharts never enforce safety decisions, and `SyncInterpreter` is never used. DevSecOps sign-off is required on an *adopt* outcome specifically.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. Where statechart state reaches the admin health panel (E42) it must be conveyed as text, never colour alone (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
The benchmark results are a review input: adoption requires the budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` to hold under the library as measured by `E50-T06`, not as claimed. If the library is faster than the shim, that is a genuine argument for adoption and should be recorded as one; if it is slower, adoption must show the budget still holds.

## Observability
Post-decision, `cv_statechart_runtime{kind,runtime}` shows the active executor per family, so a phased adoption is visible in Grafana and a rollback is observable rather than inferred.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Evidence pack assembled with a gate report no older than the latest release.
- [ ] All seven ADR-0016 Part 3 criteria answered with evidence.
- [ ] Cost and risk of all three outcomes assessed, including key-person risk on the shim branch.
- [ ] Decision taken with the Owner present.
- [ ] Dated amendment merged into ADR-0016; `27-adrs/README.md` status updated.
- [ ] Outcome-specific plan recorded: migration plan, next review date, or Part 3 closure.
- [ ] DevSecOps sign-off if the outcome is adopt.
- [ ] `E50-T08` raised to fold the outcome into the plan documents.

## Dependencies
- **E50-T04** - the gate report is the primary input.
- **E50-Q01** - invariant, chaos and soak evidence.
- **E50-T06** - budget evidence.
- **E50-C01** - the upstream suite materially affects the maintenance argument.
- **E50-C03..U10** - their statuses are the open-Blocker count.
- Feeds **E50-T08**.

## Branch
`spike/e50-adoption-go-no-go`

## Input to this review: the 0.8.0 re-evaluation (2026-09-17)

This section is evidence for the review, not the review's outcome. The decision
is still taken at Sprint 08 with the Owner, Architect, Backend lead, QA and
DevSecOps present, and *defer* and *keep the shim permanently* remain live
options.

**Source of truth:** `docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md`, backed by
`13`-`16` (benchmarks, 51 semantic probes, 11 adversarial probes, full source-diff
review) and 34 per-issue re-verifications in `issues/verify-0.8.0/`.

### The gate report

```
Gate run 2026-09-17 - xstate-statemachine 0.8.0 (9bf6065)
DECISION: ADOPT WITH CONSTRAINTS, CONDITIONAL
  repros   : 12/34 pass unconditional; 9 verified fixed-but-opt-in; 13 stale/triaged; 0 unfixed
  probes   : 43/51 pass (was 41/51)
  benches  : 5/7 thresholds met (was 2/7)
  suite    : 3170 passed, 13 skipped, 0 failed
  blockers open: none, CONDITIONAL on the LC-01/LC-03 config being lint-enforced
  high open    : LC-07, LC-26, LC-38, LC-43
  new defects  : N-1..N-17 (2 High, 9 Medium, 6 Low, 0 Blocker)
  constraints  : CV-C01..CV-C15
```

Classification of the 34 filed issues: **23 FIXED-DEFAULT, 6 FIXED-OPT-IN,
5 PARTIAL, 0 NOT-FIXED.**

### The seven ADR-0016 Part 3 criteria, each answered with evidence

| # | Criterion | Met? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Every Blocker closed upstream | **Yes, conditionally** | LC-02, LC-16 FIXED-DEFAULT; LC-01, LC-03 **FIXED-OPT-IN**; LC-15, LC-17 close as consequences. Conditional on criterion 6. |
| 2 | Every High fixed or mechanically mitigated | **Partly** | 13 FIXED-DEFAULT, 3 FIXED-OPT-IN, 4 PARTIAL. Mechanisms specified (CV-C01..C15) but not built. |
| 3 | Conformance parity on both runtimes | **No** | `E50-T03` not shipped. |
| 4 | Performance gate holds | **No** | BENCH-2 380.9 vs >=2000 ev/s; BENCH-6 174.4 vs <=100 ms. |
| 5 | `tests/xstate_contract/` under 60 s | **No** | Suite does not exist. |
| 6 | Prerequisites shipped (`E29-T10/T11/T12`, reaper) | **No** | **The binding constraint.** |
| 7 | Pin + vendored copy | **No** | Re-pin target `== 0.8.0` + sha256. |

### The one thing this review must decide clearly

**Two of the four filed Blockers (LC-01, LC-03) are closed by a per-machine
policy whose default still reproduces 0.7.x behaviour.** They are closed for a
caller that sets the option and open for one that does not. Because every Blocker
in the register is a *silent* failure and MUST-09 holds that an unenforced rule is
not a rule, the review must satisfy itself that CV-LINT-XS1/XS2 in `E29-T10`
actually ship and are blocking - not that the upstream fix exists. If the linter
is not green, criterion 1 is not met and decision-table row 4 (DEFER) applies.

**What genuinely changed since 2026-09-15:** the remaining work moved from
upstream (unbounded) to us (`E29-T10` + `tests/xstate_contract/`, both already
required by MUST-09 before the first statechart regardless of runtime). That is
the material argument for *adopt with constraints* over *defer*.

**What argues the other way, and must be weighed rather than waved past:**

1. The mandated configuration costs **-22.4% throughput** while armed and idle
   (`actionErrorPolicy="rollback"`: 35,532 -> 27,586 ev/s), putting BENCH-1 at
   ~2.46x against its 3.0x bar. Criterion 4 is missed partly *because of* the
   configuration criterion 1 depends on.
2. **17 new defects**, two of them High, both inside features 0.8.0 added:
   `send(wait=True)` hangs forever on a reused `Event` instance (N-1), and
   `SyncInterpreter` timers become unreachable by `tick()` in a running loop
   (N-2). The release did not entirely escape its own critique.
3. `rollback` is a context + configuration transaction, **not an effect
   transaction** (N-5) - so CV-C02 becomes a standing design rule on every
   machine, which is exactly the class of "mitigation that fails silently if a
   developer forgets it" this Epic exists to eliminate.

### Recommended framing for the decision

A **split outcome** is available and is probably the honest one:

- **Non-order paths** (replay/backtest, rule-runtime lifecycle, B10-B14,
  B16-B20): adopt now under the *legitimate* partial-adoption path in
  `20-adoption-gate.md` s.8. Every Blocker affecting them is FIXED-DEFAULT, and a
  silent no-op there costs a wrong chart, not money. Requires the written
  boundary and the contract suite for those families.
- **Order path** (B1-B9, B19, B20): adopt **only** once `E29-T10` (with
  CV-LINT-XS1..XS10) and `tests/xstate_contract/` are green, then per-family
  behind `CV_STATECHART_RUNTIME`. Until then the shim remains.

Record whichever outcome is chosen as a dated amendment to ADR-0016 (Amendment 2;
Amendment 1 already records this re-evaluation), per `27-adrs/README.md` rule 3.

## Latest verdict feeding this review - `main` @ `5327ba6` (2026-09-18)

> **Identify the build by commit.** `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on commit `5327ba69fb735cfe24c7b3772050dac0a71a7b3d` while its CHANGELOG targets 0.8.1. Full write-up: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 **Amendment 2**.

```
Gate run 2026-09-18 - xstate-statemachine main @ 5327ba6 (unreleased, pre-0.8.1)
DECISION: ADOPT WITH CONSTRAINTS, CONDITIONAL (unchanged in form from 0.8.0)
  verify (mandated config, blocking) : 32/34 pass - FAILs: #43, #60/LC-52
  repro  (defaults, informational)   : 13/34 pass
  probes                             : 43/51-equivalent, identical baseline
  suite                              : 3234 passed, 13 skipped, 0 failed (was 3170)
  coverage                           : 90% (was 87% at 0.7.0)
  benches                            : BENCH-1 armed 2.43x (bar >=3.0x);
                                       BENCH-2, BENCH-6 still missed
  regressions                        : NONE
  blockers open                      : none (LC-01, LC-03 FIXED-OPT-IN)
  high open                          : LC-07/#31 (narrowed), M-1, F-1, F-2
  new defects                        : 13 (3 High, 6 Medium, 3 Low, 0 Blocker)
  constraints                        : CV-C01..CV-C18 (2 clauses RETIRED, 3 NEW)
```

**What this review must carry forward.**

1. **The condition is ours, not upstream's - and that is now unambiguous.** Every Blocker is closed; both 0.8.0-era High defects that lacked a mitigation are fixed; two CandleViewer constraints retired *into* the library (CV-C06's fresh-`Event` clause, CV-C14's gateway validation). The remaining upstream items sit behind an opt-out we never take, a capacity-planning line item, an ergonomics gap, or a namespace CV-C15 already bans. **Nothing upstream blocks a non-order path.** Criterion 6 - `E29-T10` plus `tests/xstate_contract/` - is the single gate for those families.

2. **The order path has one additional, specific blocker: M-1 (High).** `onUnhandled: "defer"` (CV-C01) and `send(wait=True)` (CV-C06) - the two settings the order path is *mandated* to use together - compose into a confident false negative: a deferred event's receipt resolves `changed=False, error=None`, denying a transition that is about to happen. This review must ask explicitly whether M-1 is fixed upstream **or** covered by the new CV-C06 `deferred_count` clause in `cv.statechart`, locked by `test_receipt_is_inconclusive_when_deferred`. A "we'll be careful" answer is not admissible - the defect produces a *confidently wrong* answer, and carefulness does not detect those.

3. **Constraint delta to apply before adopting anything.** Retire: CV-LINT-XS9's fresh-`Event` rule, and the gateway's duplicate validation. Add: **CV-C16** (no self-`send()` in actions; CV-LINT-XS11), **CV-C17** (no `raise` chain deeper than 1,000; the cut is silent), **CV-C18** (one `MachineLogic` per `create_machine()`, one spelling per implementation; CV-LINT-XS12, `MachineLogic(strict=True)` in the factory). The six-key machine-config block itself is **unchanged** - no library default moved.

4. **The pin is a commit, not a version.** Evaluate `== 0.8.1` **once tagged**; until then commit `5327ba6` with sha256. Before pinning, confirm upstream has bumped `__version__` (it has not), and ideally that the three defects in the `#77` fix's own code path (F-1, F-6, M-2) are resolved.

5. **Performance posture is unchanged and accepted.** BENCH-1 with `rollback` armed measures **2.43x** against the >=3.0x bar - statistically identical to 0.8.0's ~2.46x, not a regression. CV-C13 (dedicated event loop / process) is what buys it back. Note the CHANGELOG's "~0.98x of the default" for the new checkpoint skip applies **only to transitions that run no actions**; no CandleViewer machine qualifies.

6. **Upstream debt we owe, drafted and unfiled.** Eight new-issue drafts (`docs/research/xstate/issues/new-main/`), sixteen verification comments and a meta-issue update (`issues/comments-main-5327ba6/`). Filing remains tracked on the `E50-C*` chores; this review should confirm it has happened rather than assume it.

## Verdict input from `main` @ `3c527b0` (2026-09-18, PR #83 merged)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it, two verification passes running. Source: `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 3. **This section supersedes the `5327ba6` input above as the current position.**

**The gate decision has moved to DEFER for the first time since 0.7.0**, and this review must start from that rather than from the earlier "adopt with constraints" reading.

1. **The decision is arithmetic, not a re-weighting.** `20-adoption-gate.md` §7's table is applied in order and **row 5 matches on the merits**: all Blockers closed, **7 High open** against a bar of 5. Four are carried forward (LC-07/`#31`, M-1, F-1, F-2) and three are new, all from PR #83 - **G-1** (`Event.system` is a public, user-settable field that bypasses `strict`, `onUnhandled` and `"*"`), **G-2** (event provenance is not persisted, so a restored `escalate` event becomes user traffic and fails a machine configured `onUnhandled: "error"` - the one behavioural regression in the window), **G-3** (a pending `ErrorEvent` is silently dropped by `get_persisted_snapshot()`, so a machine restores believing its invoke never failed). Nothing was promoted in severity to force the row.

2. **This is a pre-release build, and the expected path back is short.** Fixing G-2 and G-3 before 0.8.1 tags returns the count to 5 and restores row 6. Both are filed upstream with runnable repros, ranked first in our release-readiness note. **This review must therefore ask a dated question: were G-2 and G-3 fixed before the tag?** If yes, the decision reverts and the remaining condition is ours again (`E29-T10` + `tests/xstate_contract/`). If no, they are documented 0.8.1 behaviour we must design around, and CV-C20 becomes permanent rather than a bridge.

3. **The order path's blocker got worse, not better.** M-1 is unchanged - a deferred event's `wait=True` receipt still resolves `changed=False, error=None` - and **the CV-C06 `deferred_count` mitigation recorded at `5327ba6` has been shown unsound**: at the caller's `await` point it reads `0` for the deferred case *and* the true negative, so `test_receipt_is_inconclusive_when_deferred` cannot be written as specified. The clause is withdrawn and replaced by a prohibition (see `E50-C16`). **A "we'll be careful" answer remains inadmissible** - the defect produces a confidently wrong answer, and carefulness does not detect those. This review must confirm M-1 is fixed upstream **or** that `cv.statechart` has a working out-of-band discriminator, not merely a plan for one.

4. **Three fixes genuinely landed, and the review should credit them.** `#43` (one asyncio task per invoked child - `children + 1`, `onDone` 0.96 ms median, clean teardown, leak-free over 1 000 cycles), `#79` (provenance-based system events, which retires CV-C15's case-insensitivity requirement outright), and `#80` (`ErrorEvent`, which gives us `isinstance(event, ErrorEvent)` / `event.error`). Suite 3 242/13/0 at 90% coverage, no gate/suite/bench/probe regression. **Revise any capacity planning that used `2 x children` per actor.**

5. **Constraint delta to apply before adopting anything.** Retire CV-C15's case-insensitivity clause and re-scope the rule to the six `ENGINE_EVENT_SHAPES` prefixes (`E50-T05` must be re-specified). Withdraw CV-C06's `deferred_count` clause as unsound. Add **CV-C19** (never construct `Event(system=True)`; never trust library provenance as a routing or trust boundary; CV-LINT-XS13), **CV-C20** (`cv.statechart.persistence` quiesces before snapshotting and reconciles every `pending_invocations()` entry on restore), **CV-C21** (`onError` branches on `isinstance(event, ErrorEvent)` and reads `event.error`; CV-LINT-XS14), **CV-C22** (no global `-W error::DeprecationWarning` while the library trips its own). The six-key machine-config block is **still unchanged** - no library default has moved across two verification passes.

6. **The pin is a commit, and it records what was tested, not what is endorsed.** Evaluate `== 0.8.1` once tagged; until then commit `3c527b0d04c0d2d0ebb565af7e9e905f7178f620` with sha256. Confirm upstream has bumped `__version__` (it still has not, two passes running).

7. **Performance posture unchanged.** BENCH-1 with `rollback` armed measures ~**2.03x** (1.56-2.37 over three runs) against the >=3.0x bar - noisy, statistically consistent with the 2.43x/~2.46x history, and no source touched this path. CV-C13 (dedicated event loop / process) is what buys it back.

8. **Upstream debt, drafted and unfiled.** Sixteen verification comments (three of them `comment+reopen`: `#31`, `#77`, `#79`), sixteen new-issue bodies, a meta-issue replacement and a `manifest.json` posting plan, all in `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-3c527b0/`. Filing is tracked on the `E50-C*` chores; this review should confirm it has happened rather than assume it.

**Note for whoever runs this review:** "keep the shim permanently" remains a first-class outcome. Nothing in this window makes it more likely - the library is improving and the fixes are real - but the two snapshot findings are a reminder that the adopting cost includes tracking interactions between features that were each individually correct.

title: Fold the adoption decision back into ADR-0016, the catalogue, the architecture docs and the rules
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: shim/dual-runtime/gate/decision work withdrawn by the owner decision for full adoption (ADR-0016 Accepted; 29-statechart-adoption-plan §4a)**

## Context
A decision that is taken and not written down where people read is a decision that gets re-litigated in six months by someone who was not in the room. `E50-X01` produces an outcome; this ticket makes the document set consistent with it.

The surface is wider than it first appears, because ADR-0016's premise is referenced deliberately across the plan: `28-statechart-catalogue.md` section 0 names the executor per period; `20-architecture.md` carries the statechart-contract note and the hot-path exclusion; `24-internal-schemas.md` points every lifecycle section at its contract; `CONSTITUTION.md` and `AGENTS.md` carry the binding rules; `30-release-roadmap.md` carries E50 and its soft dependencies. Each of those either changes or is confirmed unchanged, and "confirmed unchanged" is a real outcome worth recording.

The **contract** half of ADR-0016 is unaffected by any outcome. That is the point of having split it: the twenty contracts stay binding whether the executor is the shim, the library, or both.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **ADR-0016**: the dated amendment from `E50-X01` merged; status updated from *Proposed (gated)* to *decided* if the gate resolved either way, or the next review date stated if deferred. Never an in-place edit of the original outcome (`27-adrs/README.md` rule 3).
- **`27-adrs/README.md`** and **`20-architecture.md` section 16**: the ADR index status row updated in the same PR, as the ADR rules require.
- **`28-statechart-catalogue.md` section 0 and section 23.3**: the executor table and the runtime-swap text updated to reflect reality. Regenerated from the registry, never hand-edited.
- **`20-architecture.md`**: the statechart-contract note and the hot-path exclusion confirmed or adjusted; the degraded-mode matrix entry and the `cv_machine_*` metrics reviewed against what actually shipped.
- **`24-internal-schemas.md`**: the "Statechart contract: see 28 section Bn" pointers verified against the final section numbering.
- **`CONSTITUTION.md` and `AGENTS.md`**: the statechart rules updated if the runtime language changed; the hot-path prohibition and the conformance requirement are **not** weakened under any outcome.
- **`30-release-roadmap.md`**: E50's register row and the section 11 soft dependencies reconciled with actuals; any follow-on migration epic added if the outcome was *adopt*.
- **`32-risk-register.md`**: the statechart-adoption risk entry updated - closed, re-scoped, or re-pointed at the shim's key-person risk.
- **A short decision note** in `docs/research/xstate/20-adoption-gate.md` so the research set ends with its own conclusion rather than trailing off.

## Out of scope
- The migration itself, if *adopt* was chosen - that is a follow-on epic.
- Re-opening the contract half of ADR-0016.
- Any change to the twenty contracts. If the outcome were to require one, that is a contract change through `E50-S01`/`S02`'s process with the `machine_hash` gate, not a documentation edit.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The decision is discoverable from every entry point
  Given the recorded outcome
  Then ADR-0016, 27-adrs/README.md, 20-architecture.md section 16, 28 section 0, CONSTITUTION.md,
   AGENTS.md and 30-release-roadmap.md all state the same thing

Scenario: The original decision text is preserved
  Given ADR-0016's outcome section
  Then it is unchanged and the new position appears as a dated amendment below it

Scenario: The binding rules are not weakened
  Given any outcome including keep-the-shim-permanently
  Then CONSTITUTION.md and AGENTS.md still require lifecycles to conform to their JSON contract
  And still forbid hot paths from being statecharts

Scenario: The catalogue is regenerated, not edited
  When section 0's executor table changes
  Then it is produced by the renderer and make gen leaves no diff

Scenario: The research set ends with its conclusion
  Then 20-adoption-gate.md records the decision, its date and its evidence
```

## Technical notes / design
The whole change lands in **one PR** so the document set is never internally inconsistent, even briefly. The ADR rules already require the index row and the ADR to move together; this extends the same discipline across the rest of the set.

Section-number pointers into `24` are verified mechanically rather than by reading, because a stale cross-reference in a single-source-of-truth regime is worse than no cross-reference - it sends a reader confidently to the wrong place.

## Test plan
A link and anchor check across the edited documents asserting every cross-reference resolves. `make gen && git diff --exit-code` proves the catalogue was regenerated rather than hand-edited. A consistency check asserting the ADR status string is identical in ADR-0016, `27-adrs/README.md` and `20-architecture.md` section 16.

## Security notes
If the outcome was *adopt*, this PR is where the dependency pin, the sha256 and the vendored-copy policy become documented policy rather than a plan in a spike report. Security reviews the documented supply-chain position. Under every outcome, MUSTNOT-05 (statecharts never enforce safety decisions) and C-2.6 (the native-SL invariant) must read identically to before - a documentation pass is a classic way for a safety rule to get softened by accident.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. Where statechart state reaches the admin health panel (E42) it must be conveyed as text, never colour alone (`docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`).

## Performance notes
No runtime change. Budget text in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` is confirmed against the measured values from `E50-T06` rather than left at their planned figures.

## Observability
If the executor changed, the fleet dashboard and the `cv_statechart_runtime` panel are updated to match, so the documentation and the dashboard agree.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Single PR updating ADR-0016 (amendment), both ADR indexes, `28` section 0/23.3 (regenerated), `20`, `24` pointers, `CONSTITUTION.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `30` and `32`.
- [ ] Link/anchor check green; `make gen` leaves no diff; ADR status string identical in all three places.
- [ ] Binding rules verified unweakened by explicit diff review.
- [ ] `20-adoption-gate.md` records the decision, date and evidence.
- [ ] Architect code-owner review; Security review if the outcome was adopt.

## Dependencies
- **E50-X01** - the decision being recorded.
- **E50-T01** - the catalogue renderer.
- **E01** - the constitution amendment process governs the `CONSTITUTION.md` edit.

## Branch
`docs/e50-fold-adoption-decision`

## References
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md
- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md
- docs/research/xstate/10-fit-analysis.md Part A, Part B, Part C
- docs/research/xstate/11-adversarial-review.md section 3, section 5
- docs/research/xstate/12-challenge-register.md
- docs/plan/27-adrs/README.md (amendment rules)
- CONSTITUTION.md section 16 (amendment process, single-source registry)
- docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md sections 3, 11; docs/plan/32-risk-register.md

title: Track upstream [VERIFIED FIXED main@3c527b0]: `send(wait=True)` hangs forever on a reused `Event` instance
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context
> **Round-7 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `221ce7c`).** **Still VERIFIED FIXED at `221ce7c`** for cases A/B/C. **Case D is NOT fixed** - `stop()` never resolves duplicate-`Event`-instance receipts with `InterpreterStoppedError` (160/160 across 20 trials resolved as ordinary success), and the shipped regression test pins only a weaker `ok == applied` invariant that passes while the defect is live. Reopened upstream as #175.
> Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md`, `docs/research/xstate/43-r7-findings-register.md`.

**Severity: High. Register id: N-1. Found by the 0.8.0 re-evaluation, not present in the 0.7.0 register.**

`Interpreter.send(event_obj, wait=True)` keys its pending-receipt map on `id(event_obj)`. Two concurrent sends passing the **same `Event` instance** collide on that key: the second `_make_receipt` overwrites the first future, which is then never resolved and never failed. The awaiting coroutine hangs forever - no exception, no timeout, no log line, and `stop()` does not resolve it because the future is no longer in `_receipts`.

This is a silent hang inside the API 0.8.0 added specifically to make `send` answerable, in the release whose stated theme is eliminating silent failure. That is why it is High rather than Medium.

**Measured evidence.** `docs/research/xstate/issues/new-0.8.0/repro/N-01_send-wait-receipt-id-collision.py`, exit 1 on 0.8.0:

```
OBSERVED control_fresh_2way              : resolved
OBSERVED control_fresh_200way            : resolved
OBSERVED control_same_object_sequential  : resolved
OBSERVED subject_same_object_concurrent  : HUNG
```

The 200-way fresh-object control rules out `id()` recycling of dead objects; the sequential control rules out "an `Event` is single-use by design". It is specifically caller-side identity reuse, and reusing a pre-built `Event` as a template is a natural pattern since `send()` accepts `Event` instances in every documented overload.

**Affected contracts.** Every machine that gates a decision on a receipt - B18 `kill_switch`, B20 `risk_lockout`, B17 `live_gate`, and the order path's synchronous checks (constraint CV-C06).

**Current CandleViewer mitigation.** Constraint CV-C06 plus lint rule CV-LINT-XS9: every `send(..., wait=True)` call site must pass a literal event type or a freshly-constructed `Event`, never a name bound outside the call. This is a convention backed by an AST check - adequate, but it is exactly the "fails silently if forgotten" shape this Epic exists to remove.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **File the upstream issue** from the prepared draft at `docs/research/xstate/issues/new-0.8.0/N-01-send-wait-receipt-id-collision.md`, which already carries the evidence, the minimal repro, the controls and the proposed fix. Also post the follow-up comment drafted at `issues/followups-0.8.0/LC-42.md` on the parent issue #39.
- **Record the issue number** in `12-challenge-register.md` against the LC-42 row and in `17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md` section 7.3.
- **Keep the repro in the gate**: it already lives under `issues/new-0.8.0/repro/` with the standard exit-1-while-present convention; wire it into `run_gate.py`'s primary set so `E50-T04` executes it per release.
- **Proposed fix to carry into the issue**: replace the identity key with a monotonic per-send token carried on the queued envelope rather than on the caller's object, so caller-side reuse is irrelevant by construction.
- **Verify CV-LINT-XS9 covers it** in the interim.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fix upstream (library repo work).
- Removing CV-C06 / CV-LINT-XS9, which stay until the gate shows the repro passing against a released version.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The issue is filed with evidence and a repro
  Given this Chore is In Progress
  Then an upstream issue exists carrying the controls, the repro and the proposed fix
  And its number is recorded in 12-challenge-register.md against LC-42

Scenario: The repro runs in the gate on every release
  Given a new upstream release
  When the scheduled gate job runs
  Then N-01's repro is executed and its result appears in the gate report

Scenario: The Chore closes on evidence, not on assertion
  Given the upstream issue is marked closed
  Then this Chore closes only if N-01's repro exits 0 in a gate report
  And CV-LINT-XS9 may only be relaxed after that report exists
```

## Technical notes / design
The repro is four lines at its core and runs against a clean install with no CandleViewer dependency, so it is directly actionable upstream. Keep the three controls in the filed version - without them the report invites the "you are holding it wrong" response, and the 200-way control is what proves this is not `id()` recycling.

## Test plan
The repro is the test and is a negative test today: it must fail against 0.8.0, proving it exercises the defect. `E50-T04` runs it per release. Add `tests/xstate_contract/test_send_receipt_fresh_event_only.py` asserting our own call sites comply with CV-C06.

## Security notes
The issue carries reproduction code and measured behaviour only - no account identifiers, no strategy detail, no credentials, no live or demo account data (C-2.7).

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface.

## Performance notes
No CandleViewer runtime impact; this Chore ships no product code.

## Observability
Visible through `cv_ci_xstate_gate_items_open{severity}` and the per-version gate reports.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Upstream issue filed from the prepared draft; number recorded in the register.
- [ ] Follow-up comment posted on #39.
- [ ] Repro wired into `run_gate.py`'s primary check set.
- [ ] CV-LINT-XS9 confirmed to catch the pattern in our own code.
- [ ] Closed only when a gate report shows the repro passing against a released version.
- [ ] Architect review.

## Dependencies
- **E50-T04** - the scheduled gate job that verifies closure.
- Feeds **E50-X01**.

## Branch
`chore/e50-c13-upstream-n01-send-wait-receipt`

## References
- docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md (section 5, new defects; section 6, constraints)
- docs/research/xstate/15-reeval-0.8.0-adversarial.md
- docs/research/xstate/16-reeval-0.8.0-diff-review.md
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md (Amendment 1)

**Status: VERIFIED FIXED. This Chore may close once a gate report exists against a tagged release.**

`verify-main-5327ba6/N-1_send-wait-receipt-collision.py` and the original `new-0.8.0/repro/N-01_*.py` both exit 0. All acceptance criteria pass:
