title: Track upstream [N-3 REOPENED on main@3c527b0]: the sync macrostep budget no longer loses events, but overflow is still silent
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context
**Severity: High (N-2) and Medium (N-3). Found by the 0.8.0 re-evaluation, not present in the 0.7.0 register.**

Two independent defects in `SyncInterpreter`, filed together because they share an owner and a decision: both are reasons **MUSTNOT-06 (never use `SyncInterpreter`) is reinforced rather than relaxed** by 0.8.0.

**N-2 (High) - timers unreachable by `tick()` in a running loop.** `RealClock.set_timeout` branches on the *caller's* context, not on which engine owns the clock. A `SyncInterpreter` constructed inside a running asyncio loop parks its `after` deadlines on `loop.call_later`, leaving `clock._heap` empty; `tick()` and the `send()` pump drain only the heap, so `tick()` cannot deliver a genuinely-due deadline. Measured, same machine, `after: {40: "b"}`:

| context | `clock.pending` | state after `tick()` |
|---|---|---|
| off-loop thread (control) | 1 | `{'sy.b'}` |
| inside a running loop | 0 | `{'sy.a'}` |

This is #50's defect displaced rather than resolved: the thread-per-timer is genuinely gone (25 machines -> +0 threads), but the deadline now lands somewhere the sync engine's own API cannot reach. It bites any async app keeping one sync machine for a hot path, and **any async test that constructs a sync machine** - so a suite can be green while production differs.

**N-3 (Medium) - macrostep budget still discards legitimate external events.** `_process_event_queue` increments its runaway counter per *event* and, past `max_iterations` (1000), calls `self._event_queue.clear()`. The 0.8.0 CHANGELOG claims "the two engines now agree"; they do not - `replay_credit` exempts only replayed deferred events. Measured via `send_events()`:

| batch | sync processed | async processed |
|---|---|---|
| 999 | 999 | 999 |
| 1001 | **1000** | 1001 |
| 1501 | **1000** | 1501 |
| 3000 | **1000** | 3000 |

A silent 501-event drop on the default configuration of a shipped engine.

**Affected contracts.** None directly - MUSTNOT-06 bans `SyncInterpreter` everywhere in CandleViewer, and CV-LINT-XS8 enforces that by AST check. This Chore exists because (a) we owe the fixes upstream as the filer of the original issues, and (b) N-2 and N-3 are the evidence that MUSTNOT-06 must not be quietly relaxed now that the thread-per-timer defect is fixed.

**Current CandleViewer mitigation.** MUSTNOT-06 + CV-C03 + CV-LINT-XS8: the async `Interpreter` only, in every process. Cost to us: none.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **File two upstream issues** from the prepared drafts: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-02-sync-timer-unreachable-in-loop.md` and `issues/new-0.8.0/N-03-sync-macrostep-budget-clears-queue.md`, each with its runnable repro under `issues/new-0.8.0/repro/`.
- **Post the follow-up comment** drafted at `issues/followups-0.8.0/LC-38.md` on issue #50, since N-2 is the same class that issue addressed.
- **Ask for the CHANGELOG correction** on the "the two engines now agree" line, which is inaccurate as written (part of the N-3 filing).
- **Record the issue numbers** in `12-challenge-register.md` against LC-38 and in `17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md` section 7.3.
- **Wire both repros into `run_gate.py`'s primary set** so `E50-T04` runs them per release.
- **Proposed fixes to carry into the issues**: for N-2, bind the clock lane at attachment time from the `owner` the clock already receives, or reject constructing a `SyncInterpreter` with a `RealClock` inside a running loop (this release's own `WrongThreadError` precedent). For N-3, port the async engine's `_raise_depth` concept - count microstep depth within a macrostep, not events across a drain - and raise on overflow rather than clearing.
- **Record explicitly in the register that MUSTNOT-06 is reinforced**, so a future reader does not read "thread-per-timer fixed" as "sync engine now safe".

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fixes upstream.
- Any relaxation of MUSTNOT-06. These defects are the argument against it.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Both issues are filed with evidence and repros
  Given this Chore is In Progress
  Then two upstream issues exist, each with its controls, repro and proposed fix
  And their numbers are recorded in 12-challenge-register.md against LC-38

Scenario: Both repros run in the gate on every release
  Given a new upstream release
  When the scheduled gate job runs
  Then N-02 and N-03 are executed and their results appear in the gate report

Scenario: MUSTNOT-06 survives the fixes
  Given both defects are fixed upstream
  Then MUSTNOT-06 is re-reviewed on evidence at E50-X01, not relaxed automatically
```

## Technical notes / design
Both repros carry controls that isolate the engine: N-2 runs the identical machine on an off-loop thread in the same process and the same run (it fires correctly), and N-3 runs the identical batch through the async engine (all 1501 processed). Without those controls neither report is credible, because both failures look like machine-wide timing artefacts.

N-3's boundary was swept at 999 / 1001 / 1501 / 3000 to confirm `max_iterations = 1000` as the mechanism rather than inferring it from source.

## Test plan
Both repros are negative tests today and must fail against 0.8.0. `E50-T04` runs them per release. On our side the only test needed is `tests/xstate_contract/test_no_sync_interpreter.py` - an AST check that `SyncInterpreter` appears nowhere in `src/`.

## Security notes
Reproduction code and measured behaviour only - no account identifiers, no strategy detail, no credentials, no live or demo account data (C-2.7).

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface.

## Performance notes
No CandleViewer runtime impact; this Chore ships no product code and we do not use the affected engine.

## Observability
Visible through `cv_ci_xstate_gate_items_open{severity}` and the per-version gate reports.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both upstream issues filed from the prepared drafts; numbers recorded in the register.
- [ ] Follow-up comment posted on #50; CHANGELOG correction requested.
- [ ] Both repros wired into `run_gate.py`'s primary check set.
- [ ] MUSTNOT-06's reinforcement recorded in the register and in ADR-0016 Amendment 1.
- [ ] Closed only when a gate report shows both repros passing against a released version.
- [ ] Architect review.

## Dependencies
- **E50-T04** - the scheduled gate job that verifies closure.
- Feeds **E50-X01**.

## Branch
`chore/e50-c14-upstream-n02-n03-sync-engine`

## References
- docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md (section 5, new defects; section 6, constraints)
- docs/research/xstate/15-reeval-0.8.0-adversarial.md
- docs/research/xstate/16-reeval-0.8.0-diff-review.md
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md (Amendment 1)
- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md section 1.3b

## Verification on `main` @ `5327ba6` (2026-09-18)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it. Source: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 2.

**Status: N-2 VERIFIED FIXED; N-3 PARTIAL. Stays open against N-3's residual and three new defects in the same fix.**

**N-2 - FIXED.** `verify-main-5327ba6/N-2_sync-timer-clock-lane.py` exits 0. `RealClock.set_timeout` now takes an explicit `sync=` lane selector and `BaseInterpreter._clock_sync_lane` decides the lane at construction from the **owning engine**, not from ambient loop state. A `SyncInterpreter` built inside `asyncio.run(...)` shows `clock.pending == 1` for an armed `after`, does not advance on a bare `await asyncio.sleep()`, and `tick()` delivers the elapsed deadline on the caller's thread. Off-loop behaviour is unchanged (25 sync machines, 0 extra threads). Upstream `#76` and `#50` are **closable**.

**N-3 - PARTIAL.** The data-loss defect is genuinely fixed: `send_events(["T"]*1501)` and `*5000` are processed in full with `queue_depth == 0` afterwards, 3,000 independent one-deep raises in one batch are all delivered, sync and async produce byte-identical action traces for a 2,000-event batch, and named parity tests exist in `tests/test_core_algorithm.py`. **But overflow is still silent** - `send()` returns normally, `status` stays `"running"`, and the only signal is a log line. The issue's acceptance criteria asked for the guard to trip *by raising*; the shipped fix stopped the clearing but did not add the raising. `#77` stays open, re-scoped.

**Three new defects landed in this fix's own code path**, all drafted in `issues/new-main/`:

- **F-1 (High)** - the `tripped` flag is scoped to the drain rather than the chain, so one self-feeding event starves every later unrelated event's one-deep `raise` in the same `send_events()` batch. The async engine delivers all of them: this is the engine-parity divergence `#77` claims to have closed, in the opposite direction.
- **F-6 (Medium)** - a `done.invoke` from a sync service is classed as self-generated, so after a trip a legitimate completion is dropped and the machine parks permanently in the invoking state. A silent hang.
- **M-2 (Medium)** - on the async engine the budget does not bound an action-side `send()` at all, so the parity claim covers the `raise` built-in only.

**CV-C03 (async `Interpreter` only) stands, with its rationale shifted**: the sync defects that originally motivated it are fixed; it now stands on F-1 / F-6 and the remaining sync surface. It does **not** protect us from M-2, which is an async hole - hence new constraint **CV-C16** (no action may call `send()` on its own interpreter; use the `raise` built-in), enforced by CV-LINT-XS11, plus **CV-C17** for the silent chain-depth cut.

## Verification on `main` @ `3c527b0` (2026-09-18, PR #83 merged)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it, two passes running. Source: `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 3.

**Status: unchanged - `#77` REOPENED.** Nothing in PR #83 touches the `maxIterations` path. The data-loss defect stays fixed; **overflow is still silent** (`send()` returns normally, `status` stays `"running"`, `last_transition_ok` stays `True`, only a log line), and the acceptance criteria asked for a raise. Comment + reopen drafted at `issues/post-3c527b0/77.md`, re-scoped to raise-on-overflow.

All three defects in the fix's own code path reproduce identically on `3c527b0` and are now filed as new issues 5 (F-1, High - the `tripped` flag is scoped to the drain, not the chain; `INNER handled: 0 of 5`), 7 (M-2, Medium) and 11 (F-6, Medium) in `issues/post-3c527b0/`. F-9 rides along on `#77`.

**CV-C03, CV-C16 and CV-C17 all stand unchanged.**

title: Track upstream [N-4 VERIFIED FIXED; #79 REOPENED on main@3c527b0] [VERIFIED FIXED main@cec108b]: `send_threadsafe()` strict bypass and `error.*`/`done.*` namespace visibility
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context
> **Round-6 re-verification (2026-09-20, `main` @ `cec108b`).** #150 charges `send_threadsafe` self-sends to `maxIterations` on both the flag and the contextvars-inherited route. Residuals: R6-05 (Medium, loop-side RAISE refusals are silent → E50-T18) and R6-12 (Medium, the in-flight counter leaks). Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §1/§5.

**Severity: Medium (N-4) and Medium (N-8). Found by the 0.8.0 re-evaluation, not present in the 0.7.0 register.**

Two silent-drop defects in the validation surface 0.8.0 added, filed together because both defeat the same guardrail from different directions.

**N-4 - `send_threadsafe()` bypasses `strict` and `event_schemas`.** `_check_strict` is called from `Interpreter.send`, `SyncInterpreter.send` and the `raise` built-in, but **not** from `send_threadsafe()`, which goes `_prepare_event` -> `_enqueue` directly. Verified on a `strict: True` machine with a registered schema:

```
OBSERVED send_typo               : UnknownEventError
OBSERVED send_bad_payload        : InvalidEventPayloadError
OBSERVED threadsafe_typo         : accepted      <- silently dropped at dispatch
OBSERVED threadsafe_bad_payload  : accepted      <- AND the machine transitioned to st.b
```

The payload case is the worse of the two: an event the registered schema rejects drives a real transition. This matters because 0.8.0 made `send_threadsafe()` the *recommended* - and after the `run_coroutine_threadsafe` break (N-6), effectively the *only* - cross-thread API. The path a multi-threaded app is required to take is the one without the guardrail.

**N-8 - `error.*` / `done.*` user event names are invisible.** `_matching_descriptors` exempts the prefixes `("done.", "error.", "after.", "xstate.", "___xstate")` from wildcard and partial matching by **prefix-testing the name string**, not by checking provenance. That list is now load-bearing in three places (the matcher, the `onUnhandled` policy, `_check_strict`). Verified: a user-sent `error.myapp.validation` does **not** match `on: {"*": ...}`, and an unhandled `done.review` does **not** trip `onUnhandled: "error"` - while the `my.namespaced` control matches fine and the `UNKNOWN_PLAIN` control trips correctly. For any domain naming events `done.review` / `error.validation` this is a silent-drop class, reachable purely by choosing an unlucky name.

**Affected contracts.** N-4: any machine fed from a foreign thread - B13 `ws_conn`, B14 `book`, B11 `recording`. N-8: potentially all twenty, since `done.*`/`error.*` are idiomatic names we would otherwise have used.

**Current CandleViewer mitigation.** N-4: constraint CV-C14 - all cross-thread sends go through `cv.statechart.gateway`, which performs the `strict`/`event_schemas` check itself before delegating, since the library's own path does not. N-8: constraint CV-C15 - no CandleViewer event may be named `error.*` or `done.*`, enforced by the event-name gate (`E50-T05`).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **File two upstream issues** from the prepared drafts: `issues/new-0.8.0/N-04-send-threadsafe-bypasses-strict.md` and `issues/new-0.8.0/N-08-error-done-namespace-invisible.md`, each with its runnable repro.
- **Post the follow-up comments** drafted at `issues/followups-0.8.0/LC-34.md` (on #51, strict mode) and `issues/followups-0.8.0/LC-03.md` (on #28, which asks for the namespace exemption to be documented).
- **Record the issue numbers** in `12-challenge-register.md` against LC-34 and in `17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md` section 7.3.
- **Wire both repros into `run_gate.py`'s primary set**.
- **Proposed fixes to carry into the issues**: for N-4, route `send_threadsafe()` through the same prepare-and-validate helper `send()` uses, so the two cannot drift again - one validation path, two delivery strategies, matching #60's own lesson. For N-8, tag engine-synthesised events at mint time and test that flag instead of prefix-matching the name, keeping the prefix list only as a fallback for 0.7.x snapshots; plus a `create_machine()` warning when a machine declares an `on:` key in a reserved namespace.
- **Confirm `E50-T05`'s event-name gate rejects reserved namespaces** before any catalogue machine is authored against the library.

## Out of scope
- Implementing the fixes upstream.
- Removing CV-C14's gateway wrapper or CV-C15's name ban, both of which stay until a gate report shows the repros passing.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Both issues are filed with evidence and repros
  Given this Chore is In Progress
  Then two upstream issues exist, each with its controls, repro and proposed fix
  And their numbers are recorded in 12-challenge-register.md against LC-34

Scenario: Our own guardrails are in place regardless of upstream
  Given the gateway wrapper and the event-name gate
  Then a cross-thread send of an unknown event is rejected by our code
  And CI fails if any machine declares or any gateway sends an event named error.* or done.*

Scenario: The Chore closes on evidence
  Given the upstream issues are marked closed
  Then this Chore closes only if N-04's and N-08's repros exit 0 in a gate report
```

## Technical notes / design
Both repros carry the controls that make them credible: N-4 shows the ordinary `send()` path correctly raising both `UnknownEventError` and `InvalidEventPayloadError` on the same machine in the same run, so strict mode and the schema are provably armed; N-8 shows `PLAIN` and `my.namespaced` matching `"*"` and `UNKNOWN_PLAIN` tripping `onUnhandled: "error"`, so the mechanism works and only the reserved prefixes are swallowed.

N-8 is arguably a documentation issue rather than a bug, and the draft says so - but "documented silent drop" is still a silent drop, so the draft asks for provenance-tagging first and documentation only as the fallback.

## Test plan
Both repros are negative tests today and must fail against 0.8.0. `E50-T04` runs them per release. On our side: `tests/xstate_contract/test_threadsafe_send_validates_event_name.py` (CV-C14) and an extension to `E50-T05`'s event-name gate covering the reserved namespaces (CV-C15).

## Security notes
Reproduction code and measured behaviour only - no account identifiers, no strategy detail, no credentials, no live or demo account data (C-2.7). N-4 is worth flagging to DevSecOps in passing: an unvalidated event path into a machine that gates order submission is a defence-in-depth concern, which is why CV-C14 wraps rather than trusts.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface.

## Performance notes
The CV-C14 gateway wrapper adds one dict lookup and one schema call per cross-thread send. Negligible against the ~29 us per-event floor, and cross-thread sends are not on the order hot path.

## Observability
Visible through `cv_ci_xstate_gate_items_open{severity}` and the per-version gate reports. The gateway wrapper exports `cv_machine_rejected_events_total{kind,reason}`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Both upstream issues filed from the prepared drafts; numbers recorded in the register.
- [ ] Follow-up comments posted on #51 and #28.
- [ ] Both repros wired into `run_gate.py`'s primary check set.
- [ ] CV-C14 gateway wrapper and CV-C15 name ban implemented and tested.
- [ ] Closed only when a gate report shows both repros passing against a released version.
- [ ] Architect review; DevSecOps sighted on N-4.

## Dependencies
- **E50-T04** - the scheduled gate job that verifies closure.
- **E50-T05** - the event-name coverage gate, extended for CV-C15.
- Feeds **E50-X01**.

## Branch
`chore/e50-c15-upstream-n04-n08-validation-bypass`

## References
- docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md (section 5, new defects; section 6, constraints)
- docs/research/xstate/15-reeval-0.8.0-adversarial.md
- docs/research/xstate/16-reeval-0.8.0-diff-review.md
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md (Amendment 1)
- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md section 1.3b

## Verification on `main` @ `5327ba6` (2026-09-18)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it. Source: `docs/research/xstate/22-verify-main-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 2.

**Status: N-4 VERIFIED FIXED; N-8 PARTIAL and deferred upstream to 0.9. Stays open against N-8.**

**N-4 - FIXED.** `verify-main-5327ba6/N-4_send-threadsafe-strict.py` exits 0; all five acceptance criteria pass. `send_threadsafe()` now calls `_check_strict` before scheduling the enqueue, raising `UnknownEventError` (with a difflib "Did you mean...?" suggestion) or `InvalidEventPayloadError` **on the calling thread**, with nothing queued or processed - verified under loop saturation and 10-thread contention. The schema guardrail applies even when `strict` is unset. All three named tests are present in `tests/test_strict.py` (renamed from `test_strict_mode.py`). Additionally, static `raise` targets are now validated at `create_machine()` time on `strict` machines, with a Did-you-mean suggestion.

**Consequence for us: CV-C14's gateway-validation clause RETIRES.** Delete the duplicate `strict` / `event_schemas` check from `cv.statechart.gateway`. **The `run_coroutine_threadsafe` ban is unaffected and stands** - CV-C14 becomes a ban-only rule. Upstream `#78` and `#51` are **closable**.

**N-8 - PARTIAL, and the real fix is explicitly deferred to 0.9.** What shipped: `events.SYSTEM_EVENT_PREFIXES` as a documented importable constant, a build-time `UserWarning` for reserved-namespace `on` keys the engine will never synthesise (confirmed not to false-positive on engine-shaped keys), and documentation across five guide pages. What did **not** ship: the runtime behaviour. A user event named `done.review` or `error.myapp.validation` is still invisible to `on: {"*": ...}`, still exempt from `onUnhandled: "error"`, and still accepted silently by `strict`. The CHANGELOG defers the fix honestly ("provenance-tagged system events... are planned for 0.9").

**CV-C15 therefore STANDS, and `E50-T05`'s event-name gate must run and must be CASE-INSENSITIVE** - the library's own warning is case-sensitive (`DONE.review` slips through), does not cover `send()`, and only inspects `on` keys (M-5, riding along on `#79`). One new CI risk to note: because `create_machine()` now warns on these keys, a `-W error` setup will break machines that previously worked with the silent-drop bug.

## Verification on `main` @ `3c527b0` (2026-09-18, PR #83 merged)

> Build identified by **commit**; `__version__` still reports `0.8.0` on it, two passes running. Source: `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 3.

**Status: the reported defect is FIXED; `#79` is REOPENED for a different criterion, and CV-C15 is RE-SCOPED.**

`#79`'s runtime half landed in PR #83, and landed well. System status is now decided by **provenance** (`Event.system`, `is_system_event()`, `ENGINE_EVENT_TYPES`), not by name. A user-sent `done.review` or `error.validation` is matched by `"*"` and by `"done.*"`, trips `onUnhandled: "error"`, and is rejected by `strict` - **case variants included**, because neither spelling is exempt any longer. The build-time reserved-namespace warning is correctly withdrawn, taking the `-W error` CI risk this Chore flagged with it.

**CV-C15's case-insensitivity clause therefore RETIRES**, and the constraint is **re-scoped**: no CandleViewer event may be named with any prefix in `ENGINE_EVENT_SHAPES` - `done.invoke.`, `done.state.`, `error.platform.`, `after.`, `xstate.`, `___xstate`. Those are the only names `models.is_known_event` still exempts **by name** (G-7), so a typo inside them is still silent under `strict` (`after.party` - not even a well-formed `after.` shape - is accepted undeclared). **`E50-T05` must be re-specified to that list, case-sensitively.**

**`#79` is reopened for acceptance criterion 8**, which is unmet by code in two ways: **G-1** - `Event.system` is a public, user-settable field, so provenance is spoofable from user code (the name rule it replaced was at least hard to hit by accident). **G-2** - provenance is **not persisted**, so a restored engine event becomes user traffic and fails a machine configured `onUnhandled: "error"`; under the old name rule the answer was the same either side of a restore. **G-2 is the one behavioural regression in this window.** G-7, G-10, G-11 and G-12 ride along or are filed separately.

Comment + reopen drafted at `issues/post-3c527b0/79.md`.

title: Order-path receipt gate: a working defer discriminator, or hold (M-1)
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: closed upstream in v0.9.1 (xstate-statemachine==0.9.1, tag 45bb7f3); residuals and future releases go to the E50-C17 liaison chore (29 §4a)**

## Context

This Chore exists because a mitigation we had already written down turned out not to work, and the failure mode it was guarding is one that carefulness cannot catch.

**The defect (M-1, High, still present on `main` @ `3c527b0`).** The two library settings the order path is *mandated* to use together - `onUnhandled: "defer"` (CV-C01) and `send(wait=True)` receipts (CV-C06) - compose into a confident false negative. When `defer` parks an event, the run loop still resolves that event's receipt at the end of the macrostep by diffing configuration and context. Nothing changed, because the event was never processed, so the receipt reports `changed=False, error=None`.

That is **byte-identical to "the machine looked at your event and correctly did nothing"**, for an event that is parked and *will* drive its transition on replay - after the caller has already acted on the receipt. A FILL arriving one microstep early (the precise scenario `defer` was adopted to fix) returns a receipt saying the fill did not land. A caller that retries, or reports "not filled" and unwinds, does so against a machine that is about to fill.

Not a hang, not data loss: a gate that says *no* about an event that is about to say *yes*.

**Why this is a new ticket rather than a line in `E50-C05`.** The verdict at `5327ba6` specified a mitigation - *treat `changed=False, error=None` as inconclusive unless `interpreter.deferred_count` is `0` at the same instant* - and recorded it as CV-C06's new clause, to be locked by `test_receipt_is_inconclusive_when_deferred`. **Re-testing on `3c527b0` shows it does not work.** At the caller's `await` point `deferred_count` reads **`0`** for the deferred case *and* for the genuine no-op; the `1` observed in the original probe is read from inside the macrostep, where a caller cannot stand. The test cannot be written as specified, and had we not re-tested, it would have shipped into `cv.statechart` and `tests/xstate_contract/` as a mitigation that reads the wrong value and always passes.

`Receipt` on this commit is still `('state_ids', 'changed', 'error')`. PR #83 rewrote `_handle_unhandled_event` (for #79) and reworked `interpreter.py` (for #43) without either change reaching the receipt.

## Scope

**Until this Chore closes, the rule is a prohibition, not a mitigation:**

> A `send(wait=True)` receipt reading `changed=False, error=None` is **inadmissible** as a gate on any machine configured `onUnhandled: "defer"` - which is every catalogue machine. **No order-path statechart ships** while that holds.

Three ways out, in order of preference:

1. **Upstream fixes it.** `Receipt` gains a `deferred` flag (or a tri-state `disposition`) set from the `defer` decision `_handle_unhandled_event` has already made, or the receipt resolves on replay so `wait=True` means "wait until this event is actually processed". Filed as new issue 1 in `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-3c527b0/` with a runnable repro and acceptance criteria. **This is the outcome to push for.**
2. **The library exposes a correlatable hook.** An `on_event_deferred(event)` plugin hook carrying enough identity to match a specific send would let `cv.statechart` wrap `send(wait=True)` and return a three-valued result of its own. The library does not currently expose one; ask for it as a fallback in the same issue.
3. **We stop depending on the receipt for this class of decision.** Gate on an explicit acknowledgement event from the machine (an `entry` action on the committed state raising a correlated `ACK`), rather than on the transport-level receipt. More work, no upstream dependency, and arguably the more honest design for an order path.

Whichever lands, the enforcement is the same shape: a single wrapper in `cv.statechart`, one lint rule, one contract test that **fails** if the wrapper is bypassed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **CV-LINT-XS9** (re-purposed from the retired fresh-`Event` rule) rejects any direct `send(..., wait=True)` outside `cv.statechart`'s wrapper.
- [ ] `cv.statechart` exposes a send API whose result distinguishes **three** outcomes - processed-and-changed, processed-and-no-op, deferred-and-pending - and the distinction is proved by a test that would fail under today's library behaviour.
- [ ] `test_receipt_is_inconclusive_when_deferred` is **replaced** with a test that asserts against the mechanism actually chosen. The old name must not survive as a green test against a discriminator that reads `0` in both cases.
- [ ] A negative test pins the trap: a deferred event and a genuinely-handled action-less event are both driven, and the test asserts our API reports them **differently** (the library reports them identically).
- [ ] The choice between routes 1/2/3 is recorded in ADR-0016 with its date and its reason.
- [ ] No order-path machine is added to the registry until this is green - enforced by a registry assertion, not by convention.
- [ ] Architect review.

## Dependencies

- Blocks the order-path families in **E50-S01** (B1-B9).
- Feeds **E50-X01** - the go/no-go review must confirm this is closed, not planned.
- Related: **E50-C05** (the `onUnhandled: "defer"` chore this was split out of), **E50-C13** (the `wait=True` receipt chore, verified fixed for its own defect).

## Branch

`chore/e50-c16-order-path-defer-discriminator`

- docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md (section 4.3 - M-1 stated explicitly; section 5.2 - CV-C06 restated)
- docs/research/xstate/23-verify-3c527b0-findings.md (section 2 - the four-variant deep re-test, incl. the `deferred_count` check)

title: Strip the retired A3 deferral scaffolding from all twenty catalogue contracts, proving trace equivalence
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: done in the corrected JSON (CV-C34 retired) (29 §4a)**

## Context
House rule **A3** required every transient state to carry an explicit deferral handler - `"*": {"actions": ["defer"]}` plus `drain_deferred` on entry, with a `_deferred` list in `context`. It existed because `xstate-statemachine` 0.7.0 silently discarded any event with no handler in the current state (register `LC-03`, a Blocker), and it was the single most invasive workaround in the whole design.

0.8.0 closed `LC-03` with a native, library-owned `onUnhandled: "defer"` policy, verified 9/9 under adversarial probing: replay is at the **head** of the queue in original order, still-unhandled events are re-deferred rather than dropped, the buffer survives snapshot/restore, `DEFER_MAX` overflow evicts the oldest and reports it, and system events are never deferred. ADR-0016 Amendment 1 retires A3 and `28-statechart-catalogue.md` section 1.3b records the mandatory `onUnhandled` policy in its place.

**The scaffolding is still inline in all twenty contracts.** It was left there deliberately rather than stripped mechanically: removing it touches every transient state in a ~6,000-line normative document, and the register's own re-verification protocol is explicit that when a defect closes upstream we must **delete the corresponding mitigation and its workaround test** - carefully, not blindly, because a botched edit to a normative contract is worse than dead code.

With `onUnhandled: "defer"` set, the inline handler never fires (the runtime holds the event before any `"*"` handler is consulted), so the scaffolding is **dead but harmless** today. It is still worth removing: it is ~40 lines of misleading machinery per machine that a reader will reasonably copy into machine twenty-one.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Remove from all twenty contracts** in `28-statechart-catalogue.md`: the `"_deferred": []` context key, every `"*": {"actions": ["defer"]}` handler, and every `drain_deferred` entry action.
- **Prove equivalence, do not assert it.** For each machine, run the conformance harness (`E50-T03`) over its recorded event sequences before and after the edit and assert **identical state/action traces**. A machine whose trace changes is a machine whose scaffolding was load-bearing - stop and investigate rather than accepting the diff.
- **Update the derived tables** (section B*.3 Events and transitions, B*.6 Actions) so they stay consistent with the JSON, which is the normative part.
- **Update the conventions section**: `_deferred` is no longer a reserved context key; the deferral buffer is runtime-owned and observed as `interpreter.deferred_count`.
- **Strike house rule A3 from the table** in section 1.3 rather than leaving it struck-through, once the contracts match.
- **Delete the workaround tests** that asserted the scaffolding's behaviour, and confirm the replacement assertions live in `tests/xstate_contract/` against the library's own buffer.
- **Keep INV-5 per family** ("no delivered `exec_id` is ever unaccounted for") - that invariant is about outcomes and is unaffected by which layer owns the buffer.
- **Confirm the shim honours `onUnhandled: "defer"`** with head-of-queue replay semantics before the scaffolding is removed, since the shim is the runtime until the gate passes. If the shim does not, this ticket blocks on that shim work.

## Out of scope
- Any other change to machine semantics. This is a pure removal with a proof, not a redesign.
- Removing MUST-03/MUST-04's alerting, which is re-expressed against `deferred_count` / `pending_events` rather than deleted.
- The `_fault` key and house rule A1, which are unaffected.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The scaffolding is gone
  Given 28-statechart-catalogue.md after this ticket
  Then no contract contains "_deferred", "drain_deferred", or a "*" defer handler
  And every contract still carries onUnhandled in its mandatory policy block

Scenario: Behaviour is provably unchanged
  Given each machine's recorded event sequences
  When the conformance harness runs the before and after definitions
  Then the state and action traces are identical for every machine
  And any divergence blocks the removal for that machine pending investigation

Scenario: The shim is ready first
  Given the shim is still the runtime
  Then onUnhandled "defer" is honoured by the shim with head-of-queue replay
  And this is asserted by a test before any scaffolding is removed

Scenario: The derived tables stay honest
  Given the JSON is the normative source
  Then the Events, Actions and conventions tables match it after the edit
```

## Technical notes / design
Do this **per machine, one commit each**, not as a single sweep - twenty small reviewable diffs against a normative document, each with its conformance trace attached. A regex sweep across 6,000 lines of JSON embedded in Markdown is exactly how a normative contract acquires a silent error.

Order the work easiest-first (B10 `alert`, B17 `live_gate`, B18 `kill_switch` have the least scaffolding) so the harness workflow is proven on simple machines before touching B1 `order` and B3 `leg`.

Note that the equivalence proof is only meaningful if the recorded sequences actually exercise a deferral - include at least one sequence per machine where an event arrives during a transient/invoking state, or the test proves nothing.

## Test plan
The conformance harness (`E50-T03`) is the test: before/after trace equality per machine, with at least one deferral-exercising sequence each. Plus `tests/xstate_contract/test_deferred_survives_crash_and_drains_at_boot.py` re-pointed at the library's buffer rather than our context key, and a linter assertion that `_deferred` and `drain_deferred` appear nowhere in the catalogue.

## Security notes
No security surface. The deferral buffer's contents are the same events either way; the change is which layer holds them. Note that the runtime buffer is included in snapshots, so the existing snapshot-at-rest protections cover it unchanged.

## Accessibility notes
N/A - no user interface. Where deferral depth reaches the admin health panel (E42) it must be conveyed as text, never colour alone.

## Performance notes
A small improvement: `onUnhandled: "defer"` measures ~-1.7% throughput when nothing is actually deferred (34,936 vs 35,532 ev/s baseline), against the per-event cost of a wildcard handler plus a `drain_deferred` entry action on every transient state. Not the reason to do this, but it is not a regression.

## Observability
`cv_machine_deferred_depth{kind}` is re-pointed from `len(context["_deferred"])` to `interpreter.deferred_count`. The MUST-04 alert (non-empty for longer than 5 s) is unchanged in meaning.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All twenty contracts free of `_deferred`, `drain_deferred` and `"*"` defer handlers.
- [ ] Conformance trace equality proven per machine, with deferral-exercising sequences.
- [ ] Shim confirmed to honour `onUnhandled: "defer"` with head-of-queue replay, asserted by a test.
- [ ] Derived tables and the conventions section updated; A3 struck from section 1.3.
- [ ] Workaround tests deleted; replacements in `tests/xstate_contract/` green.
- [ ] `cv_machine_deferred_depth` re-pointed; MUST-04 alert verified still firing.
- [ ] Architect review (ADR-0016 is architect-owned) and QA sign-off on the equivalence evidence.

## Dependencies
- **E50-T03** - the conformance harness that proves equivalence. **This ticket cannot start without it.**
- **E50-T07** - the shim, which must honour `onUnhandled` first.
- `docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md` Amendment 1 - the decision this implements.

## Branch
`chore/e50-t09-strip-a3-deferral-scaffolding`

## References
- docs/research/xstate/17-reeval-0.8.0-verdict.md (section 5, new defects; section 6, constraints)
- docs/research/xstate/15-reeval-0.8.0-adversarial.md
- docs/research/xstate/16-reeval-0.8.0-diff-review.md
- docs/plan/27-adrs/ADR-0016-statechart-runtime.md (Amendment 1)
- docs/plan/28-statechart-catalogue.md section 1.3b

title: Restore legality check before start() — state_ids ⊆ configuration (CV-C27′) — VERIFIED at 6db65d8, WIDENED to two-sided
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: CV-C27′ assertion folded into E50-T49 (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 9 (2026-09-22) — UPSTREAM GROUND CLOSED; guard retained as defence in depth (CV-C27' / restore legality).** **#186 + #198 CONFIRMED FIXED at `f28719c`.** `configuration`/`state_ids` agreement is now enforced in **both** directions on **both** engines (round 8's R8-08 was that the rule was a single `or`, so emptying either field short-circuited it), and #198 additionally refuses a versioned running blob with either field emptied or dropped. **CV-C27' becomes defence in depth rather than the only two-sided check.** Residual R9-14 (Low): #198 also refuses a `version: 1` running blob with no `configuration` key, which previously restored — a compat narrowing the changelog does not name.

## Context
> **NARROWED, round 6 (2026-09-20).** Upstream #142/#143 now enforce configuration legality on the **read** side using the identical predicate as the write side, so the general obligation this ticket carried (CV-C27) is **retired** — 5 000 mutations produce 0 raw builtins and 0 restored `running`-with-no-leaf machines. One hole remains (R6-16, Low): `configuration` can be emptied alone with `state_ids` intact and still restores live, because the check keys on `state_ids` and never cross-validates the two copies. Scope shrinks to **one assertion**: `set(state_ids) ⊆ set(configuration)` before `start()`, raising `CvRestoreError`. Source: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7.

After `from_snapshot()`: assert non-empty configuration that is a subset of machine states, status in the known set, context is a dict matching the machine schema; raise `CvRestoreError` otherwise. Detects R4-01/R4-02 corruption at restore time.
Source: `docs/research/xstate/29-r4-final-verdict.md` §6 (upstream R4-02), ADR-0016 Amendment 4.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implementation under `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/` (factory / lint / gateway as named)
- Unit tests plus a contract test in `tests/xstate_contract/` that reproduces the upstream defect and proves the guard prevents it
- Lint rule registered in `tools/lint_statecharts.py` where applicable

## Out of scope
Fixing the library itself (tracked upstream in #26).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: guard trips
  Given a machine built via cv.statechart.factory
  When the guarded condition occurs
  Then a Cv*Error is raised and no state change or snapshot is produced

Scenario: normal path unaffected
  Given a quiescent machine used correctly
  Then behaviour matches the library documentation and overhead is < 5 us per call

Scenario: upstream fixed
  Given the pinned library closes R4-02
  When the contract test runs
  Then it flags the guard as removable
```

## Technical notes / design
See constraint text above and the factory design in `docs/research/xstate/26-verify-3c527b0-verdict.md` §4.

## Test plan
Unit + contract test; adapt the repro from `docs/research/xstate/probes/main-5e07ba8-final/`.

N/A (backend).

## Observability

- [ ] Lint rule documented in CONSTITUTION
- [ ] Removal condition recorded in ADR-0016

feat/e50-e50-t12-cv-guard

## References
`29-r4-final-verdict.md` §3, §6; `30-r4-findings-register.md`.


---

## Round-8 update (2026-09-21, `main` @ `6db65d8`, ADR-0016 Amendment 8)

**Chore verified, and the rule is widened.** #185 (null/absent `machine_hash` on a versioned blob is drift) and #186 (`configuration`/`state_ids` must agree) both landed and both verify clean on their filed cases.

**Two clauses are added to our own check, because the library's is narrower than it reads.** (1) **R8-08:** #186's agreement rule is **one-sided** — emptying either field short-circuits it, so an emptied `state_ids` lets a forged `configuration` relocate the machine. Our check asserts agreement in **both** directions and treats an empty field on a `version >= 1` payload as disagreement. (2) **R8-06:** a `version: 0` or absent-`version` blob still skips the drift check entirely (`persistence.py:320-329`, `versioned = bool(version)`). Our envelope always writes `version >= 1` plus a `machine_hash`, and our restore path refuses v0/absent on **our** blobs. Note for the record: we rated R8-06 a security bypass and then refuted ourselves — `structure_hash` is a public unkeyed checksum, not a MAC, so an attacker who can edit the blob needs no downgrade. The residue is lossy transit, not an adversary.

title: Linter: no `always` into an invoked child, no `always` to an ancestor (CV-C35)
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: CV-C35 lint folded into E50-T11 (29 §4a)**

## Context
Upstream **R6-01 (Blocker)**: on the async engine, an event re-entering a compound state whose `always` descends into a child carrying an `invoke` livelocks the run loop once that invoke completes — `await send(wait=True)` never resolves, a core is pegged, and the machine reports `status="running"` with `error is None`. `SyncInterpreter` returns in 0.04 s on the identical config. Unwrappable at runtime (there is nothing observable to watch), so the only mitigation is to make the shape unrepresentable in our catalogue at build time.
Also covers **R6-02 (High)**, the same root cause seen as an unbounded silent invoke cycle.
Source: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7, ADR-0016 Amendment 6.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implementation under `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/` (factory / lint / gateway as named)
- Unit tests plus a contract test in `tests/xstate_contract/` that reproduces the upstream defect and proves the guard prevents it
- Lint rule registered in `tools/lint_statecharts.py` where the constraint is static
- Constraint id recorded in the machine registry so a reviewer can trace the rule to its finding

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `CV-LINT-XS17`: a machine is rejected if any `always` transition targets a state that is, or contains, a state carrying an `invoke`
- [ ] `CV-LINT-XS18`: a machine is rejected if any `always` targets an ancestor of its own source
- [ ] All 20 catalogue contracts pass both rules (or are corrected until they do)
- [ ] Contract test reproduces the upstream livelock on the bare library and shows the lint rejects that JSON before it can be built

title: Gateway: every send_threadsafe future is read; refusals counted and paged (CV-C36) — VERIFIED at 6db65d8, rule RETAINED
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: CV-C36 future-read folded into E50-T15 (29 §4a)**

## Context
Upstream **R6-05 (Medium)**. Our original filing (#157: the inbox bound is bypassed and events are accepted then lost) was **refuted by our own corrected repro** — `_enqueue()` on the loop is authoritative and refuses correctly, max observed depth 0 against a bound of 3. What survives is narrower and still ours to handle: while the loop is busy — the only time backpressure matters — the refusal lands on exactly the future a fire-and-forget producer never reads, and the RAISE branch emits no log and no `on_event_dropped`. Correct load shedding with a **hidden shed rate**.
Source: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7, ADR-0016 Amendment 6.

Scheduling: parked in **Backlog** — every sprint in the current train window is at or over capacity, and this is a non-blocking guard for a Medium-severity upstream defect. Pull it in when the order path resumes (see E50-X01).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implementation under `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/` (factory / lint / gateway as named)
- Unit tests plus a contract test in `tests/xstate_contract/` that reproduces the upstream defect and proves the guard prevents it
- Lint rule registered in `tools/lint_statecharts.py` where the constraint is static
- Constraint id recorded in the machine registry so a reviewer can trace the rule to its finding

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The gateway's cross-thread submit API cannot be called in a way that discards the result (no bare fire-and-forget overload exists)
- [ ] Every refusal increments a `statechart_events_shed_total` counter labelled by machine
- [ ] A sustained shed rate above threshold pages, rather than being visible only in a log
- [ ] Contract test: flood a busy loop and assert shed count equals sends minus enqueued, with zero silent losses
- [ ] `CV-LINT-XS19`: direct `interp.send_threadsafe` outside the gateway is rejected

## Out of scope
- Fixing the upstream defect itself. These are our guards; the upstream work is tracked by the `E50-C*` chores.


---

## Round-8 update (2026-09-21, `main` @ `6db65d8`, ADR-0016 Amendment 8)

**Chore verified.** #157's loop-side RAISE refusal observability holds at this commit: 200 sends with `max_queue_size=1` / RAISE give `refused_futures=199, queue_full_hook_fires=199` — still exactly 1:1.

**CV-C36 is retained on R8-13's ground:** the **call-site** `QueueOverflowError` refusals still fire no `on_event_dropped`, and hook coverage of the overall shed rate measured **0.3 %**. Reading every future remains the only complete accounting we have.

title: RETIRED (round 7): children_ready() barrier — superseded by E50-T20 bounded start()
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: already dead (CV-C37) (29 §4a)**

## Context
> **RETIRED 2026-09-20 (round 7, ADR-0016 Amendment 7). Do not implement.**
> Upstream #171 fixed the race this ticket existed for: `_actors` is populated **the instant `await start()` returns**, verified 20x with an identical trace on both engines, and an immediate `sendTo` no longer drops with `unresolved_target`. **CV-C37 retires.**
>
> It is replaced by its inverse. The same fix introduced **R7-03**: `_await_actor_bringups` (`interpreter.py:561`, `:2586`) gathers the bring-up tasks with **no timeout**, and a bring-up awaits `child.start()` - i.e. arbitrary user entry actions. A child whose async entry action sleeps 30 s makes `await start()` hang for 30 s with `status` reading `"running"` throughout, and no timeout knob exists anywhere in `src/`. The problem is no longer "has the machine come up?" but "will `start()` ever return?". See **E50-T20** (CV-C39).
>
> Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md` §5, §7.

Upstream **R6-11 (Medium)**. `await Interpreter.start()` returns ~13 ms before the initial entry set's `invoke` children are registered and before an initial plain-`def` service completes; `SyncInterpreter.start()` does both before returning, so the engines disagree on what `start()` means. A `sendTo` issued in that window is dropped — not silently (`on_event_dropped(reason='unresolved_target')` fires, which is #133 working), but dropped. Root cause: `interpreter.py:487,496` never calls `_await_inline_services()`.
Source: `docs/research/xstate/39-r6-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7, ADR-0016 Amendment 6.

Scheduling: parked in **Backlog** — every sprint in the current train window is at or over capacity, and this is a non-blocking guard for a Medium-severity upstream defect. Pull it in when the order path resumes (see E50-X01).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Implementation under `services/api/candleviewer/statechart/` (factory / lint / gateway as named)
- Unit tests plus a contract test in `tests/xstate_contract/` that reproduces the upstream defect and proves the guard prevents it
- Lint rule registered in `tools/lint_statecharts.py` where the constraint is static
- Constraint id recorded in the machine registry so a reviewer can trace the rule to its finding

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cv.statechart.factory.start()` does not return a usable handle until every `invoke.id` declared on the initial configuration is present in `interpreter.actors`
- [ ] Bounded wait with an explicit timeout and a typed `CvStartTimeout`, never an unbounded poll
- [ ] Contract test: reproduce the dropped `sendTo` on the bare library, then show zero drops through the factory across 100 starts
- [ ] Retired when upstream `start()` settles the initial macrostep or ships `children_ready()`

## Out of scope
- Fixing the upstream defect itself. These are our guards; the upstream work is tracked by the `E50-C*` chores.

title: Factory: `await start()` is always bounded (CV-C39) — VERIFIED at 6db65d8, and WIDENED by CV-C44
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: bounded start() (CV-C56) folded into E50-T59 (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 9 (2026-09-22) — UPSTREAM GROUND CLOSED; guard retained as defence in depth (CV-C39 / bounded start()).** **#181 + #194 CONFIRMED FIXED at `f28719c`.** `start(children_timeout=)` now bounds each child *individually* and the overrun WARNING fires on **every** overrun — including the non-preemptable plain-`def` lane, which was round 8's entire complaint (R8-03: the shipped test gave the `def` arm `time.sleep(0.05)` against the async arm's `asyncio.sleep(3.0)`, so it could not fail). Verified at n=1 and n=5 on both spellings. **CV-C39 and CV-C44 stay as defence in depth**, not as the only bound — re-grounded, not deleted.

## Context

Replaces the retired `E50-T19`. Upstream **R7-03 (High)**: `_await_actor_bringups`
(`interpreter.py:561`, `:2586`) gathers actor bring-up tasks with **no timeout**, and a
bring-up awaits `child.start()` - i.e. arbitrary user entry actions. A child whose
`async def` entry action sleeps 30 s makes `await start()` hang for 30 s with `status`
reading `"running"` throughout. No timeout knob exists anywhere in `src/`.

We downgraded this from Blocker ourselves after testing it: the run loop is spawned
**before** the await, so with a bounded call the interpreter is live and unharmed - a
`POKE` sent during the window is accepted and processed, the child finishes bring-up
afterwards, and `stop()` returns cleanly. That is exactly why a one-line caller-side
bound is a genuine mitigation rather than a fig leaf.

Source: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md` §5, §7 (CV-C39).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `cv.statechart.factory` wraps every start in `asyncio.wait_for(interp.start(), CV_START_TIMEOUT)`.
- A timeout is a **warning with the interpreter live**, never a failure to start: log,
  emit `cv_machine_start_timeout_total{kind}`, and return the handle anyway.
- Lint rule banning a bare `await interp.start()` anywhere in the codebase.
- Contract test: a child with a slow async entry action; assert `start()` returns inside
  the bound, that an event sent during the window is processed, and that `stop()` is clean.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No code path in the repo awaits `Interpreter.start()` without a bound; the lint fails on a deliberate break
- [ ] Contract test reproduces the unbounded hang on the bare library and shows the factory bounded across 100 starts
- [ ] `CV_START_TIMEOUT` is configurable and its default is recorded in the machine registry
- [ ] Retired when upstream ships a timeout parameter on `_await_actor_bringups`

## Out of scope
- Fixing the upstream defect. Ours are guards; upstream work is tracked by the `E50-C*` chores.


---

## Round-8 update (2026-09-21, `main` @ `6db65d8`, ADR-0016 Amendment 8)

**Chore verified.** #181 landed `start(children_timeout=, default 2 s)` upstream and it works for the case it was filed against: a coroutine child entry action is bounded, the repro returns in ~2.01 s instead of hanging 30 s, and the WARNING fires. CV-C39 stands and the factory bound remains mandatory.

**But the upstream bound cannot be relied on alone (R8-03).** It is a **no-op** against a non-yielding plain-`def` child entry action and it **suppresses its own WARNING** while failing: 1 child -> 3.00 s, 5 -> 15.0 s, 50 x 1 s -> 50.04 s, and 20 x 100 ms -> 2.02 s at *every* bound (0.05 / 0.2 / 1.0 / `None`), with no WARNING in any case. The bound is also **aggregate**, not per child. See the new ticket for CV-C44, which is the half we own.

title: Linter CV-LINT-XS16: invoke-cycle WARNING (CV-C38 retired round 8; was error)
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: invoke-cycle W lint folded into E50-T11 (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 9 (2026-09-22) — UPSTREAM GROUND CLOSED; guard retained as defence in depth (CV-LINT-XS16 / invoke-cycle warning).** **#200 + #201 CONFIRMED FIXED at `f28719c`.** `_chain_owed` is now a task set self-clearing via a done-callback on any terminal outcome **including a bare `BaseException`**, with debts independent per invocation (closes R8-10); and initial-descent completions are seeded rather than charged, so async lap counts match sync exactly (closes R8-11). **Re-confirmed this round by POLLING TO CONVERGENCE rather than trusting the changelog:** the rollback + `onDone` storm plateaus at **exactly `maxIterations` + 2 (1003/1003) on both lanes** and stays there. Keep CV-LINT-XS16 at WARNING. Residual R9-09 (Medium, doc): the 'all three lanes agree at every limit' claim is still false at **odd** `maxIterations` on the `def` lane.

## Context

Upstream **R7-01 (Blocker)** makes every self-generated invoke cycle unbounded **when the
service is written as `async def`** - which is what CV-C32 requires on the async engine.
Measured: 28 108 service calls in 2.0 s against **23** for the identical chart with a
plain `def` service, `last_error=None`, `status="running"`, and `maxIterations` of
2/5/25/100/1000 all identical. One variant settles into an **empty configuration** 10/10
while `send(wait=True)` reports `ok=True`. On a real contract machine, one kill-switch
`ENGAGE` produced **3 547 `flatten_all_positions` invocations in 3.0 s**, still
accelerating.

**There is no wrapper-level mitigation** (DC-4): the only one is plain-`def` services,
which #174 documents as blocking the machine's own `after` timers - and B19's
`backing_off` retry ladder depends on `after` firing during a service. Our own refutation
of R7-04 then showed plain `def` has its *own* inbox-starvation failure on the same shape.
So the only thing we can do on our side is **make the shape unrepresentable**.

This also covers our own `CD-03` (B8 `naked` <-> `verifying`: 4 027 laps in 8.05 s,
4 027 `raise_critical_alert` firings, `status="running"`, `last_error=None`), which is our
defect on any runtime and the exact shape R7-01 makes silent.

Source: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md` §4, §5, §7 (CV-C38).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CV-LINT-XS16** in `tools/lint_statecharts.py`: reject any two invoking states that can
  target each other on success paths, and any `invoke.onDone` that can re-enter its own
  source state, **unless** the re-entry is gated by a bounded attempt counter in context
  (a guard reading a counter that an entry action increments, with an exhaustion target).
- Registry field recording, per machine, which invoke cycles were found and which counter
  bounds each one.
- Contract test per machine carrying an `invoke`: drive the cycle and assert the service
  invocation count is bounded by the declared counter.
- Fix `CD-03` under this rule: bounded fallback-attempt counter on `naked.invoke.onDone`
  routing to `naked_unrecoverable` on exhaustion, and edge-trigger `raise_critical_alert`
  on `naked_since` rather than firing per lap.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The linter rejects a deliberately added unbounded invoke cycle, naming the machine and both states
- [ ] Every catalogue machine either has no invoke cycle or has a bounded counter on it, recorded in the registry
- [ ] B8's `naked` <-> `verifying` cycle terminates with a bounded, asserted invocation count
- [ ] Contract test proves the rule catches the B18 `ENGAGE` shape that produced 3 547 invocations on the bare library

## Out of scope
- Fixing R7-01 upstream. This is containment; it does not make the cycle safe, it makes it absent.


---

## Round-8 update (2026-09-21, `main` @ `6db65d8`, ADR-0016 Amendment 8)

**CV-C38 RETIRES as a machine-shape prohibition, and this rule is DOWNGRADED from error to warning. Do not delete it.**

Upstream #179 closed R7-01 at the root: completions of both service spellings now route through `_publish_completion` -> the charged priority lane, and the engine bounds the cycle itself. Measured on the real B18 at `6db65d8`: `maxIterations` 2 / 5 / 100 -> **4 / 7 / 102** service calls, `max + 2` exactly, **identical cell for cell on `def` and `async def`**; the kill-switch storm that produced 3 547 calls in 3.0 s at `221ce7c` now plateaus at **1 002** with `last_error = RunawayChainError`, flat from t=0.5 s to t=4.1 s on both lanes. A 500-config x 2 spellings x 2 engines fuzz found 0 hangs, 0 silent runaways, 0 lap mismatches.

**Why it stays as a warning.** An unguarded invoke cycle is still a design smell, and it is still the trigger R8-04 needs (an `always` into a state in its own region self-re-enables and trips `RunawayChainError` on 3 of 4 engine x service-kind combinations, silently on the fourth). A warning in review is cheap; a livelock that only *mostly* trips is not.

**Consequence for the plan: B18 leaves the library-blocked set** and moves behind C-07b, which is ours.

## Revised acceptance criteria
- [ ] The rule emits a WARNING, not an error, and CI does not fail on it
- [ ] The warning text cites R8-04 (the shape that still bites) rather than R7-01 (closed)
- [ ] A contract test pins the bound the engine now provides: `maxIterations` N -> N+2 service calls, asserted equal on both service spellings

title: Factory snapshot wrapper: post-start settle gate and root-only capture (CV-C40/C41) — VERIFIED at 6db65d8, rules RETAINED
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: settle gate + root-only (C40/C41) folded into E50-T10 (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 9 (2026-09-22) — UPSTREAM GROUND CLOSED; guard retained as defence in depth (CV-C40 / post-start settle gate).** **#199 CONFIRMED FIXED at `f28719c`.** The in-flight flag is now raised **before** `on_interpreter_start` on both engines, and a snapshot taken from inside the hook is refused with `SnapshotMidStepError` — closing the window #182 left open and with it round 8's R8-09. **CV-C40 stays in depth.** Residual R9-15 (Low): a `SnapshotMidStepError` raised from an *invoked child's* entry action reports `child=False`, which makes it harder to attribute than it needs to be.

## Context

`E50-T10` shipped the quiescence-only snapshot wrapper (CV-C23). Round 7 found two
residual windows that quiescence alone does not cover, both **High**, both upstream:

- **R7-05** - the async engine's `start()` never sets the in-flight flag (`_processing` is
  assigned only at `interpreter.py:420/1654/1698`, while `start()` at `:536-556` runs
  `_enter_states` and `_settle_transient_transitions` with it `False`; `sync_interpreter.py:370-374`
  deliberately sets it). So the #169 mid-step refusal is **inert for the entire initial-entry
  window**: 720/720 torn blobs land in `entry@start` and nowhere else, while `on_transition@start`
  tears zero times out of 320. A torn order blob (`filled_qty=100, avg_px=0`) restores silently
  with `last_error=None`.
- **R7-07 / R7-08** - a root snapshot harvests a **child actor's** half-applied context
  (`ACCEPTED child=['kid.y'] ctx={'q':100,'p':0}` against settled truth `{'q':100,'p':101}`),
  and the mechanism meant to handle that case, `_await_settled_for_snapshot`, spins
  `time.sleep` on the **event-loop thread** (`base_interpreter.py:1280-1289`), so the child
  it waits for cannot progress - 501 ms blocked per call, 1 502 ms with three children.

Source: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md` §5, §7 (CV-C40, CV-C41).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **CV-C40**: the factory records a post-start settle observation and the `snapshot()` wrapper
  **refuses** until it exists. The initial-entry window is explicitly excluded from the
  snapshot-eligible set, not merely assumed quiescent.
- **CV-C41**: snapshots capture the **root only**. Child-actor state is reported upward by
  explicit `sendTo` into parent context and persisted from there; the wrapper never relies on
  hierarchical capture and never calls `get_persisted_snapshot()` on a parent whose children
  may be mid-step (which would also block the loop).
- Restore-side clause under CV-C23: refuse a `version >= 1` payload whose `machine_hash` is
  null or absent (upstream R7-06 accepts it), in addition to the existing
  `state_ids` ⊆ `configuration` assertion (CV-C27′).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A snapshot attempted during the initial-entry window is refused by the wrapper, on a test that reproduces the 720/720 tear on the bare library
- [ ] The persisted blob's child branch is ignored on restore; a contract test asserts child state arrives only via `sendTo`-reported parent context
- [ ] No factory call path can reach `_await_settled_for_snapshot` on the async engine
- [ ] A `version >= 1` payload with a null or missing `machine_hash` is refused, with a test

## Out of scope
- Fixing R7-05/R7-07/R7-08 upstream (one-liners, filed).


---

## Round-8 update (2026-09-21, `main` @ `6db65d8`, ADR-0016 Amendment 8)

**Chore verified, and the rules are retained on narrower grounds.** #182 closed the initial-descent window (the in-flight flag now covers the whole `start()` descent and `on_action_execute`; both engines refuse the initial-entry snapshot, 0 torn blobs each), and #183/#184 closed the child mid-step harvest and the loop-spin together (37/37, same-thread children refused in <0.1 s instead of burning 0.5 s).

**CV-C40 is retained because of R8-09:** `get_persisted_snapshot()` from the `on_interpreter_start` hook still returns a torn blob (`status:"running"`, empty configuration), 600/600, on both engines. One hook short of #182's coverage. **CV-C41 is retained** as defence in depth. New clause: `SnapshotMidStepError` from a child's entry action reports `child=False` (R8-14, Low) — do not branch on that flag.

title: Gateway: ban `priority=True` OUTRIGHT (any origin) and alert on chain_budget shedding (CV-C42, widened round 8)
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: priority=True ban (C42) folded into E50-T15 + E50-T11 (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 9 (2026-09-22) — the Blocker ground is CLOSED, the ticket NARROWS but STANDS.** #192 closed R8-01 at the root: the priority lane charges self-issued sends and shields external ones **by provenance**, verified on both engines, both service kinds, and the real B18 (12/12 kill presses accepted, **0 shed**, press pre-empts the chain). The livelock and the silent external shed are both gone.
>
> **CV-C42 nevertheless stands, on narrower ground: R9-06.** A **delayed** self-`send` cycle is charged to no budget and is tagged *external* by #192, so it can never be shed — `maxIterations` is inert on that one path. Keep the outright ban and the `chain_budget` alert; **update the ticket's stated reason** so the next reader does not retire it against the (now fixed) R8-01 rationale.

## Context

Upstream **R7-02 (Blocker)**: an **external** `send(..., priority=True)` is charged to the
chain budget and silently shed. Measured at `221ce7c`: `sent=1500 processed=749 dropped=751
reasons=['chain_budget']`, with the control run - identical load, `priority=True` removed -
dropping **zero**. A burst producer loses 61 %. `_deliver_priority`
(`interpreter.py:2287-2288`) charges on `self._processing`, i.e. it decides provenance by
**when** the event arrived rather than **who** issued it, while every other enqueue path
still asks `_issued_from_own_action()` (`:826`, `:854`, `:1206`). The run loop's own
architecture note at `:1510-1516` promises external traffic is never throttled.

The loss is nearly invisible: the drop path resets `_raise_depth`/`_chain_tripped`
(`:1596-1599`), so `last_error` reads `None` and `status` stays `"running"`. It surfaces
**only** through the opt-in `on_event_dropped` hook.

**This ticket is containment, not a fix.** Nothing on our side can stop the library
charging the budget; we can only stop setting the flag and make the shedding loud.

Source: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md` §5, §7 (CV-C42).

## Scope / Deliverables
- Lint rule: `priority=True` and `send_priority(` are forbidden outside `cv.statechart` wrapper code.
- The gateway never sets `priority=True` on an externally originated event.
- Every gateway send registers an `on_event_dropped` spy; drops are counted by reason into
  `cv_machine_events_dropped_total{kind,reason}`.
- Alert: any non-zero `chain_budget` count on an externally originated send pages immediately.
  It means the library shed real input, and nothing else will tell us.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The lint fails on a deliberately added `priority=True` outside the wrapper
- [ ] A contract test reproduces the 751/1500 shed on the bare library and shows zero drops through the gateway
- [ ] `cv_machine_events_dropped_total` is emitted per reason and the `chain_budget` alert fires in a negative test
- [ ] Retired when upstream gates the charge on provenance rather than on `_processing`

## Out of scope
- Fixing R7-02 upstream.


---

## Round-8 update (2026-09-21, `main` @ `6db65d8`, ADR-0016 Amendment 8)

**CV-C42 is WIDENED. The rule is no longer 'forbidden outside wrapper code' - it is `priority=True` is forbidden EVERYWHERE, on any event, from any origin, including inside `cv.statechart` itself, and no action body may call `send(..., priority=True)`.**

Round 7's R7-02 (the *charge* half) is **fixed**: external priority sends are no longer charged - 0 drops in the filed repro, and 50 concurrent external priority sends into an open macrostep on a real control machine give 0 dropped / 0 `chain_budget` refusals on both service spellings.

But the provenance rule was applied on one side of the ledger only, and the other side is **R8-01, the round-8 Blocker**:

- a `send(priority=True)` **issued from an action** is never charged (`engine_completion` is `False` for every public priority send, whatever the issuer) and **livelocks unbounded**: 2/2 cells past the watchdog, `trip_observable: false`, `status="running"`, `last_error is None`, no drop hook, `start()` never returns. The plain-lane control on an identical machine is bounded at 27 laps with `RunawayChainError`.
- a genuinely **external** priority event at an already-tripped chain is **destroyed** as `chain_budget` - 8-9 of 2 000, `send()` accepted, `last_error is None`; the `priority=False` control loses 0 on both service kinds.

**This is containment, not a fix, and the containment is now known to be incomplete.** The library routes its own completions onto the same FIFO, so an external priority event our gateway never sent can still be shed; and the self-send half starves the loop thread that any in-process watchdog would run on. The complement is **CV-C43** (out-of-process progress supervisor) - see the new ticket.

## Revised acceptance criteria
- [ ] The lint fails on `priority=` / `send_priority(` **anywhere** in the codebase, wrapper code included - there is no allow-list
- [ ] A contract test reproduces BOTH halves of R8-01 on the bare library (self-send livelock under a process-level watchdog; external shed against a tripped chain) and shows the gateway path clean
- [ ] `cv_machine_events_dropped_total{kind,reason}` is emitted per reason and the `chain_budget` alert fires in a negative test
- [ ] Retired only when upstream carries provenance on the event and applies it at BOTH the charge site and the shed site

title: Gate harness: the verify-main-6db65d8 set, H-3 stale fixtures, and standing amendments 12+13
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: gate-harness fixtures folded into E50-T04 (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 9 (2026-09-22) — done for this round, plus the round-10 lead item.**
>
> **Landed in `gate/run_gate.py` this round:** the **`verifyM6`** set (`issues/verify-main-f28719c/`, 12 scripts, baseline **11/12 PASS** with #197 the single expected FAIL — the genuine R9-08 residual, not a stale script); `VERIFYM6_BASELINE_FAILURES`; a `SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_OVERRIDES` map so `195_provenance` / `196_always_vs_named_event` / `197_empty_config_wait` are not scored as spurious TIMEOUT/143 (they contain multiple 30 s sleep cells by construction and pass cleanly at 150 s); and standing amendments **14** and **15** recorded in the module docstring.
>
> **Our own stale fixtures fixed/retired** (`50-r9-regression.md` §2b): `R8-05_doneevent_forgery.py` now catches `UnknownEventError` as the **success** mode — it was scoring the #195 protection firing as a failure, in **both** `check1` and `check2`; re-runs green. `R8-02/03/04/11` are superseded by #193/#194/#196/#201's restated contracts and should be retired rather than repaired. `197_empty_config_wait.py` is **kept and promoted** — it is stricter than the gate's own `verifyM5` cell for the same issue, and the stricter assertion is the genuine signal.
>
> **ROUND-10 LEAD ITEM, blocking:** the **full suite + coverage run did not complete** inside the wall-clock bound this round (~51 % observed green; 92.70 % at `6db65d8`). **Decision-table row 2 keys on coverage and fires before row 6**, so the ADOPT verdict carries one unmeasured input. Run `pytest tests/ --cov=src` to completion with a fresh budget **first**, before any other round-10 step. Also owed: `bench_c_timers`, `bench_e_actors`, and a **bisection of the KB/order RSS figure**, now unbisected for a third round (3.10 -> 5.18 -> 2.128 KB) — bisect it or replace the metric.

## Context

Two harness defects found in round 7, both ours, both causing false regression signals; plus
the standing amendment the round produced.

- **H-1** - `VERIFYM3_BASELINE_FAILURES` in `gate/run_gate.py` recorded only `["157"]`, while
  the `issues/verify-main-cec108b/` directory had since gained
  `150_send_threadsafe_budgeted.py` and `probe_144_async*.py`. Both are 5/5 deterministic
  pre-existing FAILs that appear in **no** `result-main-cec108b.json` row - new rows being
  misreported as regressions. **Fixed in this round's edit** (`["157", "150", "probe"]`).
- **H-2** - the `verify` set had no baseline-failure allow-list at all, so five unchanged
  pre-existing FAILs (`LC-01`, `LC-12`, `LC-26`, `LC-48`, `LC-57`) flagged on every run.
  **Fixed in this round's edit** (`VERIFY_BASELINE_FAILURES`).
- **Standing amendment 12** - *every test that invokes a service runs under both service
  kinds, and every test of an engine-level invariant under both engines.* Round 6's failure
  mode was "fixed on the engine the issue was filed against"; round 7's is "fixed on the
  service kind the test was written against". **Our own round-6 confirmation scripts declared
  `def` services and therefore confirmed a fix that does not hold on the lane our mandatory
  configuration requires.** A gate row exercising an `invoke` that is not parametrised over
  service kind is not evidence.

Source: `docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md` §2, §6;
`docs/research/xstate/20-adoption-gate.md` standing amendment 12.

## Scope / Deliverables
- Verify the H-1/H-2 allow-lists on the next gate run and confirm the flagged-delta count drops to the true regression count.
- Parametrise every gate and contract script that declares an `invoke` over `def` / `async def`,
  and make an unparametrised invoke row a harness error rather than a silent pass.
- Add the round-7 verification set `issues/verify-main-221ce7c` as `verifyM4` (**done** in this
  round's edit) and keep the per-wave, commit-keyed convention.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A full gate run reports zero flagged deltas that are not true regressions
- [ ] Every invoke-exercising row runs under both service kinds and records which kind produced which result
- [ ] An unparametrised invoke row is reported as an ERROR row, not a PASS
- [ ] A deliberately reverted upstream fix is caught on the `async def` leg

## Out of scope
- Upstream's own test suite. We can only ask; the ask is recorded in `issues/post-221ce7c/meta-26.md`.


---

## Round-8 update (2026-09-21, `main` @ `6db65d8`, ADR-0016 Amendment 8)

**H-1 and H-2 are done and verified** — `VERIFYM3_BASELINE_FAILURES` carries `150`/`probe`, and the `verify` set has its own allow-list. Neither produced a false regression signal this round.

**Landed by the round-8 pass:** `gate/run_gate.py` gains the **`verifyM5`** set (`issues/verify-main-6db65d8/`, 16 scripts), with `VERIFYM5_BASELINE_FAILURES = ["174"]` — #174 was closed DOCUMENTED-ONLY, so its script correctly still reports the behaviour the documentation describes; if that row ever flips to PASS, the behaviour changed and the docs are stale. Note that `167` PASSES in `verifyM5` while it is allow-listed in `verifyM4`: the sets are keyed on different commits on purpose and **their allow-lists must not be merged**.

**H-3, new and outstanding (ours):** `issues/verify-main-cec108b/154_sync-restore-clock-attach.py` and `158_non_str_event_type_restore.py` hand-build a `version: N` snapshot blob with **no** `machine_hash`. That shape was valid at `221ce7c` and is correctly refused at `6db65d8` by #185, so both scripts now fail before reaching the behaviour they were written to probe. These are the only two gate deltas this round and neither is a library regression. Add a `machine_hash` to both blobs so they resume testing their original assertions. (`158`'s sub-case `[B]` still passes, which is what confirmed the underlying #158 fix is intact.)

**Standing amendment 13, new this round, binding on our scripts:** every gate row exercising a `send` must be parametrised over **issuer provenance** (external vs issued from an action) and **chain state** (untripped vs already tripped), exactly as amendment 12 requires for service kind. R8-01 survived an upstream fix, a pinned upstream test and a full battle round because every existing test sent externally into an untripped chain.

**The general form of amendments 12 and 13, worth writing into the harness docstring:** when a fix distinguishes two cases, the test must exercise both sides of the distinction — **and the arm expected to fail must be given work that can actually fail**. Round 8's own example: `tests/test_round7_findings.py:557` parametrises over `KINDS` but gives the `def` arm `time.sleep(0.05)` against the async arm's `asyncio.sleep(3.0)`, so the `def` branch cannot fail and R8-03 shipped green. A parametrised test whose arms are not equally capable of failing is not parametrised.

## Added acceptance criteria
- [ ] `machine_hash` added to the two `verify-main-cec108b` fixtures; both resume PASSing their original assertions (H-3)
- [ ] The amendment-12/13 rule is stated in `run_gate.py`'s module docstring and in the `verifyM5` runner docstring (landed)
- [ ] A reviewer checklist item: does every parametrised arm have work capable of failing?

title: Migrate the non-order machines to the library (B10-B17, B19, B20) under CV-C01…CV-C45
body:

Migration proceeds **by machine group, order path last, everything behind the standing contract suite**: **E50-T32** Phase 1 (B10-B15, B17, B19, B20 — four shims retire on #196/#194/#186/#199), **E50-T33** Phase 2 (B16, B18 — blocked on **our** C-04/C-07b, not the library), **E50-T34** Phase 3 (the order path, four preconditions including the coverage measurement still owed from this round). Contract suite in CI as a blocking gate is **E50-T31** — that ticket is the mechanism the whole row-6 verdict rests on.

## Context

**This is the GO half of the round-7 verdict, and it is a real GO, not a hedge.** Round 7
(`docs/research/xstate/44-r7-final-readiness-verdict.md` §4) drove all 20 contract machines end-to-end on
`main` @ `221ce7c`: 20/20 build with zero `InvalidConfigError` and zero
`ImplementationMissingError`; B1-B5 pass **112/112** invariant checks; B6-B10 pass 54/55 (the
single failure is a stale harness assertion of ours, HD-01); B11-B15 pass every stated
invariant with 5/5 async<->sync parity; and the B16-B20 control suites reproduce

macrostep is clean on every group - zero spurious `SnapshotMidStepError`, zero state/context
diffs against the uninterrupted run, identical traces.

**Scope of the migration is exactly B10-B17, B19 and B20.** B16, B17 and B20 carry no

## Scope / Deliverables

  `OverflowPolicy.RAISE`, explicit `service_pool_size`, `async def` services only (CV-C32),
  bounded `start()` (E50-T20), snapshot wrapper (E50-T22), gateway sends only (E50-T23).
- Health checks key on a **progress counter**, never on `status` or `last_error` - on the async

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every catalogue invariant for those machines has a passing test under the library runtime
- [ ] No machine in the set has an unguarded invoke cycle (E50-T21 lint green)

**The GO is re-confirmed at `6db65d8`, on stronger evidence than round 7 had, and the migration is now phased.** All 20 machines build from the corrected catalogue JSON with zero `InvalidConfigError` and zero `ImplementationMissingError` **on both service spellings** — the harness gained a `CV_SVC_STYLE` axis and every service-bearing cell was run twice and compared cell by cell.

title: Shim retirement ladder: shadow mode, one-machine-at-a-time cutover, 30-day hold on B1
