title: Out-of-process progress supervisor for the order path (CV-C43)
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: CV-C43 retired (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 9 (2026-09-22) — RETIRED AS A MANDATE; keep the supervisor as a recommendation.** This ticket's entire ground was R8-01's livelock, which starved the very loop thread every in-process detector runs on. **#192 closes it at the root** (verified both engines, both service kinds, real B18). **`status` and `last_error` are liveness signals again**, and CV-C43 drops from "the only permitted detector for the order path" to "good operational practice we keep anyway".
>
> **Action: do not cancel the work — descope it.** Ship the out-of-process progress counter as defence in depth for the order path (it remains the right design for an OMS), but remove the *mandate* language from CV-C43, the factory assertion that forbids in-process watchdogs, and the contract test that asserts the in-process detector fails. Estimate should drop accordingly.

## Context

Upstream **R8-01 (Blocker)** produces an unbounded livelock that **starves the event loop
thread**. Every in-process detector we might reach for runs on that thread:
`asyncio.wait_for` never fires, a loop-resident supervisor task never gets scheduled,
`stop()` never returns. And the machine looks healthy throughout — `status == "running"`,
`last_error is None`, no `on_event_dropped` hook fires.

Round 7 already established that `status` and `last_error` are not liveness signals
(R7-01/R7-03/R7-15) and that every supervisor keys on a **progress counter**. Round 8
strengthens that: the counter must be read from **outside the process**.

## Scope / Deliverables
- A monotonic progress counter per order-path machine, incremented on every applied
  transition, exported over a transport that does not depend on the machine's own loop
  (shared memory, a file, or a metrics endpoint served by a separate thread with its own
  loop — not a coroutine on the machine's loop).
- A **separate supervisor process** with a wall-clock deadline per machine. A counter that
  does not advance within the deadline while the machine reports `status == "running"` is a
  page, and the runbook entry is "the loop is starved; take a process dump before
  restarting".
- A negative test: deliberately starve a test machine's loop and assert the out-of-process
  detector fires **while the in-process one does not**. That asymmetry is the whole point of
  the ticket and it must be pinned, not assumed.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] No in-process watchdog is the sole liveness detector for any order-path machine
- [ ] The negative test above passes, and fails if the supervisor is moved in-process
- [ ] The deadline is configurable per machine group and defaults conservatively
- [ ] Alert routing and a runbook entry exist before the first order-path machine migrates

## Out of scope
- Fixing R8-01 upstream. This detects; it does not prevent.

title: Factory: per-child bring-up bound + lint banning non-coroutine entry actions on invoke-bearing states (CV-C44)
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: per-child bring-up bound (C44) folded into E50-T59 + E50-T11 (29 §4a)**

## Context

Upstream **R8-03 (High)**: `start(children_timeout=)` is a **no-op** against a non-yielding
plain-`def` child entry action, and it **suppresses its own WARNING** while failing. Measured
at `6db65d8`:

| `children_timeout` | shape | elapsed | WARNING |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.2 | 1 child, `def` entry action sleeping 3 s | 3.00 s | none |
| 0.2 | 5 children | 15.0 s | none |
| 0.2 | 50 children x 1 s | 50.04 s | none |
| 0.05 / 0.2 / 1.0 / `None` | 20 children x 100 ms | 2.02 s in all four | none |

`_await_actor_bringups` uses `asyncio.wait(timeout=)`, which cannot pre-empt a non-yielding
`def` action on the loop thread inside `child.start()`; bring-ups are serial, hence the exact
N x D scaling; and the WARNING sits on the same timeout path, so it is suppressed with the
bound. The upstream guarding test cannot fail (its `def` arm sleeps 0.05 s against the async
arm's 3.0 s).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Lint:** no non-`async def` entry action on any state carrying an `invoke`. CV-C32 already
  requires coroutine *services*; this extends the rule to *entry actions* on the states that
  bring children up, and requires at least one `await` in the body.
- **Factory:** bound each child's bring-up ourselves, per child, rather than relying on the
  library's aggregate `asyncio.wait`. A child that exceeds its bound is logged and the parent
  continues with the child recorded as not-ready.
- **Our own WARNING**, emitted from our bound rather than the library's, so a suppressed
  upstream warning is still a logged event on our side.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Contract test at N=20 children asserting total bring-up time ≈ the bound, **not**
      N x the bound
- [ ] The lint fails on a deliberately added plain-`def` entry action on an invoke-bearing state
- [ ] A bring-up timeout is visible in logs and metrics in a negative test
- [ ] Retired when upstream bounds per child and moves the WARNING off the timeout path

## Out of scope
- Fixing R8-03 upstream.

title: Restore path: strip DoneEvent/AfterEvent from pending_events; gateway rejects completion events (CV-C45)
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: CV-C45 stripping clause retired (#214) (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 10 (19cb1f1, 2026-09-22) — SEND-SIDE CLAUSE RETIRES; RESTORE-SIDE CLAUSE STANDS AND IS RE-GROUNDED.**
>
> **R9-02 is CLOSED upstream by #203.** `base_interpreter.py:4624` now gates `after` selection on
> `isinstance(event, AfterEvent) and is_system_event(event)` — the same test the `Done`/`Error`
> branch already used, which is exactly the one-line fix this ticket predicted. Re-verified fresh:
> a public `AfterEvent` with the correct type string is refused at `send()` with a named
> `UnknownEventError` **on both spellings and at the DEFAULT `strict=false`**, where it previously
> fired a 60-second timer instantly. The forged-`pending_events` vector (no `"engine"` flag) also
> no longer fires the timer.
>
> **Therefore: the GATEWAY-REJECTION half of CV-C45 retires.** We no longer need to reject
> externally submitted `AfterEvent`/`DoneEvent` instances at the gateway — the engine refuses them
> itself. Delete that clause and its test; keeping it would misstate why the protection exists.
>
> **The RESTORE-side clause does NOT retire, and its scope changes.** Two surviving residuals,
> both re-verified this round with standalone repros from a neutral cwd:
>  - **R10-05(a)** `strict` is still not applied to restored events: `_check_strict` runs at the
>    `send()` call site (`base_interpreter.py:1767`) and `_enqueue_restored` -> `_put_inbox`
>    bypasses it. A restored undeclared `BOGUS` is accepted under `strict: true`
>    (`status=running`, `last_error=None`). This contradicts the documented restore contract at
>    `events.py:403-414`.
>  - **R10-05(b), NEW and the reason the clause widens**: a 0.8.0-era record has `kind:"after"`
>    but no `engine` flag, so #203's gate **refuses** it — and **drops the deadline silently**:
>    no raise, no WARNING, nothing on `last_error`, and `has_dormant_timers` does not cover it.
>    Measured: the same blob reaches `t.late` at `f28719c` and stays at `t.wait` at `19cb1f1`.
>
> **Acceptance changes:** the restore filter matches the **serialised record `kind`** as well as
> the class (unchanged), **and additionally re-arms the corresponding deadlines from context**
> rather than relying on the restored record. A refused restored deadline must be **loud in our
> code**, because it is silent in the library's. See E50-T37 (CV-C48) for the migration fence.
>
> Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/59-r10-final-readiness-verdict.md` §1, §5, §7;
> repro `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-19cb1f1/new/repro/R10-05_restore_bypasses_strict_and_drops_after.py`.

> **ROUND 9 (2026-09-22) — STANDS and is WIDENED. This is now one of the two load-bearing containments in the whole gate decision.** R8-05's ground narrowed (#195 landed: a hand-built `DoneEvent`/`ErrorEvent`/`AfterEvent` **is** correctly refused at `send()` under `strict` — we re-ran this rather than inheriting our own claim, which had overstated it). But the restore door is wide open and is now **R9-02, High**.
>
> **Widening required, and the detail is the whole point:** the restore filter must match on the **SERIALISED RECORD** (`kind` in {`done`, `error`, `after`}), **not only on the deserialised class**, because R9-02's decisive vector is a record carrying **no `"engine"` flag** that `_enqueue_restored` (`base_interpreter.py:1768`) hands straight to the inbox — it **never meets a `send()`-time check at all**. A class-only filter passes it through. With `strict=true` the machine still fires a 60-second timer from untrusted snapshot data.
>
> Also: the gateway rejection must **explicitly name `AfterEvent`**, not only the completion classes.
>
> **Acceptance test (named in the gate decision):** `test_cv_c45_strips_completion_and_after_events` — plant `{"kind":"after","type":"after.60000.m.work"}` with no `engine` flag in a blob, assert it is stripped and the timer does **not** fire. Repro: `issues/post-f28719c/new/repro/R9-02_after_matched_on_public_class.py`.

## Context

Upstream **R8-05 (High)**: `DoneEvent` and `AfterEvent` are publicly exported, publicly
documented NamedTuples with **no provenance field**. `is_system_event` returns `True` for
them on a bare `isinstance`, so they are exempt from `strict` and `onUnhandled` — the
documented "provenance, not name" invariant is false for exactly the two classes that assert
engine authorship. A forged `DoneEvent` drives a real `onDone` while the genuine service is
still running, because the match is on name plus `event.src == inv.id` with **no liveness
check**.

The escalating vector is what makes this ours and not merely upstream's: `restore_event`
reconstitutes a **trusted** `DoneEvent` from an attacker-authored snapshot record with no
integrity check over `pending_events`, and that object then drives `onDone` on a live
machine. That is a wire vector.

For an OMS the concrete harm is a forged `done.invoke.<fill-service>` committing a fabricated
fill price and quantity into context while the real venue call is outstanding.

## Scope / Deliverables
- The restore path **strips** every `DoneEvent` / `AfterEvent` from `pending_events` before
  `from_snapshot()`. In-flight completions are re-derived from the restored configuration,
  never replayed from the blob.
- The gateway **rejects** any externally submitted event whose type is an instance of either
  class, with a counted, alertable refusal.
- A contract test that plants a forged `DoneEvent` in a blob and asserts it is stripped, and
  a second that submits one through the gateway and asserts refusal.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Forged completion events in a blob never reach the interpreter
- [ ] The gateway refuses completion-event types and the refusal is counted
- [ ] Both negative tests fail if the filter is removed
- [ ] Retired when upstream gives the two classes an engine-only provenance marker **and**
      adds a liveness check to the `onDone` match

## Out of scope
- Fixing R8-05 upstream.

title: CV-C46: the order path never runs on SyncInterpreter — factory assertion, lint, contract test
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: CV-C46 retired; async-only (C03) folded into E50-T59 + CV-LINT-IMPORT (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 10 (19cb1f1, 2026-09-22) — CLOSE THIS TICKET. CV-C46 RETIRES.**
>
> **R9-04 is CLOSED upstream by #204.** Invoke arming moved into the eventless settle pass per
> SCXML §6.1 `statesToInvoke`: a state entered and exited within one macrostep never submits its
> service. Re-verified fresh, **on both engines and both service kinds**:
>
> | measurement | `f28719c` | `19cb1f1` |
> |---|---|---|
> | roll-forward submissions, 8 cells | `def` cells submitted 1 each | **0 in all 8** |
> | `LD-01` repro, 6 lanes | **3 leaked** | **0 leaked** |
> | B6–B10 invariants, `def` lane | 51/52 | **52/52** |
> | mandated drives D1–D3, `def` lane | 13/14 | **14/14** |
> | `167 rollback_reinvoke_spin` (sync) | FAIL (recorded expected-FAIL) | **PASS ×5/5 stable** |
>
> That last row is this ticket's entire ground. We had recorded `167` as a *permanent*
> expected-failure and built CV-C46 around it, because two of R9-04's three leaking lanes were
> sync-engine lanes. **All three are closed.**
>
> **Action: retire CV-C46 as a mandate** — delete the factory assertion and the lint on direct
> `SyncInterpreter(` construction, and retire `test_cv_c46_order_path_engine_is_async`. The async
> engine remains our order-path engine as a **design preference** (throughput, preemptability),
> not as defect containment.
>
> **Do NOT also retire CV-C32.** It retires as a *safety* rule but the rule itself stands verbatim,
> re-grounded on **R10-D2**: an invoke-bearing state with an escape transition cannot be pre-empted
> on the `def` lane — the entering macrostep awaits the service, so the escape is not an escape.
> Binds B12 `buffering`, B12 `stepping`, B13 `subscribing`. Re-label the constraint's justification
> in the lint docstring; keeping the R9-04 justification is how constraints rot.
>
> **Keep `test_ld01_rollforward_lane_matrix`, inverted**: it pinned 3/6 leaks so an upstream fix
> would be *detected*. It detected one. Re-pin it at **0/6** so a regression is detected too.
>
> Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/59-r10-final-readiness-verdict.md` §0, §1, §7;
> `docs/research/xstate/55-r10-regression.md`.

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 9, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog, not undated by oversight.** The R2 train is at capacity, so this round-9 ticket is not scheduled into Sprints 10-13 without displacing committed work. It is **not** optional: E50-T29/T30/T31 are the mechanisms the ADOPT-WITH-CONSTRAINTS verdict rests on (decision-table row 6 requires a mechanically enforced mitigation AND a passing contract test for each open High). Schedule them at the next train planning, ahead of the Phase 2/3 retirement tickets, which are in any case gated on preconditions that cannot be dated yet (five green nightlies, C-04/C-07b, a two-week canary, and the coverage measurement still owed from this round).

## Context

Upstream **R9-04 (High)**: a plain `def` service armed by a transition an `always` rolls
**forward** is still submitted to the executor. Re-run fresh at `f28719c`, **3 of 6 lanes
leak**:

```
ok   case A (roll-forward) | async service | async engine | calls=[]
LEAK case A (roll-forward) | def   service | async engine | calls=['submit_child']
LEAK case A (roll-forward) | def   service | sync  engine | calls=['submit_child']
ok   case B (rollback)     | async service | async engine | calls=[]
ok   case B (rollback)     | def   service | async engine | calls=[]     <- #193 landing
LEAK case B (rollback)     | def   service | sync  engine | calls=['submit_child']
```

`docs/_guide/production-characteristics.md:97` promises the opposite **verbatim** ("rolled
forward ... is **never** submitted to the pool"), and SCXML 6.4 agrees with the doc
(`exitStates` removes the state from `statesToInvoke`). In OMS terms this is a real child
order submitted from a state the machine never settled in — and no compensation path is
attached, because the transition that would have handled it was rolled forward.

**Two of the three leaking lanes are sync-engine lanes.** CV-C32 (async engine => every
service `async def`) already removes the third. So CV-C32 + CV-C46 together make **every**
leaking lane unreachable for us — which is exactly why the gate could record ADOPT WITH
CONSTRAINTS (row 6) rather than DEFER (row 7).

## Scope / Deliverables

- Factory assertion: every order-path machine (B1-B9, B18) is constructed on the async
  `Interpreter` with an **explicit** `service_pool_size`. Constructing one on
  `SyncInterpreter` raises at build time.
- Lint: direct `SyncInterpreter(` construction is banned outside an allow-listed module set
  (tests, backtests, non-order tooling), and is **never** permitted with a side-effecting
  service.
- `test_cv_c46_order_path_engine_is_async` in `tests/xstate_contract/`.
- `test_ld01_rollforward_lane_matrix` pinning the current 3/6 leak, so an upstream fix is
  **detected** rather than silently assumed. (Round 9's lesson: a test that pins current
  behaviour must say so; see standing amendment 15.)

## Also covered by this constraint

- **R9-09** — the sync/async lap divergence at odd `maxIterations` on the `def` lane has no
  runtime consequence once the order path is never sync.
- The `167` `rollback_reinvoke_spin` gate FAIL, which is a `SyncInterpreter`-only behaviour

>    and `re_elevated_dead=False` for all four kills, **both spellings**.
>    `B16.machine.json` is byte-identical to the catalogue (sha1 `9d8ad9937417`).
>  - **C-07b / B18**: `onUnhandled:"error"` is documented opt-in policy and a guard-denied event
>    *is* an unhandled event (#170). SCXML §3.13 and XState v5 both consume an event whose only
>    guarded arm denies; **neither spec even defines an error-on-unhandled disposition**.
>    **Corrected usage** — adding the ordered unguarded `RELEASE` fallback while **KEEPING**
>    `onUnhandled:"error"` — yields `denied -> running/engaged` and `authorised -> running/clear`
>    on both engines. The round-6 Amendment-6 removal **still has not landed in the JSON**
>    (`ka_killswitch` sha1 `3d0de943effd` at `19cb1f1`).

>    `reconciliation.stale_lockout` while catalogue invariant **INV-B19-b says it is "cleared only
>    by `OPERATOR_RESOLVED`"**: the contract contradicts its own normative invariant. The lockout
>    *is* escapable (hence Medium, not High — the original High premise was refuted), but only by a
>    **connectivity** signal, so an automatic reconnect can clear a paged critical state with no
>    operator in the loop and no distinct audit record; the escape is venue-conditional; and
>    deferred events accumulate without bound (1 -> 8 across presses, still 8 after escaping).
>    Fix: add `OPERATOR_RESOLVED` to `stale_lockout.on` targeting `idle` with `reset_failures`
>    plus an audit action.
>  - **R10-C5 (Medium)** — B16's `elevated -> elevated` `STEP_UP_OK` re-enter arm carries
>    `[stamp_elevated_until]` only, omitting the `audit_step_up` present on the `normal -> elevated`
>    arm, so **a privilege extension leaves no audit record** (`audit_step_up=1` for 2 presses,
>    both lanes).

title: Snapshot envelope: HMAC tag on control-plane blobs + refuse version < 1 before restore (CV-C23 clause)
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: HMAC envelope folded into E50-T49 (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 10 (19cb1f1, 2026-09-22) — STANDS, and the ground is now MEASURED rather than argued.**
>
> #205 landed and gives a caller `minimum_version` and `expected_machine_hash`, both of which refuse
> an untrusted payload on both engines, and the payload can no longer select its own level of
> checking. **Pass both explicitly.** But #205's own docstring is correct that `machine_hash` is
> "a fingerprint against accidental drift, **not a MAC**" — and we tested what that means rather
> than accepting it: **a hand-edited snapshot with NO event forgery at all** restores a machine to
> `{'z.late'}` with context `{'n': 999}`.
>
> **So the HMAC tag over the whole blob is the only real boundary, and this ticket is the whole of
> it.** That measurement is also why R10-01 was refuted from Blocker to Low: the forged
> `"engine": true` record adds **zero capability** over what the blob writer already holds.
>
> **Scope addition:** the envelope also fences the 0.8.0-era `after` records — see E50-T37 (CV-C48).
> Evidence: `docs/research/xstate/59-r10-final-readiness-verdict.md` §0, §5, §7.

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 9, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog, not undated by oversight.** The R2 train is at capacity, so this round-9 ticket is not scheduled into Sprints 10-13 without displacing committed work. It is **not** optional: E50-T29/T30/T31 are the mechanisms the ADOPT-WITH-CONSTRAINTS verdict rests on (decision-table row 6 requires a mechanically enforced mitigation AND a passing contract test for each open High). Schedule them at the next train planning, ahead of the Phase 2/3 retirement tickets, which are in any case gated on preconditions that cannot be dated yet (five green nightlies, C-04/C-07b, a two-week canary, and the coverage measurement still owed from this round).

## Context

Upstream **R9-05**, refuted **High -> Medium** and reclassified as a **wrapper obligation,
not a library defect**. Reproduced at `f28719c`:

- An internally-consistent forged `state_ids` (`"m.b"`) **relocates the machine**
  (8 of 9 other mutations are correctly refused — that is #186/#198 working).
- **3 of 3 downgrade forms** (`version=0`, `version` key absent, `version=0` + `hash=None`)
  restore into a **drifted** machine (`m.a -> JUMP -> m.c`), while the intact control
  correctly raises `SnapshotDriftError`.

**Why this is ours and not upstream's:** `check_identity`'s docstring documents that v0
payloads are accepted unchecked **by design** and that #185 is deliberately keyed on the
declared version. #186/#198 are **shape-integrity** checks, not authenticity checks. XState
v5 `createActor({snapshot})` likewise trusts persisted snapshots, and SCXML specifies no
persistence model — so there is no divergence to cite and no correct-usage fix inside the
library. Exploitation presupposes write access to the snapshot store, i.e. trusted input.

**But for an OMS the snapshot store is not inside the trust perimeter, unqualified.**

## Scope / Deliverables

- Our envelope writes and verifies an **HMAC tag** over control-plane snapshots; the tag is
  checked **before** `from_snapshot()` is called.
- The restore path **refuses `version < 1` or absent `version`** outright on our blobs.
- Both directions of `configuration` / `state_ids` agreement still asserted (CV-C27', now
  defence in depth since #186 became two-sided).
- Contract test: a tampered blob and each of the three downgrade forms are refused.

## Upstream ask (filed, not blocking)

`minimum_version=` and `expected_machine_hash=` parameters on `from_snapshot()`, plus a
docstring note that `structure_hash` is a **checksum, not an authentication tag**.

body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: QueueOverflowError accounting folded into E50-T15 (29 §4a)**

> **ROUND 10 (19cb1f1, 2026-09-22) — BOTH HALVES STILL REQUIRED, both re-verified.**

>    Measured at `19cb1f1`: `callsite_refusals 241414`, `loopside_refusals 1811`,
>    `queue_full_hooks 1811` — **99.3 % of shed is invisible to the hook**. The call-site raise is
>    itself loud, so this is Low; the defect is that a metrics pipeline built on `on_event_dropped`
>    under-reports the shed rate by two orders of magnitude. The gateway counts refusals itself.
>  - **R10-07** (top-level config-key whitelist): unchanged and **measured harder this round**.
>    6/6 safety-relevant typos build clean while the value is dropped —
>    `actionErrorPolicyy` -> `continue`, `onUnhandledEvent` -> `ignore`, `Strict` -> `False`,
>    `maxIteration` -> `1000`. **Every one degrades in the permissive direction with a green build.**
>    Control confirms bad *values* for *known* keys are still correctly refused with
>    `InvalidConfigError`, so the gap is the key set alone.
> Repro: `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-19cb1f1/new/repro/R10-07_unknown_config_keys_accepted_silently.py`.

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 9, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog, not undated by oversight.** The R2 train is at capacity, so this round-9 ticket is not scheduled into Sprints 10-13 without displacing committed work. It is **not** optional: E50-T29/T30/T31 are the mechanisms the ADOPT-WITH-CONSTRAINTS verdict rests on (decision-table row 6 requires a mechanically enforced mitigation AND a passing contract test for each open High). Schedule them at the next train planning, ahead of the Phase 2/3 retirement tickets, which are in any case gated on preconditions that cannot be dated yet (five green nightlies, C-04/C-07b, a two-week canary, and the coverage measurement still owed from this round).

## Context

Two small upstream gaps, both Low, both cheaply contained on our side, grouped because they
land in the same two files.

**R9-11 — the drop hook under-reports by ~99.8 %.** A `QueueOverflowError` raised at the
**call site** fires no `on_event_dropped`, so a supervisor correlating shed rate via the hook
sees almost none of it. CV-C36 already requires every `send_threadsafe` future to be read;
this extends it: **the gateway counts its own refusals** rather than inferring them from a
hook that cannot see them.

**R9-16 — a typo in any top-level config key is accepted silently** and the policy
**downgrades to its default**. For our mandatory block that means a misspelled
`actionErrorPolicy` or `strict` silently reverts to the unsafe default — the exact failure
mode the mandatory block exists to prevent. `spawnBlockingTimeout` additionally parses but
sets no `MachineNode` attribute, so a post-build conformance lint **cannot** assert it
(carried since R8-15).

## Scope / Deliverables

- Gateway maintains its own refusal counter, paged on a threshold, and reconciles it against
  `on_event_dropped` (divergence between the two is itself a signal).
- Wrapper **whitelists top-level config keys** at build time and **fails the build** on an
  unknown one — this is the only place `spawnBlockingTimeout` can be asserted at all.
- Contract tests for both.

title: CV-C48: fence 0.8.0-era snapshots; a refused after deadline must be LOUD
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: CV-C48 retired (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 10, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog, not undated by oversight.** The R2 train is at capacity, so round-10 tickets are not scheduled into Sprints 10-13 without displacing committed work. They are **not** optional: they are the enforcement half of the constraints the row-8 decision names, and E50-T34 (Phase-3 order-path retirement) lists them as precondition (ii). Schedule at the next train planning, ahead of the Phase 2/3 retirement tickets, which are in any case gated on preconditions that cannot be dated yet (five green nightlies, C-04/C-07b, and a two-week canary).

## Context

**R10-05(b), Medium, CONFIRMED at `19cb1f1` with a standalone repro from a neutral cwd.**

`#203` correctly refuses a persisted `after` record that carries no `engine` flag — and **drops the
deadline silently**. A record written by 0.8.0 has `kind: "after"` (the v2 shape, so the v1
name-based fallback does not catch it) but no `engine` flag, so the new provenance gate declines it
with **no raise, no WARNING, nothing on `last_error`**, `status` stays `running`, and
`has_dormant_timers` does not cover it because the event was already in the persisted inbox rather
than awaiting re-arm.

Measured: the same blob reaches `t.late` at `f28719c` and stays at `t.wait` at `19cb1f1`.

**The security direction of `#203` is right and we are not asking for it back.** A dropped deadline
is simply the worst of the three available outcomes: firing it would be wrong (that was the bug),
refusing it *loudly* lets the caller re-arm from context, and refusing it *silently* produces a
machine that restores into a legal configuration, reports health on every surface, and never hits
its deadline. Anyone upgrading with live persisted state hits this, and by construction will not
find out from the library.

## Scope

1. **Envelope fence.** The restore path rejects any `pending_events` record with `kind: "after"`
   and no `engine` flag, refuses the blob, and **re-arms the deadline from context**. A refused
   restored deadline is loud in *our* code because it is silent in the library's.
2. **Version fence.** Envelope carries and enforces a writer-version field, so a pre-0.8.1 blob is
   identified before `from_snapshot` rather than by inspecting records.
3. **Migration pass** for any blob already at rest.
4. Pass `minimum_version=1` and `expected_machine_hash=<ours>` explicitly to `from_snapshot` (#205).

## Acceptance

- `test_cv_c48_pre_0_8_1_after_record_refused_loudly` — plants a `{"kind":"after",
  "type":"after.60000.t.wait"}` record with no `engine` flag, asserts the restore is **refused with
  our own named error** and that the deadline is re-armed from context.
- A restore drill against a real pre-0.8.1 blob, green.
- Filed upstream (**not posted**):
  `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-19cb1f1/new/R10-05-restore-bypasses-strict-and-silently-drops-after.md`.

Repro: `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-19cb1f1/new/repro/R10-05_restore_bypasses_strict_and_drops_after.py` (exit 1 = defect present).

title: CV-C47/C49: ban self-paced raise(delay=); no snapshot with armed debt
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: CV-C47 retired; C49′ half folded into E50-T10 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 10, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog, not undated by oversight.** The R2 train is at capacity, so round-10 tickets are not scheduled into Sprints 10-13 without displacing committed work. They are **not** optional: they are the enforcement half of the constraints the row-8 decision names, and E50-T34 (Phase-3 order-path retirement) lists them as precondition (ii). Schedule at the next train planning, ahead of the Phase 2/3 retirement tickets, which are in any case gated on preconditions that cannot be dated yet (five green nightlies, C-04/C-07b, and a two-week canary).

## Context

Two round-10 Mediums against the same `#206` mechanism, both CONFIRMED with standalone repros from
a neutral cwd, both on `def` and `async def`.

**R10-03 — the chain charge is TIME-BLIND.** `interpreter.py:2206-2247` makes a delayed self-send a
debt of the arming step and charges its firing as engine work. Nothing in that path is time-aware:
the chain clears only on "raised nothing, armed nothing, owes nothing", and a heartbeat re-arms in
its own entry action, so that test is false on every lap. A `raise(delay=)` self-paced heartbeat
therefore **dies at `maxIterations` beats regardless of period** — measured **9 beats at 30 ms,
100 ms and 250 ms alike** with `maxIterations: 8`. The lap count is identical at every period,
confirming the charge is purely per-lap.

**The documented idiom is unaffected** and is the migration: `after` measured **93 / 92 beats in
3 s with ZERO drops** on the same config. Downgraded High -> Medium on exactly that evidence.

**R10-04 — an armed-but-unfired delayed self-`raise` is silently lost on restore.**
`_snapshot_pending_events` (`interpreter.py:1480-1497`) reads the priority queue and inbox deque
only, so an armed timer has **no representation in the snapshot at all** — unlike a *fired* `after`,
which `#107` persists. `#206` made the delayed self-send a debt; **a snapshot discharges that debt**
with no hook, no warning and no error, and restore does not re-run entry actions. Measured on both
kinds: live reaches `debt.b`, restored is stuck at `debt.a` forever. An **external** delayed send
survives the same round-trip — the asymmetry is what makes it a defect.

## Scope

- **CV-C47**: lint bans `{"type":"raise","params":{"delay":...}}` targeting the machine's own events
  in any machine definition. Periodic work runs on the external `MonotonicScheduler`, or on `after`
  (**coarse timeouts only** — BENCH-6 is unmeasured for two rounds), or on the sync engine's
  `tick()`.
- **CV-C49**: the snapshot wrapper asserts no in-flight delayed self-`raise` before snapshotting;
  a static check forbids any state on the persisted path whose only exit is a delayed self-`raise`.

## Acceptance

- `test_cv_c47_no_self_delayed_raise` (lint over the catalogue, both engines).
- `test_cv_c49_no_armed_self_delay_at_snapshot`.
- Filed upstream (**not posted**):
  `.../new/R10-03-delayed-selfsend-heartbeat-dies-at-maxiterations.md`,
  `.../new/R10-04-armed-delayed-selfraise-lost-on-restore.md`.

Repros: `.../new/repro/R10-03_delayed_selfsend_heartbeat_dies.py`,
`.../new/repro/R10-04_delayed_selfraise_lost_on_restore.py` (both exit 1 = defect present).

title: CV-C50: chain-trip observability on BOTH lanes — never poll `last_error`
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: chain-trip observability (C50/C63) folded into E50-T60 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 10, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog, not undated by oversight.** The R2 train is at capacity, so round-10 tickets are not scheduled into Sprints 10-13 without displacing committed work. They are **not** optional: they are the enforcement half of the constraints the row-8 decision names, and E50-T34 (Phase-3 order-path retirement) lists them as precondition (ii). Schedule at the next train planning, ahead of the Phase 2/3 retirement tickets, which are in any case gated on preconditions that cannot be dated yet (five green nightlies, C-04/C-07b, and a two-week canary).

## Context

**R10-13, Low, but it is the one that would bite a supervisor silently.**

`#207` materially improved this — `RunawayChainError.stranded`, `on_invocation_stranded`,
`has_dormant_invocations`, `pending_invocations()` and an ERROR log all verified live on
`Interpreter` (`def` and `async def`) and `SyncInterpreter`, exactly-once with a correct payload.
Two residuals survive:

1. **The trip never reaches the error channel.** `interpreter.error` stays `None` and `status` stays
   `running`; `RunawayChainError` appears only on `last_error` and via
   `on_event_dropped(..., "chain_budget")`.
2. **`last_error` is LANE-ASYMMETRIC** — cleared once settled on the **`async def`** lane, retained
   on the **`def`** lane. A supervisor that samples `last_error` asynchronously rather than per-step
   therefore sees the runaway on `def` services and **misses it on the RECOMMENDED `async def`
   ones**. This is the worst shape a diagnostic can have: it works in the configuration you test
   with and fails in the one you ship.

## Scope

- `CvErrorHooks` implements `on_invocation_stranded(interpreter, state_id, invoke_id, error)`.
- The supervisor samples `on_event_dropped(..., "chain_budget")` as the chain-trip signal and
  **never polls `last_error`**.
- The health sweep asserts `has_dormant_invocations() is False`; `pending_invocations()` is
  captured into the alert payload.
- Lint: no production code reads `interpreter.last_error` as a liveness or error signal.

## Acceptance

- `test_cv_c50_chain_trip_observed_on_both_lanes` — **must pass on both `def` and `async def`**;
  a version that passes only on `def` is the defect this ticket exists to prevent.
- Filed upstream as a comment on #207 (**not posted**):
  `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-19cb1f1/comments/207.md`.

title: CV-C4x: kill/cancel on an ancestor; reenter:true lint on restart self-targets
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: kill-on-ancestor + reenter lints folded into E50-T11 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 10, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog, not undated by oversight.** The R2 train is at capacity, so round-10 tickets are not scheduled into Sprints 10-13 without displacing committed work. They are **not** optional: they are the enforcement half of the constraints the row-8 decision names, and E50-T34 (Phase-3 order-path retirement) lists them as precondition (ii). Schedule at the next train planning, ahead of the Phase 2/3 retirement tickets, which are in any case gated on preconditions that cannot be dated yet (five green nightlies, C-04/C-07b, and a two-week canary).

## Context

Two catalogue lint rules, each the residue of a finding we filed against the library and then
refuted against ourselves. Both are **statically checkable over the catalogue JSON**, which is why
they belong together.

**CV-C4x — kill/cancel must be declared on an ANCESTOR of every invoking state (R10-C4, refuted
High -> Low).** B6/B9 declare the kill event only on *sibling* states, so no handler exists on the
active invoking state or any ancestor and `onUnhandled: "defer"` holds the kill for the full service
duration. Isolated repro, both service styles, polled to convergence:

| declaration site | kill latency |
|---|---|
| sibling only | **1.458 s** |
| parent-level handler | **0.001 s** |
| invoking-state handler | **0.000 s** |

XState v5 / SCXML would **drop** the event outright; `defer` replaying after the next state change
is documented (README:1462) and **loses less**. `priority=True` does not help — it is an **inbox
lane**, not configuration-level selection, and no send is dropped or charged. Nothing about this is
a library defect; it is a modelling error with a one-line fix and a static check.

**Self-transition lint (R10-02, refuted High -> outright).** A transition targeting its own source
state is **INTERNAL by contract** — `base_interpreter.py:3021-3028` routes `source == target &&
!reenter` to `_execute_internal_transition`, XState v5 makes internal the default with
`reenter: true` as the opt-in, and the library documents this three times. So a self-targeting
`onDone` meant to **restart** a state's invoke silently becomes a one-shot: `submits = 1` forever.
With `"reenter": true` every lane re-arms to `maxIterations + 2` and the `#207` stranded hook fires.

The library's validator warns for an `always` self-target that cannot progress
(`validation.py:205`) but has **no equivalent for an `onDone`/`on` self-target restart loop**, so
our lint must cover it. This cost us a round to establish; the lint makes it cost nothing again.

## Scope

- Lint: every kill/cancel event named in the catalogue is declared on an **ancestor** of every
  invoking state in its machine (not only on siblings).
- Lint: any self-targeting `onDone`/`on` transition whose intent is to restart the state's invoke or
  entry actions **must carry `"reenter": true`**; flag any self-target without it for review.
- Fix the B6/B7/B9 declarations found by the first rule.

## Acceptance

- `test_cv_c4x_kill_declared_on_ancestor` and the self-transition lint test, both green over all
  twenty catalogue machines.
- Kill latency on B6/B9 measured at **< 10 ms**, both service spellings.

title: Gate harness round 10: verifyM7, baseline 19cb1f1, stale fixtures, amendments
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: gate-harness round 10 folded into E50-T04 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 10, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog, not undated by oversight.** The R2 train is at capacity, so round-10 tickets are not scheduled into Sprints 10-13 without displacing committed work. They are **not** optional: they are the enforcement half of the constraints the row-8 decision names, and E50-T34 (Phase-3 order-path retirement) lists them as precondition (ii). Schedule at the next train planning, ahead of the Phase 2/3 retirement tickets, which are in any case gated on preconditions that cannot be dated yet (five green nightlies, C-04/C-07b, and a two-week canary).

## Context

`gate/run_gate.py` carried a round-10 gap that the gate itself reported honestly — it flagged
`19cb1f1` as "NOT a recorded baseline" rather than passing it off as green — but it was behind by a
whole verification set.

## Scope

1. **`verifyM7` wired** for `issues/verify-main-19cb1f1/` (the #203-#210 pins). **Recorded baseline:
   8/8 PASS, NO expected failures** — the first clean verification set in the study, so **every FAIL
   here is a regression**. *(Done in the round-10 pass; this ticket carries the rest.)*
   `203_*` and `204_*` are load-bearing: if either flips, **reinstate CV-C45's send-side clause and
   CV-C46 before the order path runs** and re-gate E50-T34.
2. **`BASELINE_COMMIT` moved to `19cb1f1`** and the round-9 special-case tables re-pointed.
3. **Retire stale fixtures** that exit 1 for our own staleness, not library behaviour:
   `201_lap_parity_stated_exactly.py` (asserts the pre-#201/#209 "sync stops early with
   `RuntimeError`" shape; superseded by `209_lap_parity_sweep_1_25.py`, which passes), plus the five
   round-8 fixtures still owed from round 9 (`R8-02`, `R8-03`, `R8-04`, `R8-11` superseded by
   restated contracts; `R8-05`'s `check2` does not catch `UnknownEventError`, **which is the
   protection firing**, so treat that as the success mode).
4. **Convert `CV-F28-01` and `CV-F28-02`** from open findings into **regression pins that FAIL if the
   upstream fix is lost** (both fixed by #204 and #207/#209).
5. **Re-scope `bench_c_timers` to STREAM results** instead of buffering to one JSON dump at the end.
   It has timed out with **zero recoverable output for two consecutive rounds**, which is why
   **BENCH-6 is UNMEASURED** and why row 9 is not claimed. This is the highest-value benchmark action
   available: it is the only threshold whose status is *unknown* rather than *known-missed*.

## Standing amendments added this round (apply to every new gate row)

- **16 — Refute your own Blockers against the trust boundary, not against the repro.** A row
  asserting a security property must state the **minimum capability it presumes** and carry a
  **control** showing what that capability achieves *without* the finding. Round 10 filed three
  Blocker/High candidates and **all three fell to their own controls** (a plain registered action
  writes context arbitrarily; a hand-edited snapshot relocates the machine — both with no forgery at
  all). If the control achieves as much, the finding is hardening, not a vulnerability. Applied in
  the other direction: **before filing an engine defect against a chart, build the corrected chart
  and run it.**
- **17 — A "fixed" claim must be tested on a shape that can fail.** Every regression pin must
  demonstrate its own **discriminating power** — show the metric moving with the parameter it claims
  to bound. `#209`'s paired `nested_invoke` shape never exits its initial state, fires exactly 2
  calls at every limit 1-25, and **agrees across all three lanes because a constant agrees with
  itself**. This is the third distinct way a green suite has certified nothing in this study.

## Acceptance

- `run_gate.py --json` against `19cb1f1` reports `verifyM7` 8/8 with no expected-failure allowance.
- `bench_c_timers` produces partial results on timeout; BENCH-6 has a number.

title: Land C-04: hoist the four revocation events onto the B16 session root
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: C-04 B16 hoist folded into E50-T43 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 11, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog.** The R2 train is at capacity. These are the enforcement half of the constraints the **row-6** decision names (ADR-0016 Amendment 11), and E50-T34 lists them as precondition (ii). Round 11 REGRESSED the gate from row 8 to row 6, so unlike round 10's set these are not purely additive hardening: one of them (E50-T45) contains an OPEN LIBRARY HIGH.

## Context

**Blocker. Ours. Open SIX rounds.** Not a library defect — round 10 proved that by construction: `REVOKE`, which *is* listed in both regions, clears correctly on both engines and both service spellings, so engine dispatch is sound. Our chart is simply missing handlers.

`B16.elevation.elevated` omits `LOGOUT`, `IDLE_DEADLINE` and `ABSOLUTE_DEADLINE`. Re-run fresh at `c78ce99` on both action kinds: all three kill events leave the machine at `["session.auth.revoked", "session.elevation.elevated"]` with `still_elevated: true`.

**A dead session stays elevated, and can be re-elevated.** This is an authorisation hole in a chart that gates privileged actions, and it has survived six consecutive readiness reviews while being fixable in configuration alone.

## Scope

1. Hoist `LOGOUT`, `IDLE_DEADLINE`, `ABSOLUTE_DEADLINE` (and `REVOKE`, for symmetry) onto an **ancestor of every elevating state**, per **CV-C4x** — never on siblings only. Sibling-only declaration also costs latency: measured 1.458 s vs 0.001 s with an ancestor handler.
2. Merges **C-04b** (re-elevation after revocation is unaudited) and **C-04c** (post-revoke `STEP_UP_OK` accepted) — same missing-handler root, fixed by the same hoist.
3. Add the `test_cv_c4x_kill_declared_on_ancestor` static lint over the whole catalogue so this class cannot recur in another chart.

## Acceptance

- All three kill events drive `session.elevation` out of `elevated`, on both engines and both service spellings.
- `still_elevated` is `false` after every revocation path; re-elevation after revoke is refused and audited.
- The ancestor-declaration lint is green across all 20 machines.
- This ticket and E50-T43 are the only two Blockers of any kind left in the study; both gate the two-week canary in E50-T34.

title: Implement CV-C57: recursive state-node config key validator
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: recursive key validator (C57) folded into E50-T01 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 11, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog.** The R2 train is at capacity. These are the enforcement half of the constraints the **row-6** decision names (ADR-0016 Amendment 11), and E50-T34 lists them as precondition (ii). Round 11 REGRESSED the gate from row 8 to row 6, so unlike round 10's set these are not purely additive hardening: one of them (E50-T45) contains an OPEN LIBRARY HIGH.

## Context

**The least-defended item on the round-11 board.** #216 landed a top-level unknown-key check that is *flawless where it looks* — 47/47, 120/120 and 200/200 mutation runs caught, with a correct did-you-mean every time — and we have made `strictConfig: true` mandatory on all 20 machines on the strength of it.

But it checks the **root dict only** (R11-07). `KNOWN_MACHINE_KEYS` is overwhelmingly a list of **state-level** names (`entry`, `exit`, `on`, `after`, `always`, `invoke`, `onDone`, `initial`, `type`, `states`), and those keys do their work inside each state node where nothing checks them. Measured: **0/120 nested mutations caught**, 7/7 and 30/30 silently accepted in two other harnesses, **with no WARNING either** — so the did-you-mean safety net is absent exactly where typos are most likely.

`{"states": {"a": {"entryy": [...], "onn": {...}}}}` builds a **clean machine** with zero entry actions and zero transitions under every strict setting. Verified behaviourally: the entry action runs **0** times and the machine does not move on the event that should move it.

**Our typo surface is ~200 state nodes, not ~10 root keys**, so `strictConfig` closes roughly 5% of our actual exposure. A misspelled `entry` means an action that never runs; a misspelled `on` means a transition that does not exist; a misspelled `after` means a deadline that never fires — and the machine builds, starts and reports healthy in every case.

## Scope

1. Recursive walk over `states`, nested `states` and parallel regions in `cv.statechart.factory`, applying the same key check **and the same did-you-mean hint** to every node.
2. Split the key set explicitly into root-only and state-level rather than reusing one flat list, so the intent is legible and a future library change cannot silently widen what we accept.
3. Filed upstream as R11-07 with a standalone repro; the suggested fix there is the same recursion. **Do not wait for it** — this is cheap and it is our exposure.
4. Note the one honest narrowing: nested *policy* misspellings (`actionErrorPolicyy` under a state) are inert either way, since policies are read from the root only. The **structural** keys are the real exposure.

## Acceptance

- `test_cv_c57_nested_typo_rejected` — each of the 7 structural misspellings raises, naming the key and its state path.
- The check reaches depth > 1 and inside parallel regions.
- All 20 catalogue machines still build clean (no false positives).

title: RETIRE the CV-C47/CV-C61 raise(delay=) lint; keep the _timer_handles gauge as telemetry
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: C47/C61 retired; _timer_handles gauge folded into E50-T60 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 12, 2026-09-23): un-parked.** ADR-0016 **Amendment 12** recovers the gate to **ROW 8**. Round 11 parked this set because one of them (E50-T45) contained an **OPEN LIBRARY HIGH** — **no longer true**: #218 closed R11-04 at the mechanism. This set is **purely additive hardening again**.

> **THIS TICKET INVERTED IN ROUND 12.** It previously contained the round's only open library High. **#218 closed it at the mechanism**, so the work is now to **REMOVE** a lint, not to implement one.

## Context

**CV-C47 and CV-C61 RETIRE** (ADR-0016 Amendment 12; `69-r12-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7). CV-C47 had two grounds and **both are closed**: R10-03 (a `raise(delay=)` heartbeat dies at `maxIterations`) by **#212** in round 11, and R11-04 (unbounded `_timer_handles` retention) by **#218** now. CV-C61 existed only to narrow CV-C47's ban around R11-04 and retires with it.

**The evidence is the kind that permits retirement rather than the kind that merely fails to find the defect:** our round-11 repro **unmodified** now exits 0; a 200-beat heartbeat holds **peak 1 handle** on every engine/kind cell; a 500× arm/cancel storm peaks at **0** with **no double-release**; cancel-after-fire is a clean no-op; `stop()` releases; and a 200-machine soak reads **RSS Δ 0.00 MB over 93,168 beats** at `handles_max_per_machine = 1` — against **+753 MB** on the identical script last round.

**Why retire rather than keep it as a free safety margin?** Because CV-C47 was re-grounded once already and had just proved its worth, which makes keeping it *feel* earned — and that is exactly the trap. **A constraint with no surviving ground is not a margin, it is rot**, and rot in a lint file trains engineers to route around the linter.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The **`raise(delay=)` self-paced-periodic-work lint rule is DELETED** from the catalogue linter, along with CV-C61's allow-list clause. Keep the regression tests, re-pointed at the gauge below.
2. **The handle-count gauge SURVIVES, demoted from mitigation to TELEMETRY** under CV-C28': export `len(i._timer_handles.get(i.id, []))` and alert on sustained growth. It is what let round 12 assert `1.00 per machine` rather than "we saw no growth", and it is **how a recurrence would be detected** — which is what makes the retirement safe to make.
3. **State explicitly in the lint file what does NOT move**, so the retirement cannot be read as a general relaxation:
   - **CV-C12 STANDS UNCHANGED.** `after` and `raise(delay=)` remain **coarse, non-critical timeouts only**. Its ground is **BENCH-6**, unmeasured for five rounds (last read **174.4 ms against a ≤100 ms bar**). #218 fixed a handle-**retention** defect and says nothing about **drift under load**.
   - **All algo timing stays on the external `MonotonicScheduler`** with absolute `*_us` deadlines in context.
   - **CV-C55** (no `delay` below 10 ms, either spelling) and **R11-W-1** (stable `send_id` on every chart deadline) continue to apply.
4. A test asserts the gauge is wired and alerting, so this cannot silently rot the other way.

## Reversal condition

**If `_timer_handles` growth reappears on any shape — the gauge reads above 1 per machine on a steady heartbeat, or a soak shows non-flat RSS — CV-C47 and CV-C61 UN-RETIRE, R11-04 reopens at High, and the gate falls from row 8 back to row 6.** The gauge is retained precisely so this is detectable.

## References

`69-r12-final-readiness-verdict.md` §7; ADR-0016 Amendment 12; `issues/post-de2da4e/comments/218.md`.

title: Implement CV-C51 + CV-C56: ban self-receipt awaits in entry/exit actions; bound every start()
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: C51 lint folded into E50-T11; C56 into E50-T59 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 11, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog.** The R2 train is at capacity. These are the enforcement half of the constraints the **row-6** decision names (ADR-0016 Amendment 11), and E50-T34 lists them as precondition (ii). Round 11 REGRESSED the gate from row 8 to row 6, so unlike round 10's set these are not purely additive hardening: one of them (E50-T45) contains an OPEN LIBRARY HIGH.

## Context

#215 added `await self._descent_done.wait()` at the top of `_run_event_loop`, and `_descent_done` is set only at the **end** of `start()`'s try-body. An `async def` entry action that awaits a receipt on its own interpreter (`await i.send("GO", wait=True)`) therefore creates an unsatisfiable cycle: the receipt resolves only when the run loop processes the event, and the run loop is parked on a gate only that same action can open.

**`start()` never returns, and it is completely silent** — `last_error is None`, status `running`, configuration legal, indistinguishable from a slow entry action. #207's `on_invocation_stranded` does not cover it (no invoke involved). Proven causal against a subclass that pre-opens the gate with **library source untouched**: 3.01 s → 0.00 s.

Awaiting one's own receipt directly is unusual. **Calling a helper that happens to wrap `send(..., wait=True)` is not**, and the caller of that helper has no local signal that it is unsafe in entry position. A supervisor that retries startup on timeout retries forever; one that does not simply never comes up, with nothing in the logs naming the cause.

## Scope

1. **CV-C51** — lint action bodies (and one level of helper call) for `send(..., wait=True)` on the interpreter passed into an entry or exit action.
2. **CV-C56** — every `start()` wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for(start(), CV_START_TIMEOUT)`; **a timeout is a hard startup failure, never a retry.** Supersedes and strengthens CV-C39, which said "bounded" without saying what to do on expiry. **This is our only detector for the hang.**
3. Filed upstream as R11-06 (bound the gate, or set `_descent_done` before entry actions with a re-entrancy flag — which is what #215's own comment describes as the sync engine's approach).
4. Document in our own runbook that `send(..., wait=True)` is not reentrant from entry/exit actions — the library does not state this anywhere and it is not evident from the receipt API.

## Acceptance

- `test_cv_c51_no_self_receipt_in_entry` — lint catches the direct form and the one-level-helper form.
- `test_cv_c56_start_is_bounded` — no bare `await start()` anywhere in the codebase; expiry raises a named startup error.
- The control still holds: an `always` self-cycle in the descent returns from `start()` with `RunawayChainError` (the settle budget does cover the descent; only the receipt cycle hangs).

title: Implement CV-C49' / CV-C58: never re-persist an un-start()ed interpreter; audit the compaction job
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: C49′/C58 folded into E50-T10 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 11, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog.** The R2 train is at capacity. These are the enforcement half of the constraints the **row-6** decision names (ADR-0016 Amendment 11), and E50-T34 lists them as precondition (ii). Round 11 REGRESSED the gate from row 8 to row 6, so unlike round 10's set these are not purely additive hardening: one of them (E50-T45) contains an OPEN LIBRARY HIGH.

## Context

#213's v3 round-trip is **exact** — 600/600 trials carrying the right `remaining_ms` (±0.5 ms) and `send_id`, firing not early, not late, exactly once. This ticket is about the **second hop**.

`from_snapshot` parks restored records in `_restored_self_sends`; only `start()` converts them into live armed sends via `_rearm_restored_self_sends`, which also **consumes** the list. But `get_persisted_snapshot` builds `scheduled_sends` from `_armed_self_sends` only — the **live** dict, empty before `start()`. The parked list is written by neither path:

```
snapshot (1 record) -> from_snapshot -> get_persisted_snapshot -> 0 records
```

Both action lanes. The normal hop (restore → `start()` → re-persist) is sound and is the control.

**Loading a snapshot and writing it back without starting an interpreter is not exotic** — it is exactly what a journal-compaction job does, what a storage-migration job does, and what any offline blob-rewrite utility does. None of them has a reason to `start()` the machine; starting it would arm real timers and run real work. **The result is a maintenance job that silently destroys every deadline it touches** — the precise failure mode #213 was filed to fix.

## Scope

1. **CV-C49′** — CV-C49 is **rewritten, not retired**: its original ground (R10-04, the armed delay silently discharged by a snapshot) is **closed by #213**. The new rule is *never re-persist an interpreter that has not been `start()`ed*. Per standing amendment 20, record the re-grounding explicitly.
2. **CV-C58** — audit every snapshot-rewriting path we own. Each must either `start()` first, or copy `scheduled_sends` through verbatim.
3. Filed upstream as R11-08; suggested fix is to union `_armed_self_sends` with any unconsumed `_restored_self_sends` in `_persist_scheduled_sends`.

## Acceptance

- `test_cv_c58_repersist_preserves_scheduled_sends` on both action kinds.
- A double hop (restore → re-persist → restore → re-persist) preserves the record and does not reset `remaining_ms`.
- Code review confirms no compaction/migration path re-persists without starting.

title: Implement CV-C59 + CV-C60 + CV-C54: latch chain trips; read restore refusals before start(); reconcile record counts
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: C59 folded into E50-T60; C60/C54 into E50-T49 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 11, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog.** The R2 train is at capacity. These are the enforcement half of the constraints the **row-6** decision names (ADR-0016 Amendment 11), and E50-T34 lists them as precondition (ii). Round 11 REGRESSED the gate from row 8 to row 6, so unlike round 10's set these are not purely additive hardening: one of them (E50-T45) contains an OPEN LIBRARY HIGH.

## Context

Three observability rules with one theme: **the library's error surfaces on these paths are rolling reads, not latches, and one of them is structurally unreachable.**

**CV-C59 (R11-09).** A `RunawayChainError` trip reaches exactly one surface — `last_error` — which is recomputed **per processed event** as `None if last_transition_ok else _last_action_error`. **One benign, declared, correctly-handled event erases it.** `interpreter.error` is never set, `status` stays `running`, and no hook carries chain context. On a machine that is **permanently inert** (trips 40/40, polled to convergence over 12 s and re-checked 2 s later), **6/40 (`def`) and 8/40 (`async`)** post-mortems read `status='running'`, `last_transition_ok=True`, `last_error=None`, `pending_events=0`. **Post-#212 the race has a predictable winner:** a legal heartbeat guarantees events keep arriving, so the eraser wins. This observable produced **99 false violations** in our own harness before the read was latched.

**CV-C60 (R11-10).** `on_invalid_event` is **structurally unreachable** on the restore path: `_admit_restored` does call the reporter, but it runs inside `from_snapshot`, which is still *constructing* the interpreter — and `from_snapshot` takes no `plugins=`. No ordering exists in which a plugin observes a restore refusal (empty in all 10 cells tried). `last_error` works, but **only before `start()`**, holds only the **last** refusal, and reverts to `None` after. The library's own pin registers the plugin *after* the restore and asserts only on `last_error`, so its suite does not notice.

**CV-C54 (R11-02).** `scheduled_sends` restores without the *reported* strict refusal #214 promises, so a chart upgrade that undeclares an event yields **silent delivery** instead of `on_invalid_event`/`last_error`.

## Scope

1. **CV-C59** — supervisors never poll `last_error` for chain health. Latch `RunawayChainError` from the log or a latching plugin wrapper, and expose a monotonic counter a health sweep can diff.
2. **CV-C60** — the restore routine reads `last_error` / `last_transition_ok` **immediately after `from_snapshot` and before `start()`**. Do not register `on_invalid_event` expecting restore coverage.
3. **CV-C54** — reconcile persisted (`pending_events` + `scheduled_sends`) against admitted record counts and **fail loudly** on a mismatch. This is the only signal that survives both gaps above.
4. Filed upstream: R11-09 (sticky `chain_trips` counter or `on_chain_budget_exceeded` hook), R11-10 (`plugins=` on `from_snapshot`), R11-02 (route re-arm through `_admit_restored`).

## Acceptance

- `test_cv_c59_chain_trip_latched` — passes on **both** `def` and `async def`, and with a live heartbeat running.
- `test_cv_c60_restore_refusal_read_before_start`.
- `test_cv_c54_restore_count_reconciliation` — a dropped record fails the restore loudly.

title: Retire CV-C48 and CV-C45's stripping clause, and DELETE their workaround tests
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: workaround tests were never written on the adopted path (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 11, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog.** The R2 train is at capacity. These are the enforcement half of the constraints the **row-6** decision names (ADR-0016 Amendment 11), and E50-T34 lists them as precondition (ii). Round 11 REGRESSED the gate from row 8 to row 6, so unlike round 10's set these are not purely additive hardening: one of them (E50-T45) contains an OPEN LIBRARY HIGH.

## Context

Per `20-adoption-gate.md` §6.1 — when a defect closes, **delete the mitigation and its workaround test**. Carrying dead complexity is how a mitigation outlives its defect and becomes folklore. Round 11 closes the ground of two constraints outright.

**CV-C48** (0.8.0-era snapshots migrated before restore; a `pending_events` record with `kind:"after"` and no `engine` flag rejected at the envelope and the deadline re-armed from context) — its **entire** ground was R10-05b: a persisted 0.8.0 `after` record was *refused* rather than demoted, dropping the deadline silently. **#214's v2 upcast closes exactly this.** The migration cliff is gone. The security objection we then raised against that upcast (R11-01, filed Blocker) was **refuted on a control**, so there is no reason to re-erect the fence.

**CV-C45's restore-side stripping clause** (strip every `Done`/`Error`/`After` record from `pending_events` before `from_snapshot`, matching the serialised `kind` as well as the class, and re-arm from context) — stripping was a workaround for records being *refused* silently. With #214 they are admitted correctly and refusals are strict-checked and recorded.

## Scope

1. Remove CV-C48 and its `test_cv_c48_pre_0_8_1_after_record_refused_loudly`, plus the envelope version fence it installed.
2. Remove CV-C45's stripping code and test. **Replace with CV-C45″** — read `last_error`/`last_transition_ok` immediately after `from_snapshot` and before `start()` (implemented under E50-T48 as CV-C60).
3. **Do NOT touch CV-C49** — it is *rewritten*, not retired (E50-T47), and **do NOT touch CV-C47** — its ground changed but the rule is now load-bearing (E50-T45). Three constraints, three different outcomes from one release: this ticket handles only the two that genuinely die.
4. Update `12-challenge-register.md` and `28-statechart-catalogue.md` §1.3b so the retirement is recorded where the constraint is read, not only where it was decided.

## Acceptance

- Both constraints and both tests are gone; a 0.8.0-era snapshot with an `after` record restores and **fires** its deadline via the upcast.
- No remaining code path strips `pending_events` records before restore.
- Standing amendment 20's per-constraint pass is reflected: every surviving CV-C rule states its **current** ground.

title: Round-12 measurement debt: full suite ALONE and FIRST, then BENCH-6 alone, then multi-sample benches
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: measurement debt folded into E50-T06 (BENCH-1) + E50-T04 (BENCH-6) (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 11, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog.** The R2 train is at capacity. These are the enforcement half of the constraints the **row-6** decision names (ADR-0016 Amendment 11), and E50-T34 lists them as precondition (ii). Round 11 REGRESSED the gate from row 8 to row 6, so unlike round 10's set these are not purely additive hardening: one of them (E50-T45) contains an OPEN LIBRARY HIGH.

## Context

**This is now the largest open risk on the board, and it is entirely ours.**

**Decision-table row 2 fires BEFORE any adoption row.** It keys on the library's own suite passing and coverage ≥ 86 %. The full suite has **not completed inside the bound for three consecutive rounds** — round 11 reached only ~4 % of 3535 collected tests (zero failures observed), after round 10's ~25 % and round 9's ~51 %. The standing measurement is round 10's completed run at `19cb1f1`: 3505 passed / 13 skipped / 0 failed / **92.78 %**. **That number is one commit stale, and row 2 is currently resting on inference again** — exactly the position round 9 was in and round 10 discharged.

**BENCH-6 (loaded timer drift) has now gone UNMEASURED FOR FOUR ROUNDS** while **CV-C12 (`after` banned in catalogue machines) stands entirely on it.** A constraint whose ground has not been re-measured cannot be retired; retiring it would be a decision made on absence of evidence. Last actual measurement: 174.4 ms against a ≤100 ms bar.

Round 11's budget went to a hash-seed sweep and three benches that ran to completion, leaving the suite less time to ramp than in either prior round. **Ordering, not effort, is the problem.**

## Scope

1. **Run the full suite ALONE and FIRST**, before any benchmark competes for CPU. Produce a final pass/fail/coverage total at the pinned commit. Nothing else in round 12 matters more.
2. **Then BENCH-6 alone**, per-tier, at the specified 300 s cap. *(Its streaming fix is E50-T41 §5 — if that has not landed, land it here: `bench_c_timers` has timed out with zero recoverable output for three rounds because it buffers to one JSON dump at the end.)*
3. **Multi-sample (n>1) KB/order.** The reading has gone 2.128 → 3.064 → **5.512 KB/order** across rounds 9/10/11 — now *above* round 7's originally-flagged ceiling. Each round is a single-sample RSS delta over ~1.5–2.7 MB of signal, so probably noise, **but the spread is widening rather than narrowing.** Either sample it properly or replace the metric; a fifth unbisected round is not informative.
4. **Repeat `rollback_and_defer`.** It read **0.536×** vs baseline this round against 0.754× (round 10) and a 0.75–0.93× band (round 9) — the one policy-cost number outside its prior band rather than tracking baseline movement. Not bisected. If round 12 reproduces it, file it as a regression in the combined-policy path.

## Acceptance

- A completed suite total and coverage figure at the pinned commit, recorded in `00-README.md`.
- BENCH-6 has a **number** — met or missed, but known. If met, CV-C12 retires (and with E50-T45's upstream fix, the whole timer tension dissolves).
- KB/order and `rollback_and_defer` each carry n>1 samples with a stated verdict.

title: K11: decide whether catalogue deadlines move into the charts — BLOCKED on R11-04 upstream
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: K11 decided by CV-C12′ (coarse deadlines only) (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 11, 2026-09-22): parked in Backlog.** The R2 train is at capacity. These are the enforcement half of the constraints the **row-6** decision names (ADR-0016 Amendment 11), and E50-T34 lists them as precondition (ii). Round 11 REGRESSED the gate from row 8 to row 6, so unlike round 10's set these are not purely additive hardening: one of them (E50-T45) contains an OPEN LIBRARY HIGH.

## Context

**All 20 catalogue machines currently declare ZERO timers** — no `after` transitions, no `raise(delay=)` actions (`after=[] delayed_sends=[]`; every driver snapshot reads `v=3:sched=0`). Every deadline is a host-side timer that an action stamps.

**#213 exists precisely to make deadlines restart-safe**, and its round-trip is exact (600/600). **We cannot use it until the deadlines move into the charts.** That is the obvious next step — and it is currently the wrong one.

**The tension, stated plainly.** R11-04 says *do not use `raise(delay=)` for periodic work* (1.00 leaked timer handle per beat, unbounded, both engines). R11-DC-2 says *`after` deadlines are not persisted* (#128, deliberate). So **the only restart-safe in-chart deadline primitive is the leaking one**, and moving catalogue deadlines into the charts today would adopt a leaking primitive as a production dependency.

**This is also the trigger that would escalate R11-04 for us specifically.** Today the containment (CV-C47/CV-C61) is *free* because no chart uses a timer. The moment B6/B7/B8's algo timing moves in, CV-C61's narrow exception becomes load-bearing and R11-04 goes from High to **Critical for CandleViewer**. See `64-r11-final-readiness-verdict.md` §9 item 5 — **our own roadmap walking into the defect.**

## Scope — DO NOT START UNTIL

1. **R11-04 is fixed upstream** (one line per engine: key the delayed-self-send handle by owning state id, or discard it in `_fire`/`_cancel`). Verify with the R11-04 repro: handles/beat must be ~0.
2. **BENCH-6 is measured** (E50-T51). If it is met, `after` becomes usable for real deadlines and CV-C12 retires, which changes the design entirely — possibly making this ticket unnecessary.

Then, and only then:

3. Decide per machine which deadlines are **restart-critical** (→ `raise(delay=)` with a stable `send_id`, R11-W-1) and which are not (→ `after:`, or stay on the external `MonotonicScheduler`).
4. Re-verify every deadline property against the **REAL clock** — `SimulatedClock` fires neither `after` nor restored `scheduled_sends` on this build (R11-W-3).

## Acceptance

- A written decision per machine, with the two preconditions evidenced as met.
- If the preconditions are not met by the next train, this ticket rolls forward **unstarted** with the reason recorded. Rolling it forward is the correct outcome; starting it early is not.

title: Implement CV-C62 budget sizing and the three R11-W catalogue lints
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: C62 sizing + R11-W lints folded into E50-T11 (29 §4a)**

> **SCHEDULING NOTE (round 12, 2026-09-23): un-parked.** ADR-0016 **Amendment 12** recovers the gate to **ROW 8**. Round 11 parked this set because one of them (E50-T45) contained an **OPEN LIBRARY HIGH** — **no longer true**: #218 closed R11-04 at the mechanism. This set is **purely additive hardening again**.

> **Round 12: this set SHRINKS and becomes purely additive.** Round 11 flagged it as not purely-additive because E50-T45 contained an open library High; #218 closed it. **E50-T45 itself has inverted from 'implement a lint' to 'retire a lint'.**

## Context

Four small, independent hardening items that fell out of round 11. Each is cheap; each closes a failure mode we actually hit or measured.

**CV-C62 — two plateaus, both correct.** A descent-seeded chain gets `maxIterations+3` laps; an externally kicked one gets **exactly `+2`**. Swept over limits {3,5,7,9}, identical cell-for-cell in the `def` lane. The library's CHANGELOG conflates them (#207 says `+2`, #210 says `+3`) and its own pin asserts the external case. **Any runbook asserting `+3` for an externally triggered cycle is reliably wrong by one, and sizing against the external number under-provisions the descent case by ~2.7× — a mistake we made ourselves.**

**R11-W-1 — stable `send_id` on every chart deadline.** #213 keys `scheduled_sends` by it, and `cancel`/`rearm` address it. An auto-generated id leaves a restored deadline **unaddressable**.

**R11-W-2 — never register a user action whose name collides with a built-in** (`raise`, `send`, …). A collision **silently disarms the built-in**: `beats=0`, `last_error=None`, no warning, no error — total and completely silent. Filter registrations through `xstate_statemachine.actions.is_builtin`.

**R11-W-3 — `SimulatedClock` fires neither `after` nor restored `scheduled_sends`** on this build. A 1000 ms `raise(delay=)` persists correctly as `remaining_ms: 1000.0`, but `clock.increment(2.0)` plus a pump leaves the machine parked. **Every deadline property must be verified against the real clock** (the real-clock property verified 300/300).

## Scope

1. `test_cv_c62_both_plateaus_pinned` — pin **both** numbers, with the shape each belongs to named in the test. Per standing amendment 17, each arm must demonstrate its own discriminating power: show the lap count moving with the limit.
2. Catalogue lint: every `raise(delay=)` declares an explicit `send_id`.
3. Catalogue lint: no registered action name collides with a built-in, checked via `is_builtin` rather than a hand-maintained list.
4. Test-harness rule: deadline properties run against the real clock; mark any `SimulatedClock` deadline assertion as invalid on this build.

## Acceptance

- All four checks green across the 20 machines.
- The plateau test fails if either number is changed, and its arms vary with the limit rather than agreeing as constants.

title: Implement CV-C63: carry chain_trips and last_chain_error in the wrapper's snapshot envelope
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: v3 snapshot carries chain_trips natively; read folded into E50-T49/T60 (29 §4a)**

## Context

**#222 gives us the chain-trip API that CV-C59 asked for, and it works** - verified at `de2da4e` on both engines and both action kinds: a trip sets `chain_trips = 1`, `last_chain_error` **latches and survives 5-10 benign handled events** that erase `last_error`, `clear_chain_error()` clears the latch and **keeps the count**, and `on_chain_budget_exceeded` fires **exactly once per trip** including settle-budget trips (`on_event_dropped(reason='chain_budget')` **precedes** it, so either is safe to key on).

**But the latch is PROCESS-LOCAL.** `chain_trips` and `last_chain_error` are **not snapshot fields**: after `from_snapshot`, `restored_chain_trips == 0` and the latch is `null` (`snapshot_has_chain_key == []`). This is **consistent with the documented purpose** - it is the live supervisor's signal, and the v3 layout documents its own fields - so it is **not filed as a library defect** (Low: D12-security-1 / Q-7). It is nevertheless a real operational hole: **a restart from a snapshot erases the only record that the previous process discarded work**, which is precisely the moment an operator most wants it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The snapshot wrapper **reads `chain_trips` and `last_chain_error` BEFORE calling `get_persisted_snapshot()`** and writes both into **our own envelope** (not into the library's v3 payload - we do not fork the layout).
2. On restore, the supervisor is **seeded from the envelope**, not from the freshly restored interpreter, so a restarted machine still reports that its predecessor tripped.
3. `clear_chain_error()` semantics are mirrored in the wrapper: clearing the latch must **keep the monotonic count**.
4. `test_cv_c63_chain_trips_survive_restart` - trip, snapshot, restore, assert the supervisor still sees the trip and the count. **Must pass on BOTH engines and BOTH service spellings.**
5. **CV-C59 is re-grounded in the same pass:** supervisors must key on `chain_trips` / `last_chain_error` / `on_chain_budget_exceeded` and **never poll `last_error`**, which #222 documents as the **per-step** read it always was - one benign event erases it.

## References

`docs/research/xstate/69-r12-final-readiness-verdict.md` S5.1/S7 (CV-C63); `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-de2da4e/comments/222.md`; ADR-0016 Amendment 12.

title: Implement CV-C64: lint every action body for self-receipt sends BEFORE the dependency bump
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: C64′ lint folded into E50-T11 (29 §4a)**

> **THIS MUST RUN BEFORE THE DEPENDENCY BUMP, not after.** #219 is a deliberate **breaking change**, not a bug fix.

## Context

**#219 makes an action that awaits `send(..., wait=True)` on its OWN interpreter raise `ReentrantWaitError` instead of deadlocking** (the sync engine refuses the same shape for parity). This is strictly better than what it replaced - a **silent permanent `start()` deadlock** with `last_error = None`, `status = running` and a legal configuration - but it **breaks working code**.

**Our catalogue needed ZERO changes, and this was verified POSITIVELY rather than assumed:** 0 of 573 corpus scripts and 0 of 20 contract charts contain the shape; our ~30 `wait=True` call sites all await from **outside** an action. **That is CV-C25 (no external `send()` from inside an action - gateway queue only) doing its job since round 5, not luck.** This ticket makes the audit **standing**, so the property is maintained rather than rediscovered.

**And it must be WIDER than #219's own rule, because the documented escape hatch is also unsafe (DE-L1, Medium, filed upstream).** The guard rides an **inheritable `ContextVar`**, so `asyncio.ensure_future` / `create_task` copy `_ACTIVE_ACTION_OWNER` into a spawned task **for its whole life**. The consequence: `asyncio.ensure_future(i.send(..., wait=True))` - the idiom the changelog prescribes - is refused whenever the spawning action yields again, and a background worker born in an action is refused **even 300 ms after the machine goes idle**. The upstream pinned test passes only because its action returns immediately: **the idiom's safety is scheduling luck, not a property of the API.**

## Acceptance criteria

1. A lint over **every registered action body** (extending CV-C51's existing rule) rejects:
   - a direct `await interpreter.send(..., wait=True)` on the action's **own** interpreter;
   - **any helper-spawn site** (`asyncio.ensure_future`, `asyncio.create_task`) inside an action whose spawned callable later sends to the same interpreter.
2. **Both action kinds are covered.** A **`def`** action calling `send(..., wait=True)` receives the `_Awaitable` guard **unawaited** - no exception, no warning, no usable receipt. Nothing hangs (it cannot await), but the call is **silently useless**, so the lint must flag it too.
3. The sanctioned alternatives are documented at the lint site: route through the **gateway queue** (CV-C25), or spawn the helper with a **fresh `contextvars.Context()`** (measured working - the machine advances).
4. `test_cv_c64_no_self_receipt_from_action_or_helper` - **must pass on BOTH kinds**.
5. **Run the lint against the current catalogue and record the result in the ticket.** The expected outcome is **0 findings**; a non-zero result before the bump is a blocker for the bump.

## References

`docs/research/xstate/69-r12-final-readiness-verdict.md` S2(b)/S5.2/S7 (CV-C64); `docs/research/xstate/issues/post-de2da4e/new/DE-L1-ensure-future-escape-hatch-refused.md` (standalone repro); ADR-0016 Amendment 12.

title: Implement CV-C65'/CV-C69: drain-journal shutdown + receipt-drop supervision
body:
> **RETIRED 2026-09-24: C65′ drain journal folded into E50-T10; C69 into E50-T60 (29 §4a)**

## Context

#239 makes `drain_pending()` complete (priority first). Drained `wait=True` receipts resolve with `InterpreterStoppedError` (R14-02). #244 adds `dropped_receipts`/`on_receipt_dropped`, which is called from a finaliser.

2. Waiters check `Receipt.error`.
3. The `on_receipt_dropped` hook is thread-safe and does not touch the loop. The supervisor alerts on `dropped_receipts > 0`.
4. The round-trip test must pass on BOTH kinds.
